children.text: || śrīḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīḥ</s> (Auspiciousness).

children.text:
sāṅkhyakārikā
māṭharavṛttisahitā
children.translated_text:
<s>Sāṅkhyakārikā</s>
with the <s>Māṭharavṛtti</s> (commentary of <s>Māṭhara</s>)

children.text: sarvavidyāvidhātāram ādityasthaṃ sanātanam /
children.translated_text: To the bestower of all knowledge, the eternal one dwelling in the sun,

children.text: nato 'smi parayā bhaktyā kāpilaṃ jyotir īśvaram // 1 //
children.translated_text: I bow with supreme devotion to the light of <s>Kapila</s>, the Lord. (1)

children.text: kapilāya namas tasmai yenāvidyodadhau jagati magne /
children.translated_text: Homage to that <s>Kapila</s>, by whom, for a world drowning in the ocean of ignorance,

children.text: kāruṇyāt sāṅkhyamayī naur iha vihitā prataraṇāya // 2 //
children.translated_text: Out of compassion, the ship consisting of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> was fashioned here for crossing over. (2)

children.text: namaskṛtya tu taṃ tasya vakṣye jñānasya kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Having saluted him, I shall explain the cause of his knowledge,

children.text: hitāya sarvaśiṣyāṇām alpagranthasamuccayam // 3 //
children.translated_text: A brief compilation for the benefit of all disciples. (3)

children.text: duḥkhatrayābhighātāj jijñāsā tadabhighātake hetau /
children.translated_text: From the affliction of the threefold suffering, there arises the desire to know the means for its removal;

children.text: dṛṣṭe sāpārthā cen naikāntātyantato 'bhāvāt // ISk_1 //
children.translated_text: If [one thinks] that [inquiry] is pointless because [remedies] are seen [in ordinary life] — [we reply:] no, because [such remedies] are not absolute and final. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 1)

children.text: asyā āryāyā upodghātaḥ kriyate ---
children.translated_text: Of this <s>āryā</s> verse, the introduction (<s>upodghāta</s>) is made [as follows] —

children.text: sthānaṃ nimittaṃ vaktā ca śrotā śrotṛprayojanam /
children.translated_text: The occasion, the subject matter, the speaker, the listener, the purpose of the listener,

children.text: sambandhādyabhidhānaṃ ca upodghātaḥ sa ucyate //
children.translated_text: And the statement of the connection and so forth — this is called the introduction (<s>upodghāta</s>).

children.text:
iha hi bhagavān maharṣiḥ sāṃsiddhikadharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryasampanno bhagavataḥ purāṇapuruṣasyāvatāro jagadanujighṛkṣayā prajāpateḥ kardamasya putraḥ svāyambhuvasya manor duhitari devahūtyāṃ kapilo nāma babhūva | sa tena guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhirūpeṇa jñānenāpārapāraṃ didarśiṣayā hastāvalambeneva, kālāhidandaśyamānajagataḥ sudhāmaṇineva, duścikitsyasya bhavavyādher apanayanāya samyagauṣadheneva, avidyāndhakārapradhvaṃsanapradīpeneva, muktimārgavirodhimohavṛkṣavivraścanakuṭhāreṇevāmunāvabodhena sampanno 'ndhe tamasi majjaj jagad idam adrākṣīt | tad avalokyāsya kāruṇyam udapādi | aho khalv idaṃ jagad anādikālasambaddhaṃ nisargād eva andhe tamasi vartata iti |
athāsau mahāyogī katham asya varākasya andhe tamasi vartamānasya viśvasyānugrahaḥ kārya iti samutpannakāruṇyo manasi cintām āpede | sa(p.1) evaṃ vicintayan āsurisagotraṃ brāhmaṇaviśeṣaṃ varṣasahasrayājinam adhikāriṇam avagatya brahmopadeśavidyayā atandrito bhūtvā vācam ity uvāca --- "bho bho āsure3 ramase gṛhasthadharmeṇa" iti | sa tam uvāca --- "rame bho" iti | sa evam ukto munir īṣadaniṣpannavivekavairāgyo 'yam iti vyavasya nirgamya bhūyo 'pi dvitīye varṣasahasre pūrṇe pratyāgatya tathaivābhyuvāca --- "bho bho āsure3 ramase gṛhasthadharmeṇa" iti | sa tam uvāca --- "rame bho" iti | athāsau mahāyogīndras tathaiva nirgamya tṛtīye varṣasahasre sampūrṇe abhyetyovāca --- "bho bho āsure3 ramase gṛhasthadharmeṇa" iti | sa tam uvāca --- "na rame bho" iti | atha sa bhagavatā uktaḥ --- katham iti | punar āha āsuriḥ --- "duḥkhatrayābhighātāt" iti | athāha kapilaḥ --- tāta utsahase brahmacaryavāsaṃ vastuṃ yadi tadāmīṣāṃ duḥkhatrayāṇāṃ pratīkāraṃ vayam upadekṣyāmaḥ | so 'bravīt --- "bhagavan bāḍhaṃ śakto 'haṃ bhagavatām ādeśam anugantum" iti | sa evaṃ gṛhasthadharmam apahāya putradārādikaṃ ca, pravrajito bhagavataḥ kila kapilācāryasya yoginaḥ prāṇāḥ(?) śiṣyo babhūva |
tatra yadi kaścid evaṃ brūyāt --- kuto 'sya jijñāsā samutpannā yayāsau gurukulam abhigata iti | tatrāyaṃ prativādaḥ | duḥkhatrayābhighātāj jijñāsā samutpannā | kam iha paraṃ, kiṃ yāthātmyaṃ, kiṃ niḥśreyasaṃ, kiṃ kṛtvā kṛtārthaḥ syām iti matvāsau gurukulam abhigata iti | tathā hi ---
children.translated_text: Here, the blessed great sage, endowed with the perfections of innate <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, and sovereignty, being an incarnation of the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Being), out of compassion for the world, as the son of <s>Prajāpati Kardama</s>, was born with the name <s>Kapila</s> in <s>Devahūti</s>, the daughter of <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>. By him, the insight having the form of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>...

children.text: "tat tapaḥ sa japaḥ sā dhīs taj jñānaṃ sā ca vaiduṣī /
children.translated_text: 'That is austerity, that is recitation, that is wisdom, that is knowledge, and that is learning,

children.text: yato naiva nipātaḥ syād antaḥsaṃsārasāgaram" //
children.translated_text: By which there is no falling into the inner ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>.'

children.text: iti śravaṇāt |
children.translated_text: Thus it is heard [in scripture].

children.text: kiñ ca ---
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: ihopapattir mama kena karmaṇā kva ca prayātavyam ito bhavād iti /
children.translated_text: By what <s>karma</s> is my birth here? And where must I go from this existence?

children.text: vicāraṇā yasya na jāyate kṣitau kathaṃ sa dharmapravaṇo bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: One in whom such inquiry does not arise on earth — how can he become devoted to <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: tasmāt samīcīnam idaṃ yad asyetijijñāsā samudapādi |
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is proper that this desire to know has arisen [in the inquirer].

children.text:
kiṃ punas tad duḥkhatrayaṃ, tad āha --- ādhyātmikam, ādhibhautikam, ādhidaivikam | tatra prathamaṃ dvividhaṃ, śārīraṃ mānasaṃ ca | tatra śārīraṃ vātapittaśleṣmaṇāṃ dehadhātūnāṃ vaiṣamyād yad duḥkham ātmānaṃ deham adhikṛtya jvarātīsārādi pravartate | mānasaṃ priyaviyogād apriyasaṃyogāc ca dvividham | etad ādhyātmikaṃ duḥkham abhihitam | ādhibhautikaṃ tu bhūtāny adhikṛtya yat pravartate mānuṣapaśupakṣisarīsṛpasthāvaranimittam | ādhidaivikaṃ tu divam adhikṛtya yat pravartate śītoṣṇavātavarṣādikam | evam etais tribhir duḥkhair abhihatasyāsurisagotrasya brāhmaṇasya jijñāsā samutpannā | kva viṣaye?(p.2) tadabhighātake hetau | teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ duḥkhānām abhighātako vināśako yo 'sau hetus tatra | tāṃ jijñāsām āha | kim amūni duḥkhāni vapuṣaḥ, āhosvit tadvyatirikto 'sti kaścid anyaḥ puruṣo yasyemāni trīṇi duḥkhāni jāyante, utāmīṣāṃ pratīkāropāyo 'py asti na vā | yady asti tadānīṃ tam evāsthāsyāmaḥ | no cet prathamaprāvṛḍāsāraṃ ṣaṇḍha[?] ivāmūni nimīlitanetrā vayaṃ soḍhāraḥ | vṛścikādidaṣṭa eva viṣapratīkārāya jāṅgulikaṃ gaveṣayati no vā viṣabhavapīḍāsahaḥ | evam asahyaduḥkhābhibhūtasyāsures tadabhighātake hetau jijñāsā samutpannā | sa ca samutpannaduḥkhābhāvaṃ jijñāsus tatpratīkārakuśalaṃ bhagavantaṃ kapilācāryaṃ śaraṇam abhyupagataḥ, ayaṃ madabhilaṣitaduḥkhapratīkāropāyaṃ vakṣyatīti |
nanu duḥkhebhya eva jijñāsā samutpannā kathaṃ teṣām evābhāvāya kāraṇatvam upayāti | na hi janayitrīsakāśād utpannas tanayas tasyā eva vyāpādanaṃ kurute | satyam | iha loke yady asmād utpadyate tat tasyāpi vipattikāraṇaṃ dṛśyate | yathā karkaṭako 'śvataro vā janayitryāḥ samutpannas tām eva vyāpādayati | yad vā yathā kaścid āśīviṣaḥ śuṣkatṛṇabahulapradeśe sthitaḥ pratisarpaṃ dṛṣṭvā kruddhas tasya mukhaniḥśvāsanirgato vahnis tṛṇāni taṃ vāpi sarpaṃ dadāha | amunā nyāyena duḥkhebhya eva jijñāsā niṣpannā duḥkhānām evābhāvaṃ kariṣyatīty arthasaṅgatiḥ |
atrocyate | dṛṣṭe sāpārthā cet | ced ity ayaṃ nipātaḥ śaṅkāyāṃ vartate | iha loke sakalasamutpannaduḥkhānāṃ pratīkāro 'sty eva, kiṃ tadarthaṃ kapilopasarpaṇeneti bhāvaḥ | tam eva hetuṃ dṛṣṭaṃ darśayati | śārīrādhyātmikānāṃ jvarātīsārādisakalavyādhīnāṃ santy evāgadaṅkārā aṣṭāṅgāyurvedavido bhiṣajaḥ kāyaśalyaśalākāviṣonmādaklībajarākumāracikitsānipuṇāḥ | mānasasyādhyātmikatāpasya pratīkāraḥ priyavastusaṃyogād apriyasya dūrataḥ pariharaṇāc ca | ādhibhautikasya tu grāmanagarādikalpanayā prahāṇopapattiḥ | ādhidaivikasyābhivātayātaprāvaraṇāvaraṇādibhiḥ | atas tadabhighātakāraṇāt kiṃ kapilopasarpaṇeneti bhāvaḥ | tathā ca laukikānām ābhāṇakaḥ ---
children.translated_text: What, then, is that threefold suffering? He states: the <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), the <s>ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to beings), and the <s>ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to fate/gods). Of these, the first is twofold: bodily and mental. The bodily [suffering] is that which arises — such as fever, dysentery, and the like — from the imbalance of the bodily constituents of <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), pertaining to the self and the body.

children.text: arke cen madhu vindeta kimarthaṃ parvataṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: If honey can be found in the [nearby] tree, why would one climb the mountain?

children.text: iṣṭasya līlayā siddhau ko vidvān yatnam āśrayet //
children.translated_text: When the desired is easily achieved, what wise person would resort to effort?

children.text: atrocyate --- na | na ity ayaṃ pūrvapakṣavākyaniṣedhe | naivaṃ vācyam ity arthaḥ | ekāntātyantato 'bhāvāt | ekāntato 'vaśyaṃ tvaduktahetubhir na pratīkāraḥ | yataś cikitsakānāṃ suprayuktāgadānāṃ yathāśakti yatatām api kadācij jantur(p.3) vipadyate kadācij jīvati | vaidyagṛhe 'pi vadhūputrakalatrabhrātṛpitṛpabhṛtīnām aparihāryamaraṇadarśanān nāyam aikāntikapratīkāra ādhyātmikasya | aparam, atyantato 'pi nāsau pratīkāraḥ | agadena nīrujīkṛtānām api jvarādīnāṃ punaḥ katipayadivasair utpattidarśanāt | ataḥ sarvathā ātyantiko 'pi na dṛṣṭaḥ pratīkāra ādhyātmikaduḥkhāpanayane samarthaḥ | vasantādīnām apagatānām api punar āgamanavat | bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ ---
children.translated_text: To this it is replied: No. 'No' here negates the opponent's statement. The meaning is: it should not be stated thus. Because [the remedy] is certainly and absolutely non-existent. Certainly — necessarily, by the reasons you have stated, there is no remedy. For even when physicians have applied well-prepared medicines, and exerted themselves to the best of their ability, sometimes the patient dies, sometimes he lives. Since even in the physician's own household, the unavoidable deaths of daughters-in-law, sons, wives, brothers, fathers, and servants are seen — this is not a certain remedy for <s>ādhyātmika</s> (self-caused) suffering. Moreover, it is not even an absolute remedy, since fevers and other ailments, even when cured by medicine, are observed to recur after a few days. Therefore, no remedy that is absolute in every way has been observed capable of removing <s>ādhyātmika</s> (self-caused) suffering — just as the seasons, even after departing, return again. And there are these verses:

children.text: punar dāhaḥ samutpannaḥ punar jātaś ca vepathuḥ /
children.translated_text: Burning has arisen again, trembling has returned once more,

children.text: bādhate ca punar hikkā jvaraś ca punar āgataḥ //
children.translated_text: Hiccough torments again, and fever has come back.

children.text: anyac ca ---
children.translated_text: And another:

children.text: puṣpitākṣaḥ śalākī ca kuṣṭhī kāyacikitsakaḥ /
children.translated_text: One with diseased eyes, one with cataracts, a leper — [all are] practitioners of medicine;

children.text: pṛcchanti bālabhiṣajaṃ kathaṃ te dārakā mṛtāḥ //
children.translated_text: They ask the novice physician: 'How did your children die?'

children.text: kiñ ca nāsti samyagdhātuparijñānanipuṇatayā bhaiṣajyam | tathā hi ---
children.translated_text: Moreover, there is no medicine through precise knowledge of the proper constitution of the humors. Thus indeed:

children.text: yāni kāni ca mūlāni yena kena ca peṣayet /
children.translated_text: Whatever roots [one may use], ground with whatever [instrument],

children.text: yasmai kasmai ca dātavyaṃ yad vā tad vā bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: To be given to whomever — whatever will be, will be.

children.text: anyac ca --- kāryārthijanadravyabhakṣaṇāya, svaśaktikhyāpanāya ca svalpam api rogaṃ purastād vardhayanti bhiṣajaḥ | tataś ca kadācid asau teṣām evāsādhyatām āyāti | tathā ca ---
children.translated_text: And another: For the sake of consuming the goods of those who seek a cure, and for displaying their own skill, physicians first aggravate even a minor illness. As a result, sometimes it becomes incurable even for them. And thus:

children.text: vaidya vaidya namas tubhyaṃ kṣapitāśeṣamānava /
children.translated_text: O physician, physician, homage to you, O destroyer of all mankind!

children.text: tvayi vinyastabhāro 'yaṃ kṛtāntaḥ sukham edhate //
children.translated_text: Upon you is this burden entrusted — the god of death prospers at ease.

children.text: evam asau dṛṣṭenāgadādihetunā, ekātanto 'vaśyam, atyantataḥ sarvathā, śārīrasyādhyātmikaduḥkhasya na pratīkāraḥ | evaṃ mānasasyāpi śabdādipriyasaṃyogād api kadācin na nivṛttiḥ | evam ādhibhautikam apy upāyaiḥ kadācid vyapaiti, kadācic ca neti | evam ādhidaivikam api kadācid vyapaiti kadācic ca na | kiñ ca vyapagatir api duḥkhasya punarutpādād anarthiketi | asya tu śiṣyasyaikāntika ātyantikaś ca duḥkhavyapagame hetur iṣṭaḥ | tasmād yuktaṃ tadarthaṃ gurūpasarpaṇam iti // SkMv_1 //
children.translated_text: Thus, through the observed cause of medicines etc., the remedy for bodily <s>ādhyātmika</s> (self-caused) suffering is neither certain — necessarily — nor absolute in every way. Likewise for mental suffering too: even from the pleasant union with sounds and other [desirable objects], there is sometimes no cessation. Similarly, <s>ādhibhautika</s> (caused by other beings) suffering is sometimes removed by remedies and sometimes not. Likewise, <s>ādhidaivika</s> (caused by divine forces) suffering is sometimes removed and sometimes not. Moreover, even the removal [of suffering] is pointless because of its recurrence. But this disciple desires a cause for the removal of suffering that is both certain and absolute. Therefore, approaching a <s>guru</s> (teacher) for that purpose is appropriate.

children.text: yady evaṃ tadā dṛṣṭavyatirekeṇāpy ānuśravikaḥ śrutipraṇītaḥ svargādisādhanarūpo yajñādir hetur astu | nākapṛṣṭhe 'pi tāpatrayāsambhavāt | tatraikāntikam ātyantikaṃ vānuśrave vede śrūyate | guruṇoktaṃ paścād vedaṃ śṛṇvanti śiṣyā ity anuśravo vedaḥ | tatra bhava ānuśravikaḥ | śrauto yajñādirūpo 'yaṃ duḥkhatrayapratīkārahetur ucito 'sti | evaṃ hy āha --- "tarati mṛtyuṃ, tarati śokaṃ, tarati pāpmānaṃ, tarati brahmahatyāṃ yo 'śvamedhena yajate" [śatapathabrāhmaṇa 13 |3 |1 |1] iti | yac cainaṃ devāḥ punar apy āhuḥ ---(p.4)
children.translated_text: If so, then besides the visible [remedy], let the scriptural remedy (<s>ānuśravika</s>) — prescribed by <s>śruti</s> (revelation), in the form of sacrifices etc. as means to heaven — be a cause. For even on the summit of heaven, the threefold suffering does not occur. Therein, is the certain and absolute [remedy] heard of in the <s>ānuśrava</s> (scriptural tradition), the <s>Veda</s>? The <s>Guru</s> speaks and the disciples afterward hear the <s>Veda</s> — hence the <s>Veda</s> is called '<s>anuśrava</s>' (that which is heard after). That which pertains to it is '<s>ānuśravika</s>' (scriptural). This scriptural [remedy] in the form of sacrifice etc. would be a suitable cause for counteracting the threefold suffering. For thus it says: 'He crosses over death, he crosses over grief, he crosses over sin, he crosses over the sin of killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — he who sacrifices with the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice)' [Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 13.3.1.1]. And what the gods further say to him:

children.text: "apāma somam amṛtā abhūmāganma jyotir avidāma devān /
children.translated_text: "We have drunk the <s>Soma</s>, we have become immortal, we have attained the light, we have found the gods;

children.text: kiṃ nūnam asmān kṛṇavad arātiḥ kim u dhūrtir amṛta martyasya" //
children.translated_text: What now can an enemy do to us? What indeed, O immortal, [can] the malice of a mortal [do]?"

children.text: [ṛgvedasaṃhitā 8 |48 |3] iti |
children.translated_text: [Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 8.48.3]

children.text:
iha --- śrutāv aikāntikam ātyantikaṃ ca phalaṃ śrūyate | atrāsya vyākhyā ---
kadācit kilendro devān upasthitān niśamya ity avocat --- bho bho devatvād anyad api kim apy asti sukham | tatas te devā ūcuḥ --- nāsty anyat sukham | ata evāsmannivāsasya nāka ity abhidhānam | kam iti sukhanāma, tasya niṣedhaḥ akam asukhaṃ tan na iti nākam | kevalaṃ sukham eva | dvau nañau prakṛtam arthaṃ gamayataḥ | tataḥ prāhendraḥ --- katham iti | tatas te ūcuḥ --- anena hetunā apāma pītavantaḥ | somaṃ yajñe somarasaṃ, tena tatpānena amṛtā amarā abhūma sampannāḥ | kiṃ ca aganma prāptavantaḥ jyotiḥ svargam | anyac ca avidāma jānīmo devān | asmin svarge iyanto devā iti vidmaḥ | kim ity ākṣepe | nūnaṃ niścitam | asmān asmākaṃ vibhaktivipariṇāmaḥ | kṛṇavat kartā | arātiḥ śatrur mṛtyuḥ | kiṃ vā dhṛtir jarā asmākaṃ kariṣyati | amṛtamartyasya amṛtapāyināṃ martyānām iti | "bahulaṃ chandasi"[ ] iti vacanavipariṇāmaḥ | evam anyo 'pi yaḥ somaṃ pāsyati tasyaikāntiko 'vaśyam ātyantikaḥ sarvathā duḥkhatrayābhighāto bhaviṣyati | ato brūmaḥ kiṃ pravrajyayā sāṅkhyajñānena vā kāryaṃ vedoktaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ | duḥkhapratīkāraś ca svargo bhāvīti vedavādināṃ vacanam upaśrutya sāṅkhyācāryas tannivāraṇāya svamatapratiṣṭhāyai ca dvitīyām āryām āha ---
children.translated_text: Here — in the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) a certain and absolute result is heard. The explanation of this is as follows: Once <s>Indra</s>, having observed the gods assembled before him, said: 'O sirs, is there any happiness other than divinity?' Then those gods said: 'There is no other happiness. For this very reason our abode is called <s>nāka</s>. <s>Ka</s> is a name for happiness; its negation is <s>aka</s>, unhappiness; that which is not [unhappiness] is <s>nāka</s> — pure happiness alone. The two negatives convey the original meaning.' Then <s>Indra</s> asked: 'How so?' They replied: 'By this cause: <s>apāma</s> — we have drunk; <s>Soma</s>, the <s>Soma</s> juice in the sacrifice; by drinking that, <s>amṛtāḥ</s> — immortal, <s>abhūma</s> — we have become. Moreover, <s>aganma</s> — we have reached the light, heaven. And further, <s>avidāma</s> — we know the gods. In this heaven, we know how many gods there are. <s>Kim</s> is an exclamation. <s>Nūnam</s> means certainly. <s>Asmān</s> — of us (an irregular case change). <s>Kṛṇavat</s> means shall do. <s>Arātiḥ</s> — the enemy, death. Or what shall old age do to us who are immortal mortals, i.e., mortals who have drunk the nectar of immortality?' — this is an irregular expression 'common in the Vedic texts.' Thus any other who shall drink <s>Soma</s> will certainly and absolutely, in every way, overcome the threefold affliction of suffering. Therefore we say: what need is there for renunciation or <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge? We shall do what the <s>Veda</s> prescribes. And heaven will be the remedy for suffering — so hearing the speech of the Vedic advocates, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teacher states the second verse to refute that and to establish his own view:

children.text: dṛṣṭavad ānuśravikaḥ sa hy aviśuddhaḥ kṣayātiśayayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: The scriptural [remedy] is like the visible one, for it too is impure and subject to decay and inequality;

children.text: tadviparītaḥ śreyān vyaktāvyaktajñavijñānāt // ISk_2 //
children.translated_text: Superior to that is [the remedy] from the discriminative knowledge of the manifest, unmanifest, and the knower.

children.text: ya eṣa ānuśravikaḥ śrauto 'gnihotrādikaḥ svargasādhanatayā tāpatrayapratīkārahetur uktaḥ, so 'pi dṛṣṭavad anaikāntikaḥ pratīkāraḥ | tathā hi --- "madhyamapiṇḍaṃ putrakāmā patnī prāśnīyāt "ādhatta pitaro garbham"(vājasaneyisaṃhitā 2 |33) iti mantreṇa"[āpastambaśrautasūtra 2 |7 |14] | tad evaṃ vedavacasā bahūn piṇḍān paraḥśatān aśnāti yāvad eko 'pi putro na jāyate | tathā "paśyema śaradaḥ śataṃ jīvema śaradaḥ śatam"[ṛgvedasaṃhitā 7 |66 |16] iti śrutāv āste | paraṃ garbhastho jātamātro bālo yuvāpi kumāro mriyate | kiṃ cānyat --- sa śrauto hetuḥ aviśuddhaḥ paśuhiṃsātmakatvāt | kṣayayuktaḥ punaḥ pātāt | atiśayayuktaḥ tatrāpi svāmibhṛtyabhāvaśravaṇāt | uktaṃ ca ---(p.5)
children.translated_text: This scriptural (<s>ānuśravika</s>), Vedic [remedy] — beginning with <s>Agnihotra</s> — stated as a cause for counteracting the threefold suffering by serving as a means to heaven — that too, like the visible one, is a non-certain remedy. For indeed: 'The wife desiring a son should eat the middle cake' [with the <s>mantra</s>] 'O fathers, deposit the embryo' [Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā 2.33] [Āpastamba Śrauta Sūtra 2.7.14]. Thus, by the word of the <s>Veda</s>, she eats many cakes, hundreds of them, yet not even one son is born. Likewise, 'May we see a hundred autumns, may we live a hundred autumns' [Ṛgveda 7.66.16] — so it is heard in the <s>śruti</s>. But some die while still in the womb, or just born, or as infants, or as youths or boys. Moreover, that scriptural cause is impure — because it involves violence to animals. It is subject to decay — because of falling [from heaven] again. It is subject to inequality — because even there, the master-servant relationship is heard of. And it is said:

children.text: "ṣaṭśatāni niyujyante paśūnāṃ madhyame 'hani /
children.translated_text: "Six hundred animals are yoked on the middle day

children.text: aśvamedhasya vacanād ūnāni paśubhis tribhiḥ" //
children.translated_text: Of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> sacrifice, as prescribed — fewer by three than [the total of] animals."

children.text:
paśuvadho 'gniṣṭome mānuṣavadhaḥ gosavavyavasthā sautrāmaṇyāṃ surāpānaṃ raṇḍayā saha svecchālāpaś ca ṛtvijām | kalpasūtre 'nyad apy akṛtyaṃ bhūri kartavyatayopadiśyate | "brahmaṇe brāhmaṇam ālabheta kṣatrāya rājanyaṃ marudbhyo vaiśyaṃ tapase taskaraṃ nārakāya vīrahaṇam"[taittirīyabrāhmaṇa 3 |4 |11, āpastambaśrautasūtra 20 |24 |8] ityādiśravaṇāt |
kiñ ca ---
children.translated_text: Animal slaughter in the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; the sanction for human sacrifice in the <s>Gosava</s>; liquor-drinking in the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>; and the licentious talk of the priests with a widow in the ritual. In the <s>Kalpasūtra</s>, many other improper acts are prescribed as duties. Because it is heard: 'To <s>Brahmā</s>, one should sacrifice a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; to <s>Kṣatra</s>, a warrior; to the <s>Maruts</s>, a <s>vaiśya</s>; to <s>Tapas</s>, a thief; to <s>Naraka</s>, a slayer of heroes' [Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 3.4.11] and so forth. Moreover:

children.text: "yathā paṅkena paṅkāmbhaḥ surayā vā surākṛtam /
children.translated_text: "Just as muddy water [cannot be cleaned] by mud, or wine [purified] by that made of wine,

children.text: bhūtahatyāṃ tathaivemāṃ na yajñair mārṣṭum arhati" //
children.translated_text: So too this slaughter of beings cannot be cleansed by sacrifices."

children.text:
[bhāgavatapurāṇa, 1 |8 |52]
"na hi hastāv asṛgdigdhau rudhireṇaiva śuddhyataḥ" /
children.translated_text: [Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.8.52] 'For hands smeared with blood are not purified by blood alone.'

children.text: "tad yathāsmin loke manuṣyāḥ paśūn aśnanti tathābhibhuñjata evam amuṣmin loke paśavo manuṣyān aśnanti" [śāṅkhāyanabrāhmaṇa 11 |2] iti śrutiśravaṇāt | anyac ca ---
children.translated_text: 'Just as in this world humans eat animals, so in the other world animals eat humans' [Śāṅkhāyana Brāhmaṇa 11.2] — so it is heard in the <s>śruti</s>. And another:

children.text: "vṛkṣān chitvā paśūn hatvā kṛtvā rudhirakardamam /
children.translated_text: "Having cut down trees and killed animals, having made a mire of blood,

children.text: yajñaiś ced gamyate svargo narakaḥ kena gamyate" //
children.translated_text: If by sacrifices one goes to heaven, by what does one go to hell?"

children.text: ity aviśuddhiyuktaḥ sarvathā śrauto duḥkhatrayapratīkārahetuḥ | atha "apāma somam amṛtā abhūma" iti prāg uktam | tatredaṃ pratyuttaram | somapāyinām api nṛganahuṣendrayayātīnāṃ bedhabandhaparikleśā bahuvidhāḥ | karmaṇa upabhogād itareṣāṃ patanaṃ ca | ekāhādīnāṃ satrāṇāṃ dinaparimāṇavatāṃ kāraṇānāṃ parimāṇavad eva svargādi kāryaṃ dṛṣṭam | kāraṇānugamatvāt kāryasya | parimāṇavanmṛtpiṇḍāt parimāṇavān eva ghaṭaḥ syāt | evam ānuśravikāṇāṃ phalaparimāṇatvāt punaḥ kṣayaḥ | atiśayayuktaś ca | yathā āḍhyam avalokya daridrasya duḥkhaṃ syāt, surūpaṃ ca vīkṣya kurūpasya, prājñaṃ dṛṣṭvā mūrkhasya, tathā śatāpsarasaṃ svargiṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā pañcāpsarasas taṃ dṛṣṭvaikāpsaraso duḥkham utpadyate | evam ayaṃ dṛṣṭavat | tad evam anyonyātiśayāt svarge 'pi duḥkham avyāvṛttam | tasmāt | tadviparītaḥ śreyān | tābhyāṃ dṛṣṭānuśravikābhyāṃ hetubhyāṃ viparīto visadṛśa aikāntika ātyantiko viśuddho 'kṣayo 'nantaphalaḥ kaivalyān niratiśayo hetuḥ sa śreyān praśasyaḥ | kathaṃ punar asau bhavatīty āha --- vyaktāvyaktajñavijñānāt | vyaktaṃ cāvyaktaṃ ca jñaś ca teṣāṃ(p.6) trayāṇāṃ vijñānād anubhavāt | bhavati hy asau avaśyaṃ phaladānād aikāntikaḥ, prakṛtijñānād ātyantikaḥ, yamaniyamādimattvāc chuddhaḥ, śarīrabhede punar anāveśyatvād akṣayaphalaḥ | kaivalyād anuttaratvāc ca niratiśayaphalam iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | tatra vyaktaṃ buddhyahaṅkārendriyatanmātrabhūtabhedāt trayoviṃśatikam | avyaktaṃ pradhānam | vyaktotpattikāraṇam | na hy akāraṇaṃ kāryam ity asya siddhiḥ | jñaḥ puruṣaḥ | sannidhisattāmātreṇa cumbaka iva lohasya pravṛttikāraṇam | ataḥ pradhānasya jaḍasya pravṛttihetur ayam astīti siddhiḥ | etāni pañcaviṃśatitattvāni vyaktāvyaktajñasaṃjñāni | yadvijñānād avaśyaṃ sarvathā tāpatrayeṇa vimucyate // SkMv_2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, being connected with impurity, the Vedic [remedy] in every way is a cause for counteracting the threefold suffering [but is inadequate]. Now, it was stated earlier: 'We have drunk <s>Soma</s>; we have become immortal.' To that, here is the reply: Even for <s>Soma</s>-drinkers such as <s>Nṛga</s>, <s>Nahuṣa</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Yayāti</s>, there were manifold afflictions of separation, bondage, and torment. And from the consumption of <s>karma</s>, the fall of the others [occurred]. Of sacrificial sessions (<s>satras</s>) such as the one-day rites and so forth, which have a limited measure of days as their causes, the effect — heaven and the like — is seen to be of limited measure as well, because the effect follows the cause. From a lump of clay of limited measure, only a pot of limited measure would be produced. Thus, because the fruits of the Vedic [rituals] are of limited measure, there is again destruction. And it is connected with surpassing [i.e., relative superiority causes suffering]: just as a poor man suffers upon seeing a wealthy one, an ugly person upon seeing a handsome one, and a fool upon seeing a wise one — so upon seeing a heavenly being with a hundred <s>Apsarases</s>, one with five <s>Apsarases</s> suffers; and upon seeing that one, one with a single <s>Apsaras</s> suffers. In this way, it is just as seen [in the world]. Thus, because of mutual surpassing, suffering is not averted even in heaven. Therefore: 'The opposite of those two is better.' The cause that is opposite to — dissimilar from — those two causes, the seen and the scriptural, [namely] that which is definitive, final, pure, imperishable, of infinite fruit, unsurpassed because of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) — that is better, that is praiseworthy. But how does that come about? He says: 'Through the discriminative knowledge of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower.' The manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) and the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) and the knower (<s>jña</s>) — through the discriminative knowledge, the experiential realization, of these three. For that [knowledge] necessarily yields its fruit and is definitive; because of the knowledge of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), it is final; because of possessing restraint, discipline, and the like, it is pure; because there is no re-entering into a body after the dissolution of the body, its fruit is imperishable; and because of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) and unsurpassability, its fruit is unsurpassed — this completes the sentence. Therein, the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>), by the division into <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), the sense faculties (<s>indriyas</s>), the subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>), and the gross elements (<s>bhūtas</s>), is twenty-three-fold. The unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is <s>Pradhāna</s> (the primary [matter]), the cause of the production of the manifest. For since an effect does not arise without a cause, its existence is established. The knower (<s>jña</s>) is <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self), who, merely by the presence of his existence, is the cause of activity, like a magnet for iron. Therefore, the existence of this [<s>Puruṣa</s>] as the cause of the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s>, which is inert, is established. These twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles) bear the designations 'manifest,' 'unmanifest,' and 'knower.' Through the discriminative knowledge of these, one is necessarily and completely freed from the threefold suffering. [SkMv 2]

children.text: nanv amīṣāṃ katidhā pravibhāga ity atrocyate caturdhā | katham iti cet tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Now, in how many ways is the classification of these [principles]? To this it is said: fourfold. How so? That is stated:

children.text: mūlaprakṛtir avikṛtir mahadādyāḥ prakṛtivikṛtayaḥ sapta /
children.translated_text: The root <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) is unmodified; the seven beginning with <s>Mahat</s> (the Great) are both <s>prakṛtis</s> (productive) and <s>vikṛtis</s> (products);

children.text: ṣoḍaśakas tu vikāro na prakṛtir na vikṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ // ISk_3 //
children.translated_text: the group of sixteen is modification (<s>vikāra</s>) alone; <s>Puruṣa</s> is neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor <s>vikṛti</s>. [ISk 3]

children.text: mūlaprakṛtiḥ pradhānaṃ mūlabhūtatvāt | mūlaṃ saptānāṃ prakṛtivikṛtīnām ādir ity arthaḥ | prakaraṇāt prakṛtiḥ | prasavadharmakatvāt sā prakṛtiḥ | na vikṛtir avikṛtir anyasmād anutpatteḥ | kāraṇam eva sā na kāryam ity arthaḥ | anutpannatvād utpādakatvāc ca | mahadādyās tu sapta prakṛtayo vikṛtayaś ca | mahān ahaṅkāraḥ pañcatanmātrāṇi ceti sapta prakṛtayo 'nyeṣāṃ kāraṇatayā, vikṛtayaś ca kāryatayā svayam | tatra vyaktim āha --- pradhānād buddhir iti vikṛtiḥ, sā ca ahaṅkāraṃ janayatīti prakṛtiḥ | ahaṅkāro mahata utpanna iti vikṛtiḥ, tanmātrāṇi janayatīti prakṛtiḥ | tanmātrāṇy ahaṅkārād utpannānīti vikṛtayaḥ pañcāpi, tataḥ pañcamahābhūtāni jāyanta iti prakṛtayaḥ | utpannatvād utpādakatvāc ca saptamāḥ prakṛtayo vikṛtayaś ca | tanmātrāṇi śabdasparśarūparasagandhākhyāni | ṣoḍaśakas tu punar vikāra eva kāryatvāt | na tu tasya prakṛtitvam akāraṇatvāt | tadvyaktim āha --- vaikṛtikād ahaṅkārād utpannāny ekādaśendriyāṇi tanmātrebhyaḥ pañcamahābhūtānīti ṣoḍaśako 'yaṃ gaṇo vikāro 'nyasmād utpanno na hi tato 'nyad utpadyata ity arthaḥ | utpannatvād anutpādakatvāc ca | puruṣas tu punar na prakṛtir anutpādakatvāt na ca vikṛtir anutpannatvāt | naivāsau kāraṇaṃ na ca kāryam ity arthaḥ | evam eṣa prakṛtiḥ, prakṛtivikṛtiḥ, vikṛtiḥ, na prakṛtir na ca vikṛtir itibhedāc caturdhā prakṛtivikṛtivibhāgo 'bhihitaḥ // SkMv_3 //
children.translated_text: The root <s>Prakṛti</s> is <s>Pradhāna</s>, because it is the fundamental root. The meaning is: the root is the origin of the seven <s>prakṛti-vikṛtis</s>. From the context, [it is called] <s>prakṛti</s>; because of having the nature of production, it is <s>prakṛti</s>. It is not a modification (<s>avikṛti</s>), because it is not produced from another. The meaning is: it is only a cause, not an effect — because it is unproduced and because it is productive. But the seven beginning with <s>Mahat</s> are both <s>prakṛtis</s> and <s>vikṛtis</s>. <s>Mahat</s> (the Great), <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) — these seven are <s>prakṛtis</s> by being causes of others, and <s>vikṛtis</s> by being effects themselves. Therein, the specific manifestation is stated: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) arises from <s>Pradhāna</s> — thus it is a <s>vikṛti</s>; and it generates <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> — thus it is a <s>prakṛti</s>. <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> is produced from <s>Mahat</s> — thus it is a <s>vikṛti</s>; it generates the <s>tanmātras</s> — thus it is a <s>prakṛti</s>. The <s>tanmātras</s> are produced from <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> — thus all five are <s>vikṛtis</s>; from them the five great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>) are born — thus they are <s>prakṛtis</s>. Because they are both produced and productive, these seven are both <s>prakṛtis</s> and <s>vikṛtis</s>. The <s>tanmātras</s> are named sound (<s>śabda</s>), touch (<s>sparśa</s>), form (<s>rūpa</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), and smell (<s>gandha</s>). The group of sixteen, however, is modification (<s>vikāra</s>) alone, because of being effects. It does not have the nature of <s>prakṛti</s>, because of not being a cause. The specific manifestation of that is stated: from the <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> of the modification type (<s>vaikṛtika</s>) are produced the eleven sense faculties (<s>indriyas</s>); from the <s>tanmātras</s>, the five great elements — thus this group of sixteen is modification, produced from another; nothing further is produced from it — that is the meaning. Because they are produced and non-productive. <s>Puruṣa</s>, however, is neither a <s>prakṛti</s>, because of being non-productive, nor a <s>vikṛti</s>, because of being unproduced. The meaning is: it is neither a cause nor an effect. Thus this fourfold division of <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>vikṛti</s> has been stated by the distinction of: <s>prakṛti</s>, <s>prakṛti-vikṛti</s>, <s>vikṛti</s>, and neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor <s>vikṛti</s>. [SkMv 3]

children.text: eṣāṃ vyaktāvyaktajñānāṃ prameyāṇāṃ sādhanāya pramāṇāny āha | pramāṇaprameyapramātṛpramitikrameṇa hi sakalasya siddhir dṛṣṭā |
children.translated_text: For the establishment of these objects of valid knowledge — the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower — he states the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇas</s>). For the establishment of everything is seen [to proceed] in the sequence of means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), object of valid knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>), and valid cognition (<s>pramiti</s>).

children.text: dṛṣṭam anumānam āptavacanaṃ ca sarvapramāṇasiddhatvāt /
children.translated_text: Perception (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and reliable testimony (<s>āptavacana</s>) — because all means of valid knowledge are established [within these three],

children.text: trividhaṃ pramāṇam iṣṭaṃ prameyasiddhiḥ pramāṇād dhi // ISk_4 //
children.translated_text: threefold is the accepted means of valid knowledge; for the establishment of the object of valid knowledge is from the means of valid knowledge. [ISk 4]

children.text:
dṛṣṭam iti pratyakṣaparyāyaḥ | akṣam indriyaṃ pratītya yad utpadyate jñānaṃ tat pratyakṣaṃ dṛṣṭam ucyate | yathā śrotrādīnāṃ śabdādayaḥ pañcendriyārthāḥ pañcānāṃ dṛṣṭaṃ pramāṇam | prathamam idaṃ mukhyaṃ sakalapramāṇānām | yo 'rtho 'munā dṛṣṭena sādhayituṃ na pāryate tatrānumānasyāvakāśaḥ | tac ca trisādhanaṃ pañcasādhanaṃ vā | tryavayavaṃ pañcāvayavam ity apare | tac ca trayastriṃśadābhāsarahitaṃ pratyakṣābhāve pratanyate 'numānam | kam api hetum anvīkṣya tasya hetoḥ paścān mīyata ity anumānam | yathā dhūmaṃ hetum anvīkṣya mahānasa iva pūrvaṃ vahnidarśanād agner astitvaṃ sādhyata ity anumānam | pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ yo 'rthaḥ sādhayituṃ na śakyas tatrāptavacanam | yathā svarge 'psarasaḥ santi, nandanaṃ vanaṃ, tatra viśeṣāḥ śabdādayo viṣayāḥ, vimāne 'dhivāsa iti | āptā rāgadveṣādirahitā brahmasanatkumārādayaḥ, śrutir vedaḥ, tābhyāṃ upadiṣṭaṃ tathetiśraddheyam āptavacanam |
nanv arthāpattiḥ sambhavo 'bhāvaḥ pratibhā aitihyam upamānaṃ cetiprabhṛtīni santi bahūni pramāṇāntarāṇi katham atra trividhaṃ pramāṇam iti saṅgatiḥ | atrocyate --- sarvapramāṇasiddhatvāt | sarvāṇi hi pramāṇāni pramāṇatraye 'viruddhāni | tatra pīno devadatto divā na bhuṅkta ity ukte rātrau bhuṅkta ity arthaḥ | sārthāpattir anumānam eva | prastha ity ukte catvāraḥ kuḍavā iti bodhaḥ sambhavaḥ | so 'py anumānam eva | abhāvaś ca prāgitaretarapradhvaṃsātyantābhāvabhedāc caturdhā | yathā vrīhiśoṣaṇadarśanān na vṛṣṭo deva iti vṛṣṭer abhāvaṃ sādhayati | so 'py anumānabhedaḥ | pratibhā yathā ---
children.translated_text: '<s>Dṛṣṭa</s>' (the seen) is a synonym for <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception). That knowledge which arises depending on a sense faculty (<s>akṣa</s> = <s>indriya</s>) is called '<s>pratyakṣa</s>' or '<s>dṛṣṭa</s>.' For example, sounds and the like, being the objects of the five sense faculties such as hearing and the rest, are what is '<s>dṛṣṭa</s>' — the means of valid knowledge for the five [senses]. This is the first and primary among all means of valid knowledge. Where an object cannot be established by this means of direct perception, there is scope for inference. And that [inference] has either three components or five components — three-membered or five-membered, as others [hold]. And that [inference], free from the thirty-three fallacious forms, is employed in the absence of direct perception. Having examined some reason (<s>hetu</s>), that which is subsequently measured through that reason is inference (<s>anumāna</s>). For example, having examined smoke as a reason, from having previously seen fire in a kitchen, the existence of fire is established — this is inference. Where an object cannot be established by either direct perception or inference, there [is scope for] reliable testimony (<s>āptavacana</s>). For example: 'In heaven there are <s>Apsarases</s>; there is the <s>Nandana</s> garden; there are special sense objects such as sound and the like; there is dwelling in celestial mansions.' The reliable persons (<s>āptas</s>) are those free from attachment, aversion, and the like, such as <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, and others; '<s>śruti</s>' is the <s>Veda</s>; what is taught by them is to be believed as true — this is reliable testimony. Now, [the objection arises:] there are many other means of valid knowledge such as presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), inclusion (<s>sambhava</s>), absence (<s>abhāva</s>), intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>), tradition (<s>aitihya</s>), and analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) and so forth — how then is the statement 'threefold is the means of valid knowledge' consistent? To this it is said: 'Because all means of valid knowledge are established [within these three].' For all means of valid knowledge are non-contradictory with the three means. Therein, when it is said 'The stout <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day,' the meaning is 'he eats at night' — this presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) is nothing but inference. When '<s>prastha</s>' [a measure] is mentioned, the understanding that there are four '<s>kuḍavas</s>' is inclusion (<s>sambhava</s>) — that too is nothing but inference. And absence (<s>abhāva</s>) is fourfold, by the distinction of prior absence, mutual absence, annihilative absence, and absolute absence. For example, from seeing the drying up of grain, one establishes the absence of rain, [thinking] 'the god did not rain' — that too is a division of inference. Intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>), for example:

children.text: dakṣiṇena tu vindhyasya sahyasya tu yad uttaram /
children.translated_text: To the south of the <s>Vindhya</s> [mountains] and to the north of the <s>Sahya</s> [mountains],

children.text: pṛthivyām ā samudrāyāṃ sa pradeśo manoramaḥ //
children.translated_text: on the earth extending to the ocean — that region is delightful.

children.text: ity ukte tatra śobhanā guṇāḥ santīti pratibhotpadyate | pratibhā jānatāṃ jñānam | sāpy anumānam eva | aitihyaṃ yathā --- asmin vaṭe yakṣiṇī prativasati iti janā vadanti ity ukte, sā vighnaṃ karoti, dhanādi yacchatīti jñānaṃ, tad apy anumānam eva | upamānam --- yathā gaus tathā gavaya ity(p.8) apy anumānam eva | kiṃ ca tṛṣitasyāñjalinā, kṣudhitasya pañcāṅguliyāgāt, pṛthulākṣiprabhṛtidarśanāt durbalasya, tarjanīpaṅkadarśanāt? jñānam ityādyanumānam eva | tasmāt triṣv evānyad antarbhavatīti yuktam abhihitaṃ trividhaṃ pramāṇam | iṣṭam iti abhipretam ity arthaḥ | tena pramāṇena kiṃ sādhyam ity āha --- prameyasiddhiḥ pramāṇād dhi | yasmāt prameyaṃ sakalaṃ pramāṇena pramīyate yathā tulayā candanādi, karṣādinā ghṛtādi, prasthādinā vā vrīhyādītyādivat | pratyakṣānumānāgamāḥ pramāṇāni | prameyā vyaktāvyaktajñāḥ | pramātā ātmā | tatra trayoviṃśatikaṃ vyaktam | avyaktaṃ pradhānam | jñaḥ kṣetrajñaḥ | tad amīṣāṃ madhye kiñcit pratyakṣeṇānyad anumānenetarad āptānumānābhyāṃ pramīyate | tasmād ācāryeṇa bhagavatā yuktam abhihitam --- "prameyasiddhiḥ pramāṇād dhi" iti // SkMv_4 //
children.translated_text: When it is said that there are good qualities in that [object], <s>pratibhā</s> (intuition) arises. <s>Pratibhā</s> (intuition) is the knowledge of those who know. That too is nothing but <s>anumāna</s> (inference). <s>Aitihya</s> (tradition) is as follows — when it is said "people say that a <s>yakṣiṇī</s> dwells in this banyan tree," the knowledge that "she creates obstacles" or "she bestows wealth and such" — that too is nothing but <s>anumāna</s> (inference). <s>Upamāna</s> (analogy) — "as is a cow, so is a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox)" — this too is nothing but <s>anumāna</s> (inference). Moreover, [what about] the knowledge [derived] from a thirsty person's cupped hands, from the approach of five fingers of a hungry person, from seeing one with broad eyes and such signs of a weak person, or from seeing the mark of a forefinger in mud? Such knowledge and the like is nothing but <s>anumāna</s> (inference). Therefore, since the others are subsumed within these three alone, it is rightly stated that the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is threefold. "Accepted" means "intended" — that is the meaning. What is to be established by that <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)? To this he says — "the establishment of the <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge) is indeed from <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)." Since all that is to be known is ascertained by the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), just as sandalwood and such are [measured] by a balance, ghee and such by a <s>karṣa</s> (unit of weight) and the like, or rice and such by a <s>prastha</s> (unit of volume) and the like. <s>Pratyakṣa</s> (perception), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), and <s>āgama</s> (authoritative testimony) are the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge). The <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge) are <s>vyakta</s> (the manifest), <s>avyakta</s> (the unmanifest), and <s>jña</s> (the knower). The knower is the <s>ātman</s> (self). Therein, the twenty-three [principles] constitute the <s>vyakta</s> (manifest). The <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest) is <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). The <s>jña</s> (knower) is the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower). Among these, some are ascertained by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), others by <s>anumāna</s> (inference), and still others by <s>āptavacana</s> (authoritative testimony) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference). Therefore the venerable teacher has rightly stated — "the establishment of the <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge) is indeed from <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)."

children.text: tatra trividhasya pramāṇasya pṛthak lakṣaṇam upanyasyate |
children.translated_text: Now the separate definition of the threefold <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is presented.

children.text: prativiṣayādhyavasāyo dṛṣṭaṃ trividham anumānam ākhyātam /
children.translated_text: The ascertainment with respect to each sense-object is <s>dṛṣṭa</s> (perception); <s>anumāna</s> (inference) is declared to be threefold;

children.text: tal liṅgaliṅgipūrvakam āptaśrutir āptavacanaṃ tu // ISk_5 //
children.translated_text: that [inference] is preceded by <s>liṅga</s> (sign) and <s>liṅgin</s> (that which bears the sign); <s>āptaśruti</s> (reliable scripture) is <s>āptavacana</s> (authoritative testimony).

children.text: viṣayaṃ viṣayaṃ prati yo 'dhyavasāyo netrādīnām indriyāṇāṃ pañcānāṃ rūpādiṣu pañcasu, tat pratyakṣaṃ pratipattirūpaṃ dṛṣṭākhyam | anumānaṃ trividham | trisādhanaṃ tryavayavaṃ pañcāvayavam ity apare | tad ākhyātaṃ kathitam | pakṣahetudṛṣṭāntā iti tryavayavam | pakṣaḥ pratijñāpadam | yathā --- vahnimān ayaṃ pradeśaḥ | sādhyavastūpanyāsaḥ pakṣaḥ | itare pakṣābhāsāḥ pratyakṣaviruddhādayo nava | trirūpo hetuḥ | trairūpyaṃ punaḥ pakṣadharmatvaṃ sapakṣe sattvaṃ vipakṣe cāsattvam iti | atrodāharaṇaṃ yathā --- dhūmavattvād iti | anye hetvābhāsāḥ caturdaśa | asiddhānaikāntikaviruddhādayaḥ | sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ dvividhaṃ nidarśanam | yathā mahānasam | itare nidarśanābhāsā daśa | evaṃ trayastriṃśadābhāsarahitaṃ tryavayavam anumānam | pañcāvayavam ity apare | tad āha --- avayavāḥ punaḥ pratijñāpadeśanidarśanānusandhānapratyāmnāyāḥ | evaṃ pañcāvayavena vākyena svaniścitārthapratipādanaṃ parārthapratipādanaṃ parārtham anumānam | tac ca trividham | pūrvavaccheṣavat sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ ca | tatra viśiṣṭameghonnatidarśanāt bhavitrīṃ vṛṣṭiṃ sambhāvayati | pūrvam iyaṃ dṛṣṭeti pūrvavat | nadīpūradarśanād upari vṛṣṭo deva iti vā pratītiḥ | śeṣavad yathā --- samudrodakabinduṃ prāśya, śeṣasya lavaṇabhāvo 'numīyate iti śeṣavat |(p.9) sāmānyatodṛṣṭam --- puṣpitāmradarśanāt | anyatra puṣpitā āmrā iti | punar yathā --- bahir udyota iti kenāpy uktaṃ, tatrāpareṇāpy uktam | candra udito bhaviṣyatīty arthasaṅgatiḥ | tal liṅgaliṅgipūrvakam iti | liṅgena tridaṇḍādidarśanenādṛṣṭo 'pi liṅgī sādhyate nūnam asau parivrāḍ asti yasyedaṃ tridaṇḍam iti | āptaśrutir āptavacanaṃ tu | tṛtīyaṃ pramāṇam | āptā brahmādaya ācāryāḥ, śrutir vedas tad etad ubhayam āptavacanam | āptiḥ sākṣādarthaprāptir yathārthopalambhaḥ tayā vartata ity āptaḥ sākṣātkṛtadharmā yathārthāptyā śrutārthagrāhī tad uktam āptavacanam | tatrāpi prasiddhilakṣaṇāguṇayogāt tisraḥ śabdavṛttayaḥ | tatra lakṣaṇātraividhyam | jahallakṣaṇājahallakṣaṇā jahadajahallakṣaṇā cetyādi pramāṇaśāstreṣu bahutaraḥ prapañca āste | tatra prakrāntam eva tāvad abhidhīyate bhagavataḥ kapilasya matam |
children.translated_text: The ascertainment of each of the five sense-organs such as the eyes and others with respect to each of the five [objects] such as form and others — that is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), which has the nature of apprehension, called <s>dṛṣṭa</s> (the seen). <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is threefold. It has three instruments of proof; it has three members, or five members according to others. That is "declared," meaning stated. <s>Pakṣa</s> (thesis), <s>hetu</s> (reason), and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) — these are the three members. <s>Pakṣa</s> (thesis) is the statement of the proposition. For example — "this location possesses fire." The presentation of the thing to be proved is the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis). The other [types] are <s>pakṣābhāsas</s> (semblances of thesis), nine in number, such as those contradicted by perception and others. The <s>hetu</s> (reason) has three characteristics. The three characteristics are: being a property of the <s>pakṣa</s> (subject), presence in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instances), and absence in the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar instances). The example here is: "because of possessing smoke." The other <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (fallacious reasons) are fourteen — <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished), <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive), <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory), and others. <s>Nidarśana</s> (exemplification) is twofold, through similarity and dissimilarity. For example, "like a kitchen." The other <s>nidarśanābhāsas</s> (semblances of examples) are ten. Thus, <s>anumāna</s> (inference) with three members, free from thirty-three semblances [of error]. Five members according to others. To that he says — the members are: <s>pratijñā</s> (proposition), <s>apadeśa</s> (reason), <s>nidarśana</s> (example), <s>anusandhāna</s> (application), and <s>pratyāmnāya</s> (conclusion). Thus, the demonstration of one's own ascertained meaning to another through a five-membered statement is <s>parārthānumāna</s> (inference for the sake of others). And that [inference] is threefold: <s>pūrvavat</s> (based on what precedes), <s>śeṣavat</s> (based on what remains), and <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (based on general observation). In the first case, seeing a particular rising of clouds, one infers the coming rain — "previously this was seen" — thus it is <s>pūrvavat</s> (based on what precedes). Or from seeing the flooding of a river, the understanding that "it rained upstream" — this is <s>śeṣavat</s> (based on what remains). As for example — having tasted a drop of ocean water, the saltiness of the rest is inferred — thus it is <s>śeṣavat</s> (based on what remains). <s>Sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (based on general observation) — from seeing mango trees in bloom, [one infers] "mango trees are blooming elsewhere too." Again, for example — when someone says "there is a glow outside," another says in response "the moon must have risen" — this is <s>arthasaṅgati</s> (coherence of meaning). "That is preceded by <s>liṅga</s> (sign) and <s>liṅgin</s> (that which bears the sign)" — by means of the <s>liṅga</s> (sign), such as seeing a triple staff, the <s>liṅgin</s> (bearer of the sign), even though unseen, is established: "surely that person is a <s>parivrāj</s> (wandering ascetic) to whom this triple staff belongs." "<s>Āptaśruti</s> (reliable scripture) is <s>āptavacana</s> (authoritative testimony)" — this is the third <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge). The <s>āptas</s> (authorities) are the teachers beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>; <s>śruti</s> (scripture) is the <s>Veda</s>; both of these together constitute <s>āptavacana</s> (authoritative testimony). <s>Āpti</s> (attainment) is the direct reaching of the object, the apprehension of things as they are; one who operates by that is an <s>āpta</s> (authority) — one who has directly realized <s>dharma</s>, who grasps the meaning of what is heard through true attainment — what is spoken by such a one is called <s>āptavacana</s> (authoritative testimony). In that [testimony] also, due to the connection of fame, secondary meaning, and qualities, there are three functions of words. Among these, secondary meaning is of three kinds: <s>jahallakṣaṇā</s> (exclusive secondary meaning), <s>ajahallakṣaṇā</s> (inclusive secondary meaning), and <s>jahadajahallakṣaṇā</s> (partially exclusive secondary meaning) — and so forth; extensive elaboration exists in the treatises on <s>pramāṇa</s> (epistemology). Here, only what is relevant is stated — the doctrine of the venerable <s>Kapila</s>.

children.text: āgamo hy āptavacanam āptaṃ doṣakṣayād viduḥ /
children.translated_text: For <s>āgama</s> (scripture) is <s>āptavacana</s> (the word of the authoritative); they know the <s>āpta</s> (authority) through the destruction of faults.

children.text: kṣīṇadoṣo 'nṛtaṃ vākyaṃ na brūyād dhetvasambhavāt //
children.translated_text: One whose faults are destroyed would not speak an untrue statement, due to the impossibility of a reason [to do so].

children.text: svakarmaṇy abhiyukto yo rāgadveṣavivarjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is devoted to his own duty, free from <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion),

children.text: pūjitas tadvidhair nityam āpto jñeyaḥ sa tādṛśaḥ //
children.translated_text: always honored by those of similar [character] — such a one should be known as an <s>āpta</s> (authority).

children.text: tad evam etat trividhaṃ pramāṇam // SkMv_5 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in this way, the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is threefold.

children.text: tad evaṃ vyaktāvyaktajñākhyasya pratyakṣāditrividhapramāṇeṣu kena kasya siddhiḥ syāt iti | atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Now then, among the threefold <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) — <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and the rest — which one establishes what, with respect to the [objects] called <s>vyakta</s> (manifest), <s>avyakta</s> (unmanifest), and <s>jña</s> (knower)? To this it is said —

children.text: sāmānyatas tu dṛṣṭād atīndriyāṇāṃ pratītir anumānāt /
children.translated_text: Through <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (inference based on general observation), the apprehension of things beyond the senses is from <s>anumāna</s> (inference);

children.text: tasmād api cāsiddhaṃ parokṣam āptāgamāt sādhyam // ISk_6 //
children.translated_text: and that which is not established even by that, being beyond [direct] experience, is to be proved from <s>āptāgama</s> (authoritative scripture).

children.text: atra pradhānapuruṣāv atīndriyau tayoḥ sāmānyatodṛṣṭād anumānāt siddhiḥ | yasmān mahadādi liṅgaṃ triguṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāryaṃ tatkāraṇam adṛṣṭam apy asti triguṇaṃ ceti sādhyate pradhānam | na hy asataḥ sadutpattiḥ syād iti | na ca kāraṇāsadṛśaṃ kāryaṃ syād iti | vyaktaṃ tu pratyakṣeṇaiva sādhitam iti tadarthe na prayatnaḥ | yasmāj jaḍam api pradhānaṃ prasūtikriyāyāṃ pravartate tasmād asti lohasya calanakriyāśaktihetucumbakavad avaśyaṃ puruṣa iti jñasiddhiḥ // SkMv_6 //
children.translated_text: Here, <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit) are beyond the senses; their establishment is through <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (inference based on general observation). Since, having observed that <s>mahat</s> (the great one) and the other [evolutes] — which are the <s>liṅga</s> (signs) — possess the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and are effects, their cause, though unseen, also exists and possesses the three <s>guṇas</s> — thus <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) is established. For there can be no origination of an existent thing from a non-existent [cause]. Nor can an effect be dissimilar to its cause. The <s>vyakta</s> (manifest), however, is established by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) itself, so no effort is needed for that purpose. Since even the insentient <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) engages in the activity of creation, therefore, just as a magnet is the cause of the power of movement in iron, there must necessarily be a <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit) — thus the <s>jña</s> (knower) is established.

children.text: nanu pratyakṣeṇa yo 'rtho nopalabhyate sa sarvathā nāstīti mataṃ saṅgacchate | yathā dvitīyam anīśvaraśiraḥ, tṛtīyo bāhuḥ, śaśaviṣāṇādayo(p.10) vā | evaṃ pradhānapuruṣau nopalabhyete tasmāt tāv api na sta ity āśaṅkānirāsāyāha ---
children.translated_text: But [an objection is raised]: that which is not apprehended by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) does not exist at all — such a view might hold. Just as a second head of <s>Anīśvara</s>, a third arm, a hare's horn, and the like [do not exist]. In the same way, <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit) are not apprehended; therefore they too do not exist — to dispel this objection, he says —

children.text: atidūrāt sāmīpyād indriyaghātān mano'navasthānāt /
children.translated_text: Due to excessive distance, due to extreme proximity, due to impairment of the sense-organs, due to instability of the mind,

children.text: saukṣmyād vyavadhānād abhibhavāt samānābhihārāc ca // ISk_7 //
children.translated_text: due to subtlety, due to obstruction, due to suppression, and due to intermixture with what is similar.

children.text: iha loke satām apy arthānām aṣṭadhā nopalabdhiḥ | tathā hi darśayati --- yathā satām api devadattaviṣṇumitrayajñadattānāṃ deśāntaragatānām atidūrān nopalabdhiḥ | tat kiṃ te na santi | yathā vā cakṣur atisāmīpyāt kajjalaṃ nopalabhate | tat kim idaṃ nāsti | yathā badhirāndhau śabdarūpe nopalabhete | tat kiṃ te na staḥ | anavasthitacittau rājānam api yāntaṃ na paśyati | tat kim asau na gataḥ | dhūmoṣmatruṭinīhāraparamāṇavo nopalabhyante | tat kim amīṣām abhāvaḥ | kuḍyena vyavahitaṃ nopalabhyate | tat kiṃ nāsti | sūryāditejasābhibhūtānāṃ grahanakṣatratārakādīnām anupalambhāt teṣāṃ kim abhāvaḥ śakyate parikalpayitum | mudgarāśikuvalayāmalakamauktikakapotādinikurambe kṣiptaṃ samānaṃ yadi nopalabhyate tad avedam iti | tat kiṃ nāsti | evam aṣṭadhā satām apy anupalambho 'bhihitaḥ | idānīm asatāṃ caturdhā bhavati | tatrocyate --- prākpradhvaṃsetaretarātyantābhāvabhedāt | tatra mṛtpiṇḍe ghaṭaḥ prāg utpatter nopalabhyata iti prāgabhāvaḥ | pradhvaṃsābhāvo yathā mudgarābhighātāt pradhvasto ghaṭo nopalabhyate | itaretarābhāvo yathā aśve gotvam, gavi aśvatvam | atyantābhāvo yathā dvitīyam anīśvaraśiraḥ, tṛtīyo bāhuḥ, śaśaviṣāṇādayo vā | evam iyaṃ dvādaśadhā anupalabdhiḥ | satām aṣṭadhā hy asatāṃ caturdhā | evaṃ pradhānapuruṣāv api santau nopalabhyete // SkMv_7 //
children.translated_text: In this world, even of things that exist, there is non-apprehension in eight ways. He demonstrates this as follows — just as <s>Devadatta</s>, <s>Viṣṇumitra</s>, and <s>Yajñadatta</s>, though they exist, are not apprehended when they have gone to another region, due to excessive distance. Does that mean they do not exist? Just as the eye does not apprehend the collyrium [applied to it] due to extreme proximity. Does that mean it does not exist? Just as a deaf person and a blind person do not apprehend sound and form [respectively]. Does that mean those do not exist? One whose mind is unsettled does not see even a king passing by. Does that mean he did not go? Smoke, heat, atoms, and fog-particles are not apprehended. Does that mean they have no existence? What is concealed by a wall is not apprehended. Does that mean it does not exist? Because of the non-apprehension of planets, constellations, and stars when overpowered by the brilliance of the sun and such, can their non-existence be supposed? If something similar thrown into a heap of <s>mudgara</s> (hammers), <s>āśi</s> (swords), lotuses, <s>āmalaka</s> (myrobalan fruits), pearls, and pigeons is not apprehended, [one might say] "it is not there." Does that mean it does not exist? Thus, the non-apprehension of things that exist has been stated in eight ways. Now, [non-apprehension] of things that do not exist is fourfold. Regarding that, it is said — [it is] due to the distinction of prior non-existence, posterior non-existence, mutual non-existence, and absolute non-existence. Among these, a pot in a lump of clay is not apprehended prior to its production — this is <s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior non-existence). <s>Pradhvaṃsābhāva</s> (posterior non-existence) is as when a pot destroyed by a hammer blow is not apprehended. <s>Itaretarābhāva</s> (mutual non-existence) is as cow-ness in a horse, or horse-ness in a cow. <s>Atyantābhāva</s> (absolute non-existence) is as a second head of <s>Anīśvara</s>, a third arm, a hare's horn, and the like. Thus this non-apprehension is twelvefold: eightfold for things that exist and fourfold for things that do not exist. In the same way, <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit), even though they exist, are not apprehended.

children.text: tad amīṣāṃ madhye kena hetunemau nopalabhyete | tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Among these [reasons], due to which cause are these two not apprehended? To that it is said —

children.text: saukṣmyāt tadanupalabdhir nābhāvāt kāryatas tadupalabdhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Due to subtlety, the non-apprehension of that [<s>pradhāna</s>] is not due to non-existence; its apprehension is through its effects.

children.text: mahadādi tac ca kāryaṃ prakṛtivirūpaṃ sarūpaṃ ca // ISk_8 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Mahat</s> (Great One) and so forth — that is the effect; it is dissimilar to and similar to <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). // <s>ISk</s> 8 //

children.text: tasya pradhānasyānupalabdhir anavagamaḥ saukṣmyāt hetor nābhāvāt | sūkṣmaṃ pradhānaṃ śabdādyalakṣaṇatvāt paramāṇvādivat | na punar evaṃ, yan nāsti pradhānam ato nopalabhyate | kiṃ tu asti pradhānaṃ nopalabhyate saukṣmyāt paramāṇvādivat | tarhi katham upalabhyata iti | atrāha --- kāryatas tadupalabdhiḥ |(p.11) kāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāraṇam anumeyaṃ vaṭadhānyavat | yathā vaṭadhānyaṃ kāraṇaṃ vaṭaṃ kāryam ālokyānumīyate | evaṃ sad eva pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ mahadādeḥ sataḥ kāryād anumīyate | na hy asataḥ sadutpattir bhavatīti | mahadādi mahāna haṅkāraḥ pañcatanmātrāṇi ekādaśendriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtāni ceti trayoviṃśatikam | etan mahadādi kāryaṃ triguṇaṃ dṛṣṭvānumīyate --- asti pradhānam api triguṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ yasyedaṃ triguṇaṃ kāryam iti | kiṃ cānyat | tac ca kāryaṃ prakṛtivirūpaṃ sarūpaṃ ca | pradhānād visadṛśaṃ sadṛśaṃ cety arthaḥ | santi te hetavo yair etat pradhānaṃ visadṛśaṃ sadṛśaṃ ca | yathā loke putraḥ pituḥ sadṛśo visadṛśaḥ syāt yadi rūpeṇa tadā na guṇaiḥ, yadā guṇais tadā na rūpeṇeti yāvat | tāṃś ca hetūn upariṣṭād vakṣyāmaḥ // SkMv_8 //
children.translated_text: The non-perception of that <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) — its non-apprehension — is due to its subtlety, not due to its non-existence. <s>Pradhāna</s> is subtle because it is not characterized by sound and other [sense-objects], like atoms and the like. But it is not the case that <s>Pradhāna</s> does not exist and therefore is not perceived. Rather, <s>Pradhāna</s> exists but is not perceived due to its subtlety, like atoms and the like. Then how is it perceived? To this he says: its perception is through its effects. Having seen the effect, the cause is to be inferred, like the banyan seed. Just as the banyan tree, the effect, is observed and the banyan seed, the cause, is inferred — so too <s>Pradhāna</s>, which indeed exists as the cause of the existent effect beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, is inferred. For from the non-existent, the existent cannot arise. The <s>Mahat</s> and so forth means: <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One), <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), the five <s>Tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), the eleven <s>Indriyas</s> (sense-organs and action-organs), and the five <s>Mahābhūtas</s> (gross elements) — [totaling] twenty-three. Seeing this effect beginning with <s>Mahat</s> as possessing the three <s>guṇas</s>, one infers: '<s>Pradhāna</s> too, the cause of which this is the three-<s>guṇa</s> effect, must also possess the three <s>guṇas</s>.' And what else? That effect is dissimilar to and similar to <s>Prakṛti</s>. The meaning is: dissimilar to and similar to <s>Pradhāna</s>. There are reasons by which this [effect] is dissimilar to and similar to <s>Pradhāna</s>. Just as in the world a son may be similar to or dissimilar from his father — if in form, then not in qualities; if in qualities, then not in form, and so on. And those reasons we shall state below. // <s>SkMv</s> 8 //

children.text: tiṣṭhatu tāvad etat | anyat pṛcchāmaḥ --- kim etan mahadādi prāg utpatteḥ pradhāne sat jāyate, utāsat sambhavati | atrācāryāṇāṃ vipratipattir ataḥ saṃśayaḥ | atra vaiśeṣikā vipratipannā asataḥ sad bhavatīti manyante | mṛtpiṇḍe hi prāg utpatter ghaṭo nāstīti vyavasitāste | asti nāstīti varākā jīvakāḥ | naivāsti na ca nāsti | eṣa bauddhānāṃ pakṣaḥ | evam anyonyavirodhavādiṣu darśiṣu ko nāma niścayaḥ | tad ucyate | tatra tāvat sadasadvādino jīvakāḥ svavacanavirodhenaiva nirastāḥ | yadi sat tadāsan na bhavati | utāsat tadā sadbhāvo na | yataḥ sadasator ekatra virodhāt | atra dṛṣṭānto yathā devadatto mṛto jīvati cetivat | bauddhānāṃ tu nāsti na ca nāstīti pakṣaparigrahābhāvāt taiḥ saha sañjalpa eva na yujyate | vaiśeṣikāṇāṃ tu asataḥ sad bhavatīti matapratiṣedhāya ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Let that be set aside for now. We ask another question: Does this [effect] beginning with <s>Mahat</s> exist in <s>Pradhāna</s> prior to its production and [then] arise, or does it come into being from non-existence? On this matter, there is disagreement among the teachers, hence the doubt. Here, the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, being in disagreement, hold that the existent arises from the non-existent. For they maintain that the pot does not exist in the clay-lump prior to its production. The <s>Jīvakas</s> (Jainas) [hold that] 'it exists and does not exist' — pitiable ones! The <s>Bauddhas</s> (Buddhists) [say]: 'It neither exists nor does not exist' — this is their position. Thus, with these schools contradicting one another, what certainty can there be? The answer is given: First, the <s>Jīvakas</s>, who advocate the doctrine that [the effect] both exists and does not exist, are refuted by the very contradiction of their own statement. If it exists, then it cannot not-exist; or if it does not exist, then it cannot exist — because existence and non-existence are contradictory in a single [locus]. The illustration here is like [saying] '<s>Devadatta</s> is dead and alive.' As for the <s>Bauddhas</s>, since they hold that 'it neither exists nor does it not exist,' there is an absence of any thesis, and therefore discourse with them is simply inappropriate. To refute the view of the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> that the existent arises from the non-existent, it is said —

children.text: asadakaraṇād upādānagrahaṇāt sarvasambhavābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Because there is no production of the non-existent, because of the grasping of a material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), because of the impossibility of everything [arising] from everything,

children.text: śaktasya śakyakaraṇāt kāraṇabhāvāc ca sat kāryam // ISk_9 //
children.translated_text: Because what is capable produces only what it is capable of, and because of the nature of the cause — the effect pre-exists (<s>sat kāryam</s>). // <s>ISk</s> 9 //

children.text: iha loke sad eva sad bhavati | asataḥ karaṇaṃ nāsti | yadi syāt tadā sikatābhyas tailaṃ, kūrmaromabhyaḥ paṭaprāvaraṇam, vandhyāduhitṛbhrūvilāsaḥ, śaśaviṣāṇaṃ, khapuṣpaṃ ca syāt | na cāsti tasmād anumīyate pradhāne prāg utpatter mahadādikam asty eva | upādānagrahaṇāt | iha loke yo yenārthī sa tadupādānagrahaṇaṃ karoti | tannimittam upādatte | tad yathā dadhyarthī kṣīrasyopādānaṃ kurute | yadi cāsatkāryaṃ syāt tadā dadhyarthī udakasyāpy upādānaṃ kuryāt, na ca kurute, tasmāt pradhāne mahadādi kāryam astīti | kiṃ ca sarvasambhavābhāvāt | iha loke yad yasmin vidyate tasmād eva tad utpadyate | yathā tilebhyas tailaṃ, dadhno ghṛtam | yadi sāsatkāryaṃ syāt tadā sarvaṃ(p.12) sarvataḥ sambhavet tataś ca tṛṇapāṃsuvālukādibhyo rajatasuvarṇamaṇimuktāpravālādayo jāyeran | na ca jāyante | tasmāt paśyāmaḥ sarvasambhavābhāvād api mahadādi kāryaṃ pradhāne sad eva sad bhavatīti | ataś cāsti --- śaktasya śakyakaraṇāt | iha loke śaktaḥ śilpī karaṇādikāraṇopādānakālopāyasampannaḥ śakyād eva śakyaṃ karma ārabhate nāśakyam aśakyāt | tad yathā --- śaktaḥ kumbhakāraḥ śakyād eva mṛtpiṇḍāt śakyadaṇḍacakrasūtrodakavidalatalādibhiḥ sampanno ghaṭaśarāvodañcanādīny ārabhamāṇo dṛṣṭaḥ | na ca maṇikādi, aśakyatvāt tāvatā piṇḍena tasya | yadi punaḥ karaṇaniyamo na syād aśakyād apy aśakyam ārabhyeta | tasmāt sat kāryaṃ syān nāsat | kiṃ ca --- kāraṇabhāvāc ca | kāryaṃ sad eva syāt | iha loke yallakṣaṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ tallakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ syāt | yathā kodravebhyaḥ kodravāḥ, vrīhibhyo vrīhayaḥ syuḥ | yadi cāsatkāryaṃ syāt tadā kodravebhyaḥ śālīnām api niṣpattiḥ syāt | na ca bhavati | tasmāt kāraṇabhāvād api paśyāmaḥ pradhāne mahadādi kāryam astīti | sādhitam evam etaiḥ pañcabhir hetubhiḥ sat kāryam | "sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyaṃ taddhaika āhur asad evedam agra āsīt" ity ārabhya "sattveva somyedam agra āsīt" [chāndogyopaniṣad 6 |2 |1-2] iti śruteḥ // SkMv_9 //
children.translated_text: In this world, only the existent becomes existent. There is no production of the non-existent. If there were, then oil would come from sand, cloth and garments from tortoise-hair, the graceful eyebrow-play of a barren woman's daughter, a hare's horn, and a sky-flower would [all] exist — but they do not. Therefore, it is inferred that <s>Mahat</s> and the rest already exist in <s>Pradhāna</s> prior to their production. Because of the grasping of a material cause (<s>upādāna</s>): In this world, whoever desires something procures its material cause — takes it up for that purpose. For example, one who desires curds procures milk as the material. If the effect were non-existent [in the cause], then one desiring curds would procure even water — but one does not. Therefore, the effect beginning with <s>Mahat</s> exists in <s>Pradhāna</s>. Furthermore, because of the impossibility of everything [arising] from everything: In this world, that which exists in something arises only from that. Just as oil [comes] from sesame seeds, clarified butter from curds. If the effect were non-existent [in the cause], then everything would arise from everything, and consequently silver, gold, gems, pearls, coral, and the like would arise from grass, dust, sand, and the like — but they do not. Therefore, we see from the impossibility of everything [arising] from everything too that the effect beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, existing in <s>Pradhāna</s>, comes into being as existent from the existent. And there is this: because what is capable produces only what it is capable of. In this world, a capable artisan, endowed with instruments, material cause, time, and method, undertakes only the work that is possible from what is possible, not the impossible from the impossible. For example, a capable potter is seen undertaking [the making of] pots, saucers, water-vessels, and the like only from a suitable clay-lump, equipped with the suitable rod, wheel, thread, water, and split-bamboo tools — but not gems and the like, because those are impossible from that amount of clay. But if there were no restriction on what can be produced, then even the impossible would be undertaken from the impossible. Therefore, the effect must be existent, not non-existent. Furthermore, because of the nature of the cause: the effect must indeed be existent. In this world, whatever is the nature of the cause, such is the nature of the effect. Just as from <s>kodrava</s> (millet) [comes] <s>kodrava</s>, from <s>vrīhi</s> (rice) [comes] rice. And if the effect were non-existent [in the cause], then <s>śāli</s> rice would also be produced from <s>kodrava</s> — but it does not happen. Therefore, from the nature of the cause too, we see that the effect beginning with <s>Mahat</s> exists in <s>Pradhāna</s>. Thus, by these five arguments, the pre-existence of the effect (<s>satkāryavāda</s>) is established. [As the <s>Śruti</s> says:] 'In the beginning, O gentle one, this [universe] was Being alone, one only, without a second. Some say: "In the beginning, this was non-being alone"' — beginning thus, [and concluding:] 'Being alone, O gentle one, was this in the beginning' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 6.2.1-2] — so says the scripture. // <s>SkMv</s> 9 //

children.text: tatra yad uktaṃ pūrvasyām āryāyāṃ "prakṛtivirūpaṃ sarūpaṃ ca" iti | tatsādharmyavaidharmyapratipādanāya idam ārabhyate ---
children.translated_text: Now, regarding what was stated in the previous verse — 'dissimilar to and similar to <s>Prakṛti</s>' — in order to establish the similarities and dissimilarities, this [next verse] is commenced:

children.text: hetumad anityam avyāpi sakriyam anekam āśritaṃ liṅgam /
children.translated_text: Caused, non-eternal, non-pervasive, active, manifold, dependent, a mark (<s>liṅga</s>),

children.text: sāvayavaṃ paratantraṃ vyaktaṃ viparītam avyaktam // ISk_10 //
children.translated_text: Composite, dependent on another — [such is] the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>); the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is the opposite. // <s>ISk</s> 10 //

children.text: hetumad iti | yasyotpattikāraṇam asti tad dhetumat | hetur apadeśo nimittaṃ prakṛtiḥ kāraṇam ity anarthāntaram | pradhānasyaite paryāyaśabdāḥ | tasmāt pradhānena hetunā sakāraṇam idaṃ mahadādibhūtaparyantaṃ trayoviṃśatikaṃ liṅgam | tathā hi --- mahad buddhitattvaṃ tatpradhānena hetumat | tenāhaṅkāro 'munaikādaśendriyāṇi tanmātrāṇi ca | taiś ca bhūtānīti sarvam evedaṃ parasparahetumat | atha ca dvividho hetuḥ kārako jñāpakaś ca | tatra pradhānabuddhyahaṅkāratanmātralakṣaṇaś caturvidhaḥ kārakaḥ | viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhyanugrahabhedāt pañcadhā jñāpakaḥ | tad dvividhenāpi hetunā yuktaṃ hetumad idaṃ siddham | kiṃ ca --- anityaṃ pralayaṃ gacchati | yasmād utpattimat tasmād anityam | akāraṇavan nityam iti nityasya lakṣaṇam | tadviparītam idam ato 'nityam | tad yathā --- mṛtpiṇḍād utpanno ghaṭaḥ sa cānityo dṛṣṭaḥ | evaṃ mahadādi pradhānād utpannaṃ(p.13) tasmād anityaṃ tasminn eva ca līyate | tathā hi --- pradhāne buddhis tasyām ahaṅkāras tasminn indriyāṇi tanmātrāṇi ca teṣu bhūtāni pralayakāle līyante | tasmād anityam | kiñ ca --- avyāpi asarvagatam | yathā pradhānapuruṣau sarvagatau na tathedam ity arthaḥ | idaṃ hi yasminn eva pradeśe 'vasthitaṃ tasminn eva vartate | kiṃ ca --- sakriyam | yasmāt saṃsaraṇakāle mahadādi kāryaṃ sūkṣmaśarīram āśritya saṃsarati tasmāt sakriyam | kiṃ ca --- anekam bahuvidhaṃ trayoviṃśatiprakārakam | itarac ca --- āśritam | yad yasmād utpadyate tat tadāśritam | buddhiḥ pradhānam āśritā, tāṃ cāhaṅkāraḥ, taṃ cendriyāṇi tanmātrāṇi ca, tāni mahābhūtāny āśritāni | evam āśritam | layaṃ gacchatīti liṅgam | sāvayavam iti | avayantīty avayavā yathā piṇḍasya hastapādādyāḥ | śabdasparśarasarūpagandhādyavayavasampannaṃ vyaktam | kiṃ ca --- paratantram parādhīnam | yathā pitari jīvati putro na svatantra evaṃ vyaktam | pradhānatantrā buddhiḥ, buddhitantro 'haṅkāraḥ, ahaṅkāratantrāṇi indriyāṇi tanmātrāṇi ca, tanmātratantrāṇi mahābhūtānīti | evaṃ paratantram | vyaktam uktam | etadviparītalakṣaṇam avyaktam | ahetumat anutpannatvāt | nityam akāraṇavattvāt | vyāpi sarvagatatvāt | ābrahmastambaparyantaṃ puruṣavad vyāpya pradhānam avasthitam | niṣkriyaṃ sarvavāpakatvāt | ekaṃ sarvakāraṇatvāt | anāśritaṃ prabhaviṣṇutvāt | aliṅgam anutpattikatvāt | niravayavam amūrtatvāt | svatantraṃ sarvotpattikāraṇatvāt // SkMv_10 //
children.translated_text: 'Having a cause' (<s>hetumat</s>) — that which has a cause of origination is 'having a cause.' Cause (<s>hetu</s>), indication (<s>apadeśa</s>), ground (<s>nimitta</s>), primordial nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), and cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>) are synonymous. These are alternative terms for <s>Pradhāna</s> (the Primal Substance). Therefore, this twenty-three-fold mark (<s>liṅga</s>), from <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle) up to and including the elements, has a cause — namely <s>Pradhāna</s>. For thus: <s>Mahat</s>...

children.text: evam anayāryayā vyaktāvyaktayor vaidharmyam abhihitam | sādharmyam ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Thus, by this <s>āryā</s> verse, the dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>) between the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) and the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) has been stated. Now their similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) is stated —

children.text: triguṇam aviveki viṣayaḥ sāmānyam acetana prasavadharmi /
children.translated_text: Possessing three <s>guṇas</s>, non-discriminating, being an object [of experience], common, non-conscious, productive —

children.text: vyaktaṃ tathā pradhānaṃ tadviparītas tathā ca pumān // ISk_11 //
children.translated_text: Such is the manifest; and likewise <s>Pradhāna</s>. But <s>Puruṣa</s> is the opposite of these. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 11)

children.text: triguṇaṃ vyaktaṃ mahadādi | pradhānam api triguṇam | kāraṇānugatatvāt kāryasya | yathā kṛṣṇatantuḥ kāraṇaṃ paṭaḥ kāryam api kṛṣṇam eva bhavati | triguṇena kāryeṇāsya kāraṇam api triguṇaṃ bhavatīti pradhānaṃ sādhyate | kiṃ cānyat --- aviveki vyaktam | amī guṇā idaṃ vyaktam iti vivektuṃ na pāryate, tathā pradhānam api idaṃ pradhānaṃ amī guṇā iti na śakyate pṛthak kartum | kiṃ ca --- viṣayo vyaktaṃ mahadādi | sukhaduḥkhamohatayā bhogyaṃ tat puruṣasya | sa hi tasya bhoktā | tathā pradhānam api sarvapuruṣāṇāṃ kṣetrajñānāṃ bhogyam | sāmānyaṃ vyaktam | gaṇikāvat sarvapuruṣāṇām | tathā pradhānam(p.14) api | acetanaṃ vyaktam | sukhaduḥkhamohān na cetayati | tathā pradhānam api | prasavadharmi vyaktam | buddher ahaṅkāras tata indriyāṇi tanmātrāṇi ca tebhyo bhūtāni jāyante | evaṃ pradhānam api buddhiṃ prasūyate | uktam idaṃ vyaktāvyaktayoḥ sādharmyam | idānīṃ "tadviparītas tathā ca pumān" ity uktaṃ, tat pratipādayati | tābhyāṃ vyaktāvyaktābhyāṃ viparītaḥ | tayor yat sādharmyaṃ "triguṇam aviveki viṣayaḥ sāmānyam acetanaṃ prasavadharmi" ity uktam | tato 'sau viparīto vidharmī | aguṇo vivekī, aviṣayo 'sāmānyaḥ, cetano 'prasavadharmī ceti | vaidharmyam abhidhāya sādharmyam āha --- tathā ca pumān iti |
children.translated_text: The manifest — <s>Mahat</s> and the rest — possesses three <s>guṇas</s>. <s>Pradhāna</s> also possesses three <s>guṇas</s>, because the effect follows its cause. Just as black thread is the cause and the cloth is the effect, yet the cloth too is black — so from the effect possessing three <s>guṇas</s>, its cause too is established as possessing three <s>guṇas</s>; thus <s>Pradhāna</s> is proven. And what else — the manifest is non-discriminating (<s>aviveki</s>).

children.text: "hetumad anityam avyāpi sakriyam anekam āśritaṃ liṅgam /
children.translated_text: 'Having a cause, non-eternal, non-pervading, active, manifold, dependent, a mark (<s>liṅga</s>),

children.text: sāvayavaṃ paratantraṃ vyaktaṃ viparītam avyaktam" //
children.translated_text: Composite, and subordinate — [such is] the manifest; the unmanifest is the opposite.'

children.text: (sāṅkhyakārikā 10) ity uktam |
children.translated_text: (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 10) — thus it was stated.

children.text: tad yathā vyaktād visadṛśaṃ pradhānaṃ tathā pradhānasadharmā puruṣaḥ | tathā hi ahetumān nityo vyāpī niṣkriya eko 'nāśrito 'liṅgo niravayavaḥ svatantra iti // SkMv_11 //
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Pradhāna</s> is dissimilar to the manifest, so too <s>Puruṣa</s> shares properties with <s>Pradhāna</s> [in being unlike the manifest]. For thus: [<s>Puruṣa</s> is] without cause, eternal, all-pervading, inactive, singular, unsupported, without mark, without parts, and independent.

children.text: tatra triguṇa vyaktam avyaktaṃ ca nirguṇaḥ puruṣa ity uktam | kimātmakā guṇā ity atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: There, the manifest and the unmanifest both possess three <s>guṇas</s>, while <s>Puruṣa</s> is without <s>guṇas</s> — this has been stated. Now, what is the nature of the <s>guṇas</s>? This is addressed —

children.text: prītyaprītiviṣādātmakāḥ prakāśapravṛttiniyamārthāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having the nature of pleasure, displeasure, and despondency, [serving] the purposes of illumination, activity, and restraint,

children.text: anyo 'nyābhibhavāśrayajananamithunavṛttayaś ca guṇāḥ // ISk_12 //
children.translated_text: The <s>guṇas</s> function through mutual dominance, dependence, generation, and conjunction. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 12)

children.text: tatrāyaṃ samāsaḥ | prītiś cāprītiś ca viṣādaś ca te ātmā svarūpaṃ yeṣāṃ guṇānāṃ te bhavanti prītyaprītiviṣādātmakāḥ | teṣāṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate | tatra prītyātmakaṃ sattvam | ātmaśabdaḥ svabhāve vartate | kasmāt? sukhalakṣaṇatvāt | yo hi kaścit kvacit prītiṃ labhate tatra ārjavamārdavasatyaśaucahrībuddhikṣamānukampājñānādi ca tat sattvaṃ pratyetavyam | aprītyātmakaṃ rajaḥ | kasmāt? duḥkhalakṣaṇatvāt | yo hi kaścit kadācit kvacid aprītim upalabhate tatra dveṣadrohamatsaranindāstambhotkaṇṭhānikṛtivañcanābandhavadhacchedanāni ca tad rajaḥ pratyetavyam | viṣādātmakaṃ tamaḥ | kasmāt?
