mohalakṣaṇatvāt | yo hi kaścit kadācit kvacin moham upalabhate, tatrājñānamadālasyabhayadainyākarmaṇyatānāstikyaviṣādasvapnādi ca tat tamaḥ pratyetavyam |(p.15) kiṃ cānyat --- prakāśapravṛttiniyamārthāḥ | prakāśaś ca pravṛttiś ca niyamaś ca te arthā yeṣāṃ tathoktāḥ | tatra prakāśayitavyam iti sattvasya, pravartitavyam iti rajasaḥ, niyantavyaṃ saṃhartavyam iti tamasaḥ | kiṃ cānyat --- anyonyābhibhavāśrayajananamithunavṛttayaś ca guṇāḥ | tatrāpi samāsaḥ | anyonyābhibhavāś ca anyonyāśrayāś ca anyonyajananāś ca anyonyamithunāś ca yeṣāṃ guṇānām anyonyavṛttayaś ca vidyante tathoktāḥ | caśabdaḥ samuccaye draṣṭavyaḥ | prītyādayaś ca tāvat prāgabhihitāḥ | anyonyābhibhavāś ceti rajastamasor abhibhavāt śāntā vṛttir utpadyate sattvasya dharmādyā | sattvatamasor abhibhavād rajaso ghorā vṛttir utpadyate adharmādyā | sattvarajasor abhibhavāt tamaso mūḍhā vṛttir utpadyate ajñānādyā | kiṃ cānyat --- anyonyāśrayāś ca guṇāḥ | sattvaṃ hi pravṛttiniyamāv āśritya prakāśayati | rajaḥ prakāśaniyamāv āśritya pravartayati | tamaḥ prakāśapravṛttī āśritya niyamayati | tridaṇḍaviṣṭambhavad amī veditavyā iti | kiṃ cānyat --- anyonyajananāś ca guṇāḥ | anyonyaṃ janayanti | kadācit sattvaṃ rajastamasī janayati | kadācit tamaḥ sattvarajasī janayati | yathā saparikarakumbhakārādhiṣṭhito mṛtpiṇḍo ghaṭaṃ janayati tadvaj janayanti | anyonyaṃ bodhayantīty etat pratigṛhyate | yathā devadattayajñadattau parasparaṃ bodhayata | evaṃ buddhisthā guṇāḥ sattvarajastamāṃsi parasparaṃ bodhayanti | evam anyonyajanakā guṇāḥ | kiṃ cānyat --- anyonyamithunāś ca guṇāḥ | aviyogakadharmatvāt | evaṃ hy āhuḥ ---
children.translated_text: Here is the summary: pleasure, displeasure, and despondency — those whose self, i.e. essential nature, consists of these are the <s>guṇas</s>; they are 'having the nature of pleasure, displeasure, and despondency.' Their characteristics are stated. Of these, <s>sattva</s> has pleasure as its nature. The word '<s>ātma</s>' (self) is used in the sense of 'inherent nature.' Why? Because it is characterized by happiness. For whoever, wherever experiences pleasure...

children.text: "rajaso mithuna sattvaṃ sattvasya mithunaṃ rajaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rajas</s> is the partner of <s>sattva</s>; <s>sattva</s> is the partner of <s>rajas</s>;

children.text: ubhayoḥ sattvarajasor mithunaṃ tama ucyate" //
children.translated_text: And the partner of both <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> is said to be <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: (devībhāgavatapurāṇa 3 |50)
children.translated_text: (<s>Devībhāgavatapurāṇa</s> 3.50)

children.text: kiṃ cānyat --- anyonyavṛttayaś ca guṇāḥ | anyonyasya vṛttiṃ janayanti | yathā kācit strī nayavinayavilāsalīlāvatī bhartur ātmano bandhuvargasya ca prītiṃ janayati | saiva sapatnīṣu duḥkhamohau janayati | evaṃ sattvena strībhūtena rajasas tamasaś ca vṛttir janitā | evam anyeṣv api yojyam // SkMv_12 //
children.translated_text: And what else — the <s>guṇas</s> have mutual operations. They generate the functioning of one another. Just as a certain woman, endowed with grace, modesty, charm, and playfulness, generates pleasure for her husband, for herself, and for her kinsmen — yet that very same [woman] generates suffering and delusion in her co-wives. Thus, when <s>sattva</s>, assuming the role of the woman, [generates] the functions of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>...

children.text:
atrāha --- na khalu sattvarajastamāṃsi jātyantarāṇi | kutaḥ | svabhāveṣv avasthānāt | iha khalu rūpayauvanadākṣiṇyamatisādhutvasmṛtyugrabhāvābhāvalīlāvilāsasampannā strī sattvasya rūpam upadiśyate | sā ca bhartuḥ sukhāvahā bhavati, sapatnīnāṃ duḥkhāya rāgiṇāṃ mohāya ca | tathā kṣatriyā duḥkhapraharaṇakṛtāparādhāṃ dasyusenām abhinighnatī rajaso rūpam ity upadiśyate | tena ca dasyubhir upadrutānāṃ dāryamāṇānāṃ sukhāvahā bhavati | dasyūnāṃ duḥkhāya mohāya ca | tathā ghanāghano mahākṛṣṇo meghas toyādhmāto 'valambī grasamāna iva nabho bhūmiṃ cābhivardhamānaḥ sabalākaḥ savidyudgambhīrastanitas tamaso rūpam ity upadiśyate | sa ca karṣakāṇāṃ sajjīkṛtabījopakaraṇānāṃ sukho bhavati | sa evānācchāditaśaraṇānām anupārjitabhaktasnehalavaṇānām apraguṇitatṛṇakāṣṭhānāṃ proṣitavadhūnāṃ ca duḥkho mūḍhaś ca | tad evam avasthitasvabhāvatvād ekaṃ sattvarajastamāṃsi |
atrocyate jātyantarāṇy amūni trīṇi | lakṣaṇapṛthaktvavyavasthānāt | katham iti cet tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one raises the question: surely <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> are not of different species? Why? Because they abide in [their own] essential natures. Here indeed, a woman endowed with beauty, youth, grace, intelligence, goodness, memory, sternness, equanimity, playfulness, and charm is taught as the form of <s>sattva</s>. She brings happiness to her husband, suffering to her co-wives...

children.text: sattvaṃ laghu prakāśakam iṣṭam upaṣṭambhakaṃ calaṃ ca rajaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> is light and illuminating; <s>rajas</s> is stimulating and mobile;

children.text: guru varaṇakam eva tamaḥ pradīpavac cārthato vṛttiḥ // ISk_13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tamas</s> is indeed heavy and concealing. Their functioning is purposive, like a lamp. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 13)

children.text: atra yat pūrvasyām āryāyām abhihitaṃ sattvalakṣaṇaṃ tal laghutvaprakāśakalakṣaṇaṃ ca | yadā sattvam utkaṭaṃ bhavati devadatte tadā laghūny aṅgāni, viśuddhānīndriyāṇi svaviṣayagrahaṇasamarthāni bhavanti | tadā mantavyam adya me sattvam utkaṭatvena vartate | iṣṭaṃ ca svarūpasādhanahetutvāt | upaṣṭambhakaṃ calaṃ ca rajaḥ | upaṣṭambhakaṃ prerakamunnāḍir ity arthaḥ | yathā mattavṛṣo vṛṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā uddhato bhavati tadvat | athavā garvaś calā kriyety arthaḥ | evaṃ yasmin devadatte yajñadatte vā raja utkaṭaṃ bhavati sa kalahaṃ mṛgayate | kiṃ cānyat calacittaś ca bhavati grāmaṃ gacchāmi striyaṃ kāmaye tapaḥ karomi ityādi | evaṃ nityam utsukamanā bhavati | etad rajolakṣaṇam | tama āha --- guru varaṇakam eva tamaḥ | yad gurutvam āvaraṇatvaṃ cāsti tat tamaḥ | yadā gurūṇy aṅgāni bhavanti | indriyāṇy alasāni svaviṣayagrahaṇāsamarthāni bhavanti | tadānīṃ mantavyam etat tama utkaṭatvena vartata iti | tasmāj jātyantarāṇy eva sattvarajastamāṃsi | yat punar abhyadhāyi --- strī kṣatriyā meghaś ceti | atra traye 'pi brūmaḥ | sattvaṃ rajastamasī āśritya svena rūpeṇāṅgāṅgibhāvaṃ gacchati | tasyāpakārād duḥkham utpadyate | evaṃ rajastamasī yojye | parasparaviruddhānāṃ guṇānāṃ katham ekā vṛttir bhavatīty atrāha --- parasparaviruddhāḥ(p.17) śatravo na hy ekam arthaṃ kurvanti | ime ca guṇāḥ parasparaviruddhā api puruṣārthaṃ kurvanti | kutaḥ | pradīpavac cārthato vṛttiḥ | pradīpena tulyaṃ pradīpavat | arthataḥ kāryavaśāt | parasparaviruddhānām apy amīṣāṃ vṛttir dṛṣṭā | yathā tailāgnivarttikāsaṃyogāt parasparaviruddhā api padārthāḥ saṃhatya ekam arthaṃ prakāśarūpaṃ niṣpādayanty evaṃ guṇā api parasparaviruddhāḥ saṃhatya puruṣārthaṃ kurvanti // SkMv_13 //
children.translated_text: Here, the characteristic of <s>sattva</s> stated in the previous <s>āryā</s> verse is also characterized by lightness and luminosity. When <s>sattva</s> becomes predominant in <s>Devadatta</s>, then his limbs become light, his sense-organs become purified and capable of apprehending their respective objects. Then one should know: 'Today <s>sattva</s> is predominant in me...'

children.text: atrāha --- ayam antaraḥ praśno hi | yad uktaṃ pūrvasyām āryāyāṃ "triguṇam aviveki viṣayaḥ sāmānyam acetanaṃ prasavadharmi | vyaktam --- "tat katham evaṃ jñāyate 'vyaktam api triguṇatvādiyuktam | atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here a question is raised: this is an intermediate question. It was stated in the previous <s>āryā</s>: 'Possessing three <s>guṇas</s>, non-discriminating, being an object, common, non-conscious, productive — such is the manifest.' How then is it known that the unmanifest also possesses three <s>guṇas</s> and the rest? This is answered —

children.text: avivekyādiḥ siddhas traiguṇyāt tadviparyayābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: The [properties] beginning with non-discrimination are established [for the unmanifest] because of [its] possessing three <s>guṇas</s>, and because the opposite [of these properties] is absent;

children.text: kāraṇaguṇātmakatvāt kāryasyāvyaktam api siddham // ISk_14 //
children.translated_text: Because the effect has the nature of the <s>guṇas</s> of the cause, the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is also established. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 14)

children.text: yo 'py ayam avivekyādir gaṇaḥ prasavadharmyantaḥ sa vyakte 'pi siddho 'vyakte 'pi siddhaḥ | kathaṃ gamyate | traiguṇyāt | yat triguṇaṃ tad aviviktam, yad aviviktaṃ tad viṣayaṃ, yad viṣayaṃ tat sāmānyaṃ, yat sāmānyaṃ tad acetanam, yad acetanaṃ tat prasavadharmi | tasmād avivekyādir guṇas traiguṇyād eva siddhaḥ | tadviparyayābhāvāt | iha hi yatra tantavas tatraiva paṭaḥ yatra paṭas tatraiva tantavaḥ, yas tantūn paśyati sa paṭaṃ paśyati, yo vā paṭaṃ paśyati sa tantūn paśyati | evam eva tantupaṭayor iva vyaktāvyaktayoḥ sambandhaḥ | dūre hi pradhānaṃ sannikṛṣṭe vyaktam | yo hi vyaktaṃ paśyati sa cāvyaktam api paśyati | yo vā yogī pradhānaṃ paśyati sa vyaktam api paśyati | tasmād viparyayābhāvād avivekyādigaṇena siddham avyaktam | itaś ca siddham | kāraṇaguṇātmakatvāt kāryasyāvyaktam api siddham | kāraṇasya guṇāḥ kāraṇaguṇās te ātmā svabhāvo yasya tadbhāvaḥ kāraṇaguṇātmakatvam | ātmaśabdaḥ svabhāve vartate | kāraṇaguṇasvabhāvatvāt kāryasya | iha loke yadātmakaṃ karaṇaṃ tadātmakam eva kāryam api bhavati | kāraṇānugatatvāt kāryasya | yathā kaṭunimbavṛkṣāt kaṭur eva raso bhavati madhurāc ca madhuro drākṣādirasaḥ | tasmād avivekyādigaṇena siddham avyaktam | tatra yad uktaṃ bhavatā tat(p.18) katham evaṃ jñāyate avyaktam avivekyādigaṇena yuktam iti tad evam eva tribhir hetubhiḥ pratipāditam | atrāha --- iha loke yan na vidyate tan nāsti | yathā dvitīyam anīśvaraśiraḥ, tṛtīyaḥ pāṇiḥ, śaśaviṣāṇaṃ, vandhyāputrikābhrūvilāsādayo vā | naiva tāvat pradhānapuruṣāv upalabhyete, tau kathaṃ hi sta iti gamyate | himavata upalagaṇaparimāṇaṃ nopalabhyate | kiṃ tan nāsti? evaṃ pradhānapuruṣāv anupalabhyamānāv apy upalabhyete hetubhiḥ | tāṃś ca hetūn upariṣṭād vakṣyāmaḥ // SkMv_14 //
children.translated_text: This group [of properties] beginning with non-discrimination (<s>aviveka</s>) and ending with productiveness (<s>prasavadharmin</s>) is established both in the manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) and in the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>). How is this known? From the possession of the three <s>guṇas</s>. That which possesses the three <s>guṇas</s> is non-discriminated; that which is non-discriminated is an object; that which is an object is common; that which is common is non-conscious; that which is non-conscious is productive. Therefore, the property beginning with non-discrimination is established from the very possession of the three <s>guṇas</s>. Because of the non-existence of the opposite: For indeed, where there are threads, there is the cloth; where there is the cloth, there are the threads. One who sees the threads sees the cloth; one who sees the cloth sees the threads. In just this way, the relationship between the manifest and the unmanifest is like that of threads and cloth. <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) is remote; the manifest is proximate. One who sees the manifest also sees the unmanifest; and the <s>yogī</s> who sees <s>Pradhāna</s> also sees the manifest. Therefore, because of the non-existence of the opposite, the unmanifest is established through the group [of properties] beginning with non-discrimination. And it is established for this further reason: because the effect has the nature of the qualities of the cause, the unmanifest is also established. The qualities of the cause — those are the essential nature (<s>ātman</s>) of [the effect], whose state is having the nature of the qualities of the cause. The word '<s>ātman</s>' here means 'essential nature.' Because the effect has the essential nature of the qualities of the cause — in this world, whatever is the nature of the cause, the effect too is of that very nature, because the effect follows the cause. Just as from the bitter <s>nimba</s> (neem) tree comes only a bitter taste, and from the sweet [grape vine] comes a sweet grape-juice, and so forth. Therefore, the unmanifest is established by the group [of properties] beginning with non-discrimination. Now, regarding what you said — how is it known that the unmanifest is endowed with the group [of properties] beginning with non-discrimination? — that has thus been demonstrated by these three arguments. Here one objects: In this world, what does not exist simply is not. Just as a second head on a headless god, a third hand, a hare's horn, or the charming eyebrow-play of a barren woman's daughter, and so on. If <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> are never perceived, how can they be known to exist? [We reply:] The exact quantity of rocks on the <s>Himālaya</s> is not perceived — does that mean they do not exist? In the same way, <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, though not perceived [directly], are perceived through inferential reasons. And those reasons we shall state below. // <s>SkMv</s> 14 //

children.text: ta ucyante ---
children.translated_text: Those [reasons] are stated:

children.text: bhedānāṃ parimāṇāt samanvayāc chaktitaḥ pravṛtteś ca /
children.translated_text: Because of the finitude of modifications, because of homogeneity, because of activity proceeding from potency,

children.text: kāraṇakāryavibhāgād avibhāgād vaiśvarūpyasya // ISk_15 //
children.translated_text: And because of the separation of cause and effect, because of the non-separation of the universal form — // <s>ISk</s> 15 //

children.text: asti pradhānam | kutaḥ? bhedānāṃ parimāṇāt | loke yatra kartāsti tasya parimāṇaṃ dṛṣṭam | yathā kulālaḥ parimitāt mṛtpiṇḍāt parimitam eva ghaṭaṃ kurute prasthagrāhakam āḍhakagrāhakaṃ vā | evaṃ vyaktaṃ parimitam | ekā buddhir eko 'haṅkāraḥ pañca tanmātrāṇi ekādaśendriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtāni iti trayoviṃśatikam | evam etat parimitaṃ vyaktaṃ dṛṣṭvānumānena sādhayāmo 'sty asya kāraṇaṃ pradhānaṃ yad vyaktaṃ parimitam utpādayati | yadi ca pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ na syān niṣparimāṇam idaṃ vyaktaṃ syāt | asti cāsya parimāṇaṃ tasmād asti pradhānam | itaś cāsti samanvayadarśanāt | kasya samanvayāt? bhedānām eva | asmād eva kāraṇāc śakalakapālamātrasamastasamanvayaḥ | bhūṣaṇādīn dṛṣṭvā tattvena darśayati | sāmānyaprakaraṇāl lokabhedānām ekaikajātisamanvayo dṛṣṭaḥ | teṣāṃ dharmo 'nvayaḥ, tasmāt samanvayadarśanāt paśyāmo 'sti pradhānaṃ kāraṇam iti | itaś cāsti --- śaktitaḥ pravṛtteś ca | iha yo yasminn arthe śaktaḥ sa tasminn eva pravartate | tad yathā kumbhakāro ghaṭaghaṭikāśarāvodañcavādikaraṇe śaktaḥ | ataḥ sādhayāmaḥ pradhānasyāpy asti śaktir yayā śaktyā vyaktam utpādayati | sā ca śaktir nirāśrayā na bhavati | tasmād asti pradhānaṃ yatra śaktir avatiṣṭhate | itaś cāsti --- kāraṇakāryavibhāgāt | karotīti kāraṇam, kriyata iti kāryaṃ, tayor vibhāgas tasmāt | tad yathā mṛtpiṇḍaḥ kāraṇaṃ ghaṭaḥ kāryam | sa eva(p.19) hi madhūdakapayaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ dhāraṇe samartho na tu mṛtpiṇḍaḥ | evaṃ vyaktāvyaktayor vibhāgaḥ | anyad vyaktaṃ mahadahaṅkāratanmātrendriyamahābhūtaparyantaṃ, tac ca kāryam | anyac ca avyaktaṃ pradhānaṃ viparītaṃ kāraṇam iti | tasmād asti pradhānam | itaś cāsti --- avibhāgād vaiśvarūpyasya | na vibhāgo 'vibhāgaḥ | viśvarūpasya bhāvo vaiśvarūpyam | bahurūpam ity arthaḥ | tasya | trailokyaṃ pañcasu mahābhūteṣv avibhāgaṃ gacchati | pañcamahābhūtāni tanmātreṣv avibhāgaṃ gacchanti | pañcatanmātrāṇy ekādaśendriyāṇi cāhaṅkāre | ahaṅkāro buddhau | sā ca pradhāne | itthaṃ trayo lokāḥ pralayakāle pradhāne 'vibhaktāḥ | prakarṣeṇa dhīyate sthāpyate atrākhilam iti pradhānam | tato hi sṛṣṭau sad evāvirbhavati | na hy asata utpattir na ca sato 'bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Pradhāna</s> exists. Why? Because of the finitude of modifications. In the world, where there is a maker, finitude of [the product] is observed. Just as a potter makes from a finite clay-lump only a finite pot — one holding a <s>prastha</s> measure or one holding an <s>āḍhaka</s> measure. In the same way, the manifest is finite: one <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), one <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), five <s>Tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), eleven <s>Indriyas</s> (sense-organs), and five <s>Mahābhūtas</s> (gross elements) — thus twenty-three [principles].

children.text: "nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ" /
children.translated_text: 'Of the non-existent there is no coming into being; of the existent there is no cessation of being.'

children.text: iti gītāsu(2 |16) | "sad eva somyedam agra āsīt"[chāndogyopaniṣad 6 |2 |1] iti śruteś ca | tad yathā --- dadhyādayaḥ prāk prasūteḥ kṣīre 'vibhaktāḥ santy eva | yady asata utpattis tadā kāṣṭhakhaṇḍād api ghaṭādyutpattiḥ syāt | yato na bhavati | tasmān mṛtpiṇḍe kāraṇe ghaṭādeḥ sata evotpattir iti samīcīnam | yathā jalabhūmyor etadrasagandhādivaiśvarūpyam avibhaktam asty eva sthāvarāṇāṃ jaṅgameṣu jaṅgamānāṃ sthāvareṣu | evaṃ jātyanucchedena sarvaṃ sarvātmakam iti // SkMv_15 //
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Gītā</s> (2.16). And from the <s>Śruti</s>: 'Being alone, O gentle one, was this in the beginning' [<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 6.2.1]. For example: curds and the like exist undifferentiated in milk prior to their production. If there were production from the non-existent, then pots and the like would arise even from a piece of wood. Since that does not happen, therefore the production of pots and the like from the clay-lump as cause is only the production of the existent from the existent — this is the correct understanding.

children.text: asti pradhānaṃ yatra mahadādiliṅgam avibhāgaṃ gacchati | ity evam avaśyambhāvī avibhāgaḥ paścād vibhāgaś cāvirbhavati tat pradhānam | atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: <s>Pradhāna</s> exists — that into which the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) beginning with <s>Mahat</s> returns as undifferentiated. Thus, this non-differentiation necessarily occurs first, and afterward differentiation manifests again — that is <s>Pradhāna</s>. Here it is said:

children.text: kāraṇam asty avyaktaṃ pravartate triguṇataḥ samudayāc ca /
children.translated_text: The cause is the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>); it operates because of [its possession of] the three <s>guṇas</s>, and because of combination;

children.text: pariṇāmataḥ salilavat pratipratiguṇāśrayaviśeṣāt // ISk_16 //
children.translated_text: Through transformation, like water, [it differentiates] because of the specific distinctions of the substrate of each <s>guṇa</s>. // <s>ISk</s> 16 //

children.text: kāraṇam asty avyaktam iti | tad evaṃ pañcabhir ebhir hetubhir jñāyate 'sti tatkāraṇam ekam asya jagato 'vyaktaṃ mūlam iti | atrāha yady ekaṃ pradhānaṃ kathaṃ tarhi anekaṃ kāryam utpādayati | tathā hi naikas tantuḥ paṭākhyaṃ kāryaṃ janayati | itthaṃ pradhānam ekam anekaṃ kāryaṃ janayatīti na jāghaṭīti | ataḥ samādhīyate --- pravartate triguṇataḥ | pradhāne hi sattvarajastamasām avasthānād bahutvasambhavaḥ | tasmāt triguṇataḥ pravartate tridhā vyavahāraḥ | samudayāc ca | yathā gaṅgāyāṃ srotāṃsi samuditāni gaṅgām ārabhante, yathā vā tantavaḥ samuditāḥ paṭaṃ kurvanti evaṃ sattvarajastamāṃsi trayo guṇāḥ samuditāḥ pradhānasthā vyaktaṃ kurvanti | atrāha --- iha loke dvividhaṃ kāraṇaṃ pariṇāmakatvād(p.20) apariṇāmakatvāc ca | tatrāpariṇāmakatvān mṛtpiṇḍadaṇḍasūtrodakavidalān paśyāmaḥ | pariṇāmataś ca kṣīraṃ dadhīti | tatra pradhānaṃ kathaṃ kāraṇam ity atrocyate --- pariṇāmataḥ | yathā kṣīraṃ dadhibhāvena pariṇamati, yad eva kṣīraṃ tad eva dadhi, evaṃ pradhānaṃ vyaktabhāvena pariṇamati | dadhivad vyaktaṃ kṣīravat pradhānam ity arthaḥ | yad evāvyaktaṃ tad eva vyaktam iti | tasmād ucyate pariṇāmataḥ pradhānaṃ kāraṇam iti | atrāha ko dṛṣṭāntaḥ? tad ucyate --- salilavat | yathā salilam ekaṃ himavad himabhāvena pariṇamati, yathā cekṣuraso rasikāṣaṇḍamatsarikāśarkarāphāṇitaguḍabhāvena pariṇamati | yathā vā kṣīraṃ drapsyadadhimastunavanītaghṛtāriṣṭakilāṭakūrcikādibhāvena pariṇamati | evam evāvyaktam ādhyātmikena buddhyahaṅkāratanmātrendriyabhūtabhāvena pariṇamati, ādhidaivikena śītoṣṇavātavarṣādibhāvena pariṇamati | atrāha --- ekasmāt pradhānād utpannās trayo lokāḥ kathaṃ viṣamāḥ? iha ye devās te sukhino manuṣyās te duḥkhinas tiryañco mūḍhāḥ | ekasmāt pradhānād utpannānāṃ trayāṇāṃ lokānāṃ kathaṃ vaiṣamyaṃ mūḍhatvādinety atrocyate --- pratipratiguṇāśrayaviśeṣāt | tad yathā --- ekarasam antarikṣād jalaṃ patitam | tac ca medinīṃ prāpya nānārasatāṃ yāti | pṛthagbhājanaviśeṣāt | evam ime trayo lokā ekasmād api pradhānād utpannā guṇavaiṣamyāt pṛthagbhāvaṃ gatāḥ | yathā deveṣu sattvam utkaṭaṃ tatas te sukhinaḥ, tatrāpi rajastamasī gauṇatayā staḥ | manuṣyeṣu raja utkaṭaṃ tatas te duḥkhitāḥ, teṣv api sattvatamasī staḥ | tiryagyonigateṣu tama utkaṭaṃ tatas te mūḍhāḥ | teṣv api sattvarajasī staḥ | evam ekasmād utpannānāṃ trayāṇāṃ lokānāṃ vaiṣamyaṃ bhavati // SkMv_16 //
children.translated_text: The cause is the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>). Thus, by these five reasons, it is known: the cause of this world, one and unmanifest, is the root. Here an objection arises: If <s>Pradhāna</s> (the Primal Substance) is one, how then does it produce a manifold effect? For a single thread does not generate the effect called a cloth. Thus the proposition 'one <s>Pradhāna</s> generates a manifold effect' does not hold. To this, the resolution is: It operates by virtue of its three <s>guṇas</s>. For in <s>Pradhāna</s>, because <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> abide [therein], the possibility of multiplicity exists. Therefore, by virtue of the three <s>guṇas</s>, the activity is threefold. And by their combination: just as the tributaries, when combined, constitute the <s>Gaṅgā</s>; or just as threads, when combined, make a cloth — so <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, the three <s>guṇas</s>, combined and residing in <s>Pradhāna</s>, produce the manifest. Here an objection arises: In this world, causation is of two kinds — through transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) and through non-transformation. Among the non-transformative, we observe clay-lumps, sticks, threads, water, and split-bamboo [as causes of pots etc.]. And through transformation: milk [becomes] curds. How then is <s>Pradhāna</s> a cause? The answer is: through transformation. Just as milk transforms into the state of curds — the very milk itself is the curds — so <s>Pradhāna</s> transforms into the state of the manifest. The manifest is like curds; <s>Pradhāna</s> is like milk — this is the meaning. What is unmanifest is itself the manifest. Therefore it is said: <s>Pradhāna</s> is the cause through transformation. Here an objection arises: What is the illustration? The answer: Like water. Just as a single body of water on the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas) transforms into the state of ice; just as sugarcane juice transforms into the states of crude sugar, dry sugar, crystalline sugar, molasses, and refined sugar; or just as milk transforms into the states of cream, curds, whey, butter, ghee, fermented liquor, dried curd, and cheese etc. — so too the unmanifest transforms on the subjective (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) side into the states of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties), and <s>bhūtas</s> (gross elements); and on the cosmic (<s>ādhidaivika</s>) side into the states of cold, heat, wind, rain, and the like. Here an objection arises: How are the three worlds, born from one <s>Pradhāna</s>, unequal? In this world, the gods are happy, humans are suffering, and animals are deluded. How is there inequality among the three worlds born from one <s>Pradhāna</s>, such as delusion etc.? The answer: Because of the particular predominance of each <s>guṇa</s> in its respective substrate. Just as: water falling from the sky is of one taste, but upon reaching the earth, it takes on various tastes — due to the difference of distinct vessels. So too, these three worlds, though born from one <s>Pradhāna</s>, have reached different states due to the disparity of <s>guṇas</s>. Among the gods, <s>sattva</s> is predominant, hence they are happy; even there, <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> exist in a subordinate capacity. Among humans, <s>rajas</s> is predominant, hence they suffer; even there, <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> exist. Among those in animal births, <s>tamas</s> is predominant, hence they are deluded; even there, <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> exist. Thus, there is inequality among the three worlds born from one [<s>Pradhāna</s>].

children.text: evaṃ dvābhyām āryābhyāṃ pradhānasyādhigamaḥ kṛtaḥ | ata ūrdhvaṃ puruṣasyādhigamaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ | atrāha --- kecid ācāryā iti manyante śarīrendriyabuddhyādivyatirikto nāsti paramātmā | api ca ---
children.translated_text: Thus, the comprehension of <s>Pradhāna</s> has been accomplished in two <s>āryā</s> verses. Henceforth, we shall accomplish the comprehension of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self). Here an objection arises: Some teachers hold that there is no supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) distinct from the body, sense faculties, intellect, and the like. Moreover:

children.text:
etāvān eva puruṣo yāvad indriyagocaraḥ /
iti |
children.translated_text: A person (<s>puruṣa</s>) is only so much as is within the range of the senses.

children.text: atrocyate --- śarīrendriyabuddhyādivyatirikta ātmā astīti | ko dṛṣṭāntaḥ? yathā asikośavat | muñjeṣīkāvat | uktaṃ ca ---
children.translated_text: To this it is replied: The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) exists as distinct from the body, senses, intellect, and the like. What is the illustration? Like a sword and its sheath. Like a reed within a <s>muñja</s> grass stalk. And it is said:

children.text: maśakodumbareṣīkāmuñjamatsyāmbhasāṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as a gnat and a fig, a reed and <s>muñja</s> grass, a fish and water —

children.text: ekatve 'pi pṛthagbhāvas tathā kṣetrātmanor nṛpa //
children.translated_text: Though united, are [in fact] distinct — so too the field and the Self, O King.

children.text: evaṃ śarīrendriyabuddhyādibhiḥ kṣīranīravad ekībhūto 'pi tadvyatirikto 'sti paramātmā puruṣo 'pi | pradhānavat sūkṣmatvān nopalabhyate iti tadadhigamāya hetur abhidhīyate ---
children.translated_text: Thus, even though the supreme Self, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, has become unified with the body, senses, intellect, and the like — like milk and water — it exists as distinct from them. Like <s>Pradhāna</s>, it is not apprehended because of its subtlety. Therefore, to establish its comprehension, the reasons are stated:

children.text: saṅghātaparārthatvāt triguṇādiviparyayād adhiṣṭhānāt /
children.translated_text: Because composites exist for another's purpose, because of the opposite of the three <s>guṇas</s> etc., because of governance,

children.text: puruṣo 'sti bhoktṛbhāvāt kaivalyārthapravṛtteś ca // ISk_17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> exists — because of the nature of being an experiencer, and because of the activity directed toward <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation).

children.text: asti puruṣaḥ | saṅghātaparārthatvāt | yataḥ saṅghātaś ca parārthaḥ | tasmād hetoḥ | iha loke ye saṅghātās te parārthā dṛṣṭāḥ paryaṅkarathaśaraṇādayaḥ | evaṃ gātrāṇāṃ mahadādīnāṃ saṅghātaḥ samudāyaḥ parārtha eva | (tasmād asti nūnam anyonyādhiṣṭhito yadartho 'yaṃ saṅghāta iti saṅgatiḥ |) paryaṅkarathādayaḥ kāṣṭhasaṅghātāḥ | gṛhādayaḥ kāṣṭheṣṭakādisaṅghātāḥ | na hi te rathagṛhaparyaṅkādayaḥ kim api svārthaṃ sādhayanti | na vā parasparārthāḥ | kiṃ tv asty asau devadattādir yo 'smin paryaṅke śete rathena gacchati gṛhe nivasatīti | (cetasaḥ pratītyā) | evam amī mahadādayaś cakṣurādayo na svārthā na ca parasparārthāḥ, kiṃ tu parārthāḥ | yaś cāsau paraḥ sa cātmā | tasmād anumīmahe asti puruṣaḥ, yasyārthe cakṣurādisaṅghātaḥ śarīram utpannam iti | itaś cāsti --- triguṇādiviparyayāt | trayo guṇā yasya gaṇasyādau sambhavanti sa triguṇādiḥ | triguṇāder viparyayaḥ | tasmāt paśyāmo 'sti puruṣa iti | uktaṃ pūrvasyām āryāyāṃ triguṇam avivekītyādi vyaktapradhānasādharmyam | "tadviparītas tathā ca pumān" iti | aguṇavivekyaviṣayāsāmānyacetanāprasavadharmādiviparyayād ātmano 'stitvaṃ pṛthaktvaṃ ca siddham | ataś cāsti | adhiṣṭhānāt | na hy antareṇādhiṣṭhātāraṃ bhavati vastujātam | tad yatheha loke laṅghanaplavanadhāvanasamarthair aśvair yukto rathaḥ sārathinādhiṣṭhitaḥ pravartate | atha sārathinānadhiṣṭhitaḥ pravartate tataḥ śarīranāśaḥ syāt | na cātmavināśāya pravartate | api coktaṃ ṣaṣṭitantre --- "puruṣādhiṣṭhitaṃ pradhānaṃ pravartate" iti | tataḥ paśyāmo 'sau paramātmā asti puruṣo yenādhiṣṭhitaṃ pradhānaṃ mahadahaṅkāratanmātrendriyabhūtāny utpādayati | tasmād asti puruṣa iti | itaś cāsti --- bhoktṛbhāvāt | iha madhurāmlatiktalavaṇakaṭukaṣāyāḥ ṣaḍ rasāḥ | etaiḥ ṣaḍbhī rasair yuktaṃ bhojanaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhoktā sādhyate | asti bhoktā yasyedaṃ bhojanam | evam idaṃ vyaktāvyaktaṃ dṛṣṭvā sādhayāmo 'sty asau paramātmā puruṣo yasyedaṃ bhoktur vyaktāvyaktaṃ bhogyam iti | itaś cāsti --- kaivalyārthapravṛtteś ca | kevalabhāvaḥ kaivalyaṃ mokṣa ity arthaḥ | yā tasya pradhānasya pravṛttiḥ sā kaivalyārthā pravṛttiḥ pradhānasyeti // SkMv_17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> exists. Because composites exist for another's purpose. Since composites are for another's purpose — for this reason. In this world, whatever composites exist are observed to be for another's purpose — beds, chariots, shelters, and the like. Similarly, the composite — the assemblage — of the body and <s>Mahat</s> etc. is indeed for another's purpose. (Therefore, there must surely be someone other than these, for whose purpose this composite exists — this is the connection.) Beds, chariots, and the like are composites of wood. Houses and the like are composites of wood, brick, etc. For these beds, houses, chariots, and the like do not accomplish anything for their own purpose. Nor are they for each other's purpose. Rather, there is that <s>Devadatta</s> or someone else who sleeps on this bed, travels by this chariot, dwells in this house. (By the cognition of consciousness.) Similarly, these — <s>Mahat</s> etc., the eyes and other senses — are not for their own purpose nor for each other's purpose, but for another's purpose. And that 'other' is the Self (<s>Ātman</s>). Therefore we infer: <s>Puruṣa</s> exists — for whose purpose the composite of eyes and other senses, the body, has been produced. And for this reason too [<s>Puruṣa</s> exists]: because of the opposite of the three <s>guṇas</s> and so forth. 'That whose beginning is the three <s>guṇas</s>' — that is the <s>triguṇādi</s>. The opposite of <s>triguṇādi</s>. Therefore we see: <s>Puruṣa</s> exists. In the previous <s>āryā</s> verse, the similarity between the manifest and <s>Pradhāna</s> was stated as 'possessing three <s>guṇas</s>, non-discriminating' etc. [And it was stated:] '<s>Puruṣa</s> is the opposite of that.' From being without <s>guṇas</s>, discriminating, non-objective, uncommon, conscious, non-productive etc. — the existence and distinctness of the Self are established. And for this reason: because of governance. Without a governor, no collection of things comes into being. Just as in this world, a chariot yoked with horses capable of leaping, swimming, and running operates when governed by a charioteer — but if not governed by a charioteer, it would set off and the body [of the rider] would be destroyed — yet it does not operate toward self-destruction. Moreover, it is said in the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>: '<s>Pradhāna</s>, governed by <s>Puruṣa</s>, operates.' Therefore we see: that supreme Self, <s>Puruṣa</s>, exists — governed by whom, <s>Pradhāna</s> produces <s>Mahat</s>, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, the <s>tanmātras</s>, <s>indriyas</s>, and <s>bhūtas</s>. Therefore <s>Puruṣa</s> exists. And for this reason: because of the nature of being an experiencer. In this world, there are six tastes: sweet, sour, bitter, salty, pungent, and astringent. Seeing food endowed with these six tastes, an experiencer is established: there is an experiencer for whom this food [is meant]. Similarly, seeing this manifest and unmanifest, we establish: that supreme Self, <s>Puruṣa</s>, exists — for whom, as experiencer, this manifest and unmanifest is the object of experience. And for this reason: because of the activity directed toward <s>kaivalya</s>. The state of being alone (<s>kevala</s>) is <s>kaivalya</s>, meaning liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). That activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> which is directed toward <s>kaivalya</s> — it is the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> for the sake of <s>kaivalya</s>.

children.text: atrāha --- gṛhṇīmas tāvad ebhiḥ pañcabhir adhītair hetubhiḥ śarīravyatirikto 'sau puruṣo 'stīti | sa kiṃ sarvaśarīreṣv ekaḥ puruṣa āhosvit pratiśarīraṃ bhinnaḥ puruṣa iti | kutaḥ saṃśaya iti cec codaka ācāryavipratipatteḥ saṃśayaḥ | iha kecid ācāryā bhedavādina iti manyante --- eko 'yaṃ puruṣaḥ sarvaśarīreṣūpalabhyate maṇisūtravat | iha rasanāyāṃ yāvanto maṇayas teṣu sarveṣv ekam eva sūtraṃ pravartate | evaṃ maṇibhūteṣu śarīreṣu kim ekaḥ sūtrabhūtaḥ paramātmā | āhosvij jalacandravat puruṣa iti eka eva bahuṣu nadīkūpataḍāgādiṣv ivopalabhyate iti | ataḥ saṃśayaḥ kim ekaḥ puruṣo guṇasūtranyāyena āhosvid bahavaḥ puruṣāḥ | atrocyate --- bahavaḥ puruṣāḥ katham iti cet tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Here an objection arises: We accept, by these five reasons thus studied, that <s>Puruṣa</s> exists as distinct from the body. But is there one single <s>Puruṣa</s> in all bodies, or is there a separate <s>Puruṣa</s> for each body? If you ask whence the doubt — the doubt arises from the disagreement among teachers. Here, some teachers who are proponents of difference hold: this <s>Puruṣa</s> is one, found in all bodies, like a thread through beads. Just as on a string, however many beads there are, a single thread runs through them all — so too, in the bodies that are like beads, is there one <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) like a thread? Or is the <s>Puruṣa</s> like the reflection of the moon in water — one alone, yet appearing in many rivers, wells, ponds, and the like? Hence the doubt: is <s>Puruṣa</s> one, by the analogy of a string of beads, or are there many <s>Puruṣas</s>? To this it is replied: There are many <s>Puruṣas</s>. How? That is stated:

children.text: janmamaraṇakaraṇānāṃ pratiniyamād ayugapatpravṛtteś ca /
children.translated_text: Because of the specific allotment of birth, death, and the sense faculties, because of the non-simultaneous activity [of different individuals],

children.text: puruṣabahutvaṃ siddhaṃ traiguṇyaviparyayāc caiva // ISk_18 //
children.translated_text: And because of the opposite of the three <s>guṇas</s> — the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> is established.

children.text: janmamaraṇakaraṇānām iti | janmaniyamād iha kecin nīcajanmānaḥ, kecin madhyamajanmānaḥ, kecid utkṛṣṭajanmānaḥ | yadi punar ekaḥ puruṣaḥ syāt sa eva nīcakulotpannaḥ syāt sa eva utkṛṣṭakulotpannaḥ syāt | kasmāt? puruṣaikatvāt | asti cāyaṃ niyamaḥ, anye 'dhamā anya utkṛṣṭāḥ | tasmād bahavaḥ puruṣāḥ | ataś ca --- maraṇaniyamāt | maraṇe 'pi niyamo dṛṣṭo mama bhrātā mṛto mama pitā ca | tasmād bahavaḥ puruṣāḥ | apare punar itthaṅkāraṃ varṇayanti --- janmamaraṇaniyamāt | iha kaścit kadācin mriyate tadaiva paro jāyate | yady ekaḥ puruṣaḥ syāt tarhi ekasmin jāyamāne sarve 'pi jāyeran | na caivam | mriyamāṇe sarve mriyeran | na caivam | tasmād bahavaḥ puruṣāḥ | itaś ca paśyāmaḥ | karaṇaniyamāt | karaṇānīndriyāṇi śrotrādīni | iha loke kecid badhirāndhamūkādayaḥ | itare ca paṭutarakaraṇāḥ | ataḥ paśyāmo ya upahatendriyās te anye, ye cānupahatendriyās te cānye | tasmāt pratiniyatakaraṇatvād api paśyāmo 'neke puruṣā iti | itaś ca paśyāmaḥ | traiguṇyaviparyayāc caiva | caḥ samuccaye | pūrvoktair hetubhiḥ | asmāc ca hetor ity arthaḥ | ihaikasya brāhmaṇasya trayaḥ putrāḥ sabrahmacāriṇa ekenaiva ekasyāṃ bhāryāyāṃ jātāḥ | tatraikaḥ sāttviko medhāvī śuciḥ sukhī |(p.23) dvitīyo rājaso durmedhāvī duḥkhī | tṛtīyas tāmaso mūḍho nāstikaḥ | yady eke ātmā syād ekasmin sāttvike rājase tāmase vā sarve tathā syuḥ | na tathā bhavanti | ataḥ paśyāmo 'neke puruṣāḥ // SkMv_18 //
children.translated_text: 'Of birth, death, and the sense faculties': From the regularity of birth — in this world some are of low birth, some of middling birth, some of exalted birth. If there were only one <s>Puruṣa</s>, that same one would be born in a low family and that same one in an exalted family. Why? Because of the oneness of <s>Puruṣa</s>. But there is this regularity: some are inferior, others are exalted. Therefore there are many <s>Puruṣas</s>. And also: from the regularity of death — a regularity in death is also observed: 'my brother has died, and my father too.' Therefore there are many <s>Puruṣas</s>. Others, however, describe it thus: from the regularity of birth and death — here someone dies at a certain time, and at that very time another is born. If there were one <s>Puruṣa</s>, then when one is being born, all would be born — but this is not so. When one is dying, all would die — but this is not so. Therefore there are many <s>Puruṣas</s>. And furthermore, we observe: from the regularity of the sense faculties (<s>karaṇas</s>). The <s>karaṇas</s> are the <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties) such as hearing and so forth. In this world, some are deaf, blind, mute, and the like, while others have keener sense faculties. Hence we observe: those with impaired sense faculties are some, and those with unimpaired sense faculties are others. Therefore, from the fact that sense faculties are individually determined, we observe that there are many <s>Puruṣas</s>. And furthermore, we observe: 'And also from the reversal of the three <s>guṇas</s>.' The word 'and' is for conjunction — together with the previously stated reasons, and also from this reason — that is the meaning. Here, a single <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has three sons, fellow students, born from the same father and the same wife. Among them, one is <s>sāttvika</s> — intelligent, pure, and happy; the second is <s>rājasa</s> — dull-witted and suffering; the third is <s>tāmasa</s> — deluded and atheistic. If there were one <s>Ātman</s>, then if one were <s>sāttvika</s>, <s>rājasa</s>, or <s>tāmasa</s>, all would be likewise. But they are not so. Hence we observe that there are many <s>Puruṣas</s>. [SkMv 18]

children.text: atrāha --- ayaṃ saṃśayaḥ | kiṃ khalu kartā puruṣo 'sty āhosvid akarteti | kutaḥ saṃśaya iti cet, ācāryavipratipatteḥ | loke tāvat puruṣo gacchati dhāvati tiṣṭhati śocati, puruṣeṇedaṃ kṛtam iti vipratipattiḥ | evam ācāryā vedavādino bruvate | vaiśeṣikā api kartā iti mataṃ pratipannāḥ | ataḥ saṃśayaḥ | atrocyate --- akartā puruṣaḥ | katham iti cet tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks: this is the doubt — is <s>Puruṣa</s> indeed an agent (<s>kartṛ</s>) or a non-agent (<s>akartṛ</s>)? If one asks whence the doubt, [the answer is:] from the disagreement among teachers. In the world, indeed, '<s>Puruṣa</s> goes, runs, stands, grieves'; 'this was done by <s>Puruṣa</s>' — thus is the disagreement. Similarly, the teachers who are <s>Veda</s>-advocates say so. The <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> too have accepted the view that [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is an agent. Hence the doubt. To this it is said: <s>Puruṣa</s> is a non-agent. How so? That is stated:

children.text: tasmāc ca viparyāsāt siddhaṃ sākṣitvam asya puruṣasya /
children.translated_text: 'And therefore, from the reversal [of the properties of <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s>], the witnessing nature of this <s>Puruṣa</s> is established,

children.text: kaivalyaṃ mādhyasthyaṃ draṣṭṛtvam akartṛbhāvaś ca // ISk_19 //
children.translated_text: along with isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>), neutrality (<s>mādhyasthya</s>), the nature of being a seer (<s>draṣṭṛtva</s>), and non-agency (<s>akartṛbhāva</s>).' [ISk 19]

children.text: tasmāc ca viparyāsād iti | kartṛkāraṇānāṃ ko viśeṣaḥ atrocyate | tad yathā kaścid yamaniyamarataḥ sāṅkhyayogācāryarato bhikṣur nagare prativasati | sa ca janādiṣu prativarṇāśramavihitāsu kriyāsu pravartamānānāṃ tannagaravāsināṃ sākṣimātro bhavati | ṛtuvaśāt śītoṣṇādīn āyātān anubhavati | tadvad ayaṃ nānāvasthe guṇavimarde vartamāno vaidharmyāt kṣetrajñaḥ sākṣimātraḥ syāt | evaṃ sākṣitvaṃ siddham asya puruṣasya | kevalabhāvaḥ kaivalyaṃ nāma tribhyo guṇebhyo 'nyatvam | yathāsau bhikṣuḥ kadācin nāgarāṇāṃ vivadatāṃ vaktā bhavati tvayā sādhukṛtam iti tvayāsādhv iti | kim evaṃ puruṣo bhavati | atrocyate --- mādhyasthyam | nāsya kenacit kṛtyam asti | udāsīno hy ayam | atrāha --- yady akartā tat kiṃ parakṛtānāṃ prayoktā | atrocyate --- kartṛbhāvaś ca dvividho hi, prayoktā kartā ca | atrodāsīnasya puruṣasya kartṛtvaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ guṇalakṣaṇena // SkMv_19 //
children.translated_text: 'And therefore, from the reversal': What is the distinction between an agent and an instrument? To this it is said: Just as a certain mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>), devoted to restraint and observances, devoted to the teaching of <s>Sāṃkhya-Yoga</s>, dwells in a city. And with regard to the inhabitants of that city who are engaged in the activities prescribed for each <s>varṇa</s> (social class) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life) — births and the like — he is merely a witness. Due to the seasons, he experiences the arrival of cold, heat, and the like. Similarly, this <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), while being present in the various states and the conflict of the <s>guṇas</s>, is merely a witness because of his different nature. Thus the witnessing nature of this <s>Puruṣa</s> is established. 'The state of being alone' (<s>kevalabhāva</s>) is called '<s>kaivalya</s>' (isolation) — otherness from the three <s>guṇas</s>. Just as that mendicant sometimes, when the townspeople are disputing, becomes a speaker [saying] 'you have acted well' or 'you have acted badly.' Does <s>Puruṣa</s> likewise become [an agent]? To this it is said: neutrality (<s>mādhyasthya</s>) — he has nothing to do with anyone; he is indifferent. Here one asks: if he is a non-agent, then is he the director of what is done by others? To this it is said: 'And non-agency (<s>akartṛbhāva</s>)' — agency is of two kinds: the director and the doer. Here, the agency of the indifferent <s>Puruṣa</s> is denied by the characteristic of the <s>guṇas</s>. [SkMv 19]

children.text: atrāha --- yady akartā puruṣaḥ adhyavasāyaṃ tarhi kiṃ karoti dharmaṃ kariṣyāmy adharmaṃ ceti | yadi guṇā adhyavasāyaṃ kurvanti tarhi teṣāṃ sacetanatvaṃ(p.24) syāt | amīṣāṃ cācetanatvam eva prāg upanyastam | atha puruṣo 'dhyavasāyaṃ kurute tadā tasya kartṛtvaprasaṅgaḥ | tasmād ubhayathāpi doṣa iti | atra samādhīyate nāyaṃ doṣaḥ | katham iti cet, tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks: if <s>Puruṣa</s> is a non-agent, then what makes the determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>): 'I shall do <s>dharma</s>, I shall do <s>adharma</s>'? If the <s>guṇas</s> make the determination, then they would be conscious — but their unconsciousness was previously established. If <s>Puruṣa</s> makes the determination, then the fault of agency would apply to him. Therefore, either way there is a fault. Here the resolution is given: this is not a fault. How so? That is stated:

children.text: tasmāt tatsaṃyogād acetanaṃ cetanāvad iva liṅgam /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, from that conjunction, the unconscious <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) [appears] as if conscious;

children.text: guṇakartṛtve 'pi tathā karteva bhavaty udāsīnaḥ // ISk_20 //
children.translated_text: and even though the <s>guṇas</s> are the agents, the indifferent one (<s>Puruṣa</s>) appears as if he were the agent.' [ISk 20]

children.text: yasmāc cetanasvabhāvaḥ puruṣaḥ, tasmāt tatsaṃyogād acetanaṃ mahadādi liṅgam adhyavasāyābhimānasaṅkalpālocanādiṣu vṛttiṣu cetanāvat pravartate | ko dṛṣṭāntaḥ --- tad yathā anuṣṇāśīto ghaṭaḥ śītābhir adbhiḥ saṃspṛṣṭaḥ śīto bhavati | agninā saṃyukta uṣṇo bhavati | evaṃ mahadādi liṅgam acetanam api bhūtvā cetanāvad bhavati | tasmād adhyavasāyaṃ kurvanti guṇāḥ kāryādiṣu | yad apy uktam --- lokopacārāt kartā puruṣa iti | atra brūmaḥ --- guṇakartṛtve 'pi tathā karteva bhavaty udāsīnaḥ | atra dṛṣṭāntaś ca | kecit kila caurā grāmaṃ hṛtvā dravyaṃ gṛhītvā grāmāntaraṃ gacchanti kṛtakāryāḥ | taiḥ saha sārthena śrotriyo brāhmaṇaḥ panthānaṃ gacchati | tatpadānusāribhir ārakṣibhis te gṛhītāḥ | kṛtāparādhais taiḥ saha so 'pi brāhmaṇo gṛhītas tvam api caura iti | tad yathāsāv acauras tatsaṃsargadoṣeṇa cauratayā pratītas taiḥ | tathā sattvādayo guṇāḥ kartāras taiḥ saṃyuktaḥ puruṣo 'pi akartāpi kartā bhavati | kartṛsaṃsargāt karteva | paraṃ paramārthatayā akartā puruṣaḥ // SkMv_20 //
children.translated_text: Since <s>Puruṣa</s> is of the nature of consciousness, therefore from that conjunction, the unconscious <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) — <s>Mahat</s> and the rest — operates as if conscious in activities such as determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), self-assertion (<s>abhimāna</s>), volition (<s>saṅkalpa</s>), apprehension (<s>ālocana</s>), and the like. What is the illustration? Just as a pot, which is neither hot nor cold, when brought into contact with cold water becomes cold, and when conjoined with fire becomes hot — similarly, the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), <s>Mahat</s> and the rest, though unconscious, becomes as if conscious. Therefore the <s>guṇas</s> make the determination regarding effects and the like. As for what was said — 'from worldly usage, <s>Puruṣa</s> is the agent' — to that we say: 'Even though the <s>guṇas</s> are the agents, the indifferent one appears as if the agent.' Here there is also an illustration: some thieves, having robbed a village and taken the goods, proceed to another village, their purpose accomplished. Traveling in the same caravan with them, a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>śrotriya</s>) goes along the road. Followed by the police tracking their footsteps, they are caught. Together with those criminals, that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> too is seized — 'you are also a thief!' Just as that innocent man is perceived as a thief due to the fault of association with them, so <s>Sattva</s> and the other <s>guṇas</s> are the agents, and <s>Puruṣa</s>, though conjoined with them, though a non-agent, becomes [perceived as] an agent — as if an agent due to association with agents. But ultimately, <s>Puruṣa</s> is a non-agent. [SkMv 20]

children.text: atrāha --- tasmāt tatsaṃyogāt iti pradhānapuruṣasaṃyoga iti cet, saṃyogaḥ kaḥ | anekavidho hi saṃyogaḥ | anyatarakarmajo yathā sthāṇuśyenayoḥ, sampātajo dvayor vā saṃyogo yathā dvyaṅgulākāśayoḥ, svābhāviko yathāgnyuṣṇayoḥ, śaktihetuko yathā matsyodakayoḥ, yādṛcchikaḥ suparnayor vākasmikaḥ | ataḥ saṃśayaḥ | atrocyate --- anyatarakarmajasaṃyogaś ca saṃyogo naiva pradhānapuruṣayor vibhutvāniṣkriyatvāt | nāsti svābhāviko 'pi | tayor nityatvān mokṣābhāvaḥ syād aviyogatvāt | evam eva viṣayahetuke śaktihetukatve ca | atrāha --- kas tarhi pradhānapuruṣayoḥ saṃyoga iti | atrocyate | arthahetukaḥ | kaś cāsāv artha ity atrāha ---(p.25)
children.translated_text: Here one asks: 'From that conjunction' — if you mean the conjunction of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, what kind of conjunction is it? For conjunction is of many kinds: produced by the action of one party, as with a post and a hawk; produced by collision, or the conjunction of two [things], as with two fingers and space; natural, as with fire and heat; caused by capacity, as with a fish and water; accidental, as with two birds, or chance. Hence the doubt. To this it is said: the conjunction produced by the action of one party does not apply to <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, since both are all-pervading and inactive. Nor is there a natural conjunction — since both are eternal, there would be no liberation, because they would never separate. Likewise in the case of conjunction caused by a sense object or by capacity. Here one asks: then what is the conjunction of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>? To this it is said: it is caused by purpose (<s>artha</s>). And what is that purpose? To this he says:

children.text: puruṣasya darśanārthaṃ kaivalyārthaṃ tathā pradhānasya /
children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s seeing (<s>darśana</s>), and likewise for the purpose of <s>Pradhāna</s>'s isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>),

children.text: paṅgvandhavad ubhayor api saṃyogas tatkṛtaḥ sargaḥ // ISk_21 //
children.translated_text: the conjunction of the two is like that of the lame and the blind; from that, creation (<s>sarga</s>) is produced.' [ISk 21]

children.text: puruṣasya tāvad darśanārthaṃ saṃyogaḥ | puruṣaḥ pradhānena saha saṃyujyate suguṇāṃ prakṛtiṃ drakṣyāmy ayam arthaḥ | kaivalyārthaṃ tathā pradhānasya saṃyogaḥ | asya tapasvinaḥ puruṣasya jñāne vartamānasya kaivalyaṃ kariṣyāmīti | kaivalyaṃ mokṣa ity arthaḥ | yathā rājā puruṣeṇa saṃyujyate praiṣaṇaṃ me kariṣyatīti | puruṣo 'pi rājñā saṃyujyate vṛttiṃ me dāsyatīti | evaṃ tāvad rājapuruṣayor arthahetukaḥ sambandhaḥ | tathā pradhānapuruṣayor apy arthahetukaḥ sambandhaḥ saṃyogaḥ | kiṃ cānyat | paṅgvandhavad ubhayor api saṃyoga iti | api cātra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | yathā kila kaścid andhaḥ sārthena samaṃ pāṭaliputraṃ prasthitaḥ sa ca sārthaś caurair abhihataḥ | andho 'pi avaśeṣajīvitaḥ kṛcchreṇa mahatā nirjagāma | sa ca sarvasvajanavirahita itaś cetaś ca paribhrāmyan panthānam apaśyan samantāc caṅkramamāṇaḥ kenacid vanamadhyasthena paṅgunā dṛṣṭaḥ proktaś ca | bho bho andha mā bhaiṣīr ahaṃ paṅgur mārgadarśane kuśalī gantum asamarthaḥ | andhena prativacanaṃ proktam --- bhoḥ paṅgo yathā bhavān gamanāśaktas tathāham api na śaknomi draṣṭuṃ, gantuṃ mama sāmarthyam asti | tava darśanasāmarthyenāhaṃ bhavantaṃ skandhenādāya gacchāmy evam ubhayor duḥkhaparihāralakṣaṇā kāryasiddhir astu | evaṃ tayor yathā svārthalabdhihetukaḥ sambandhaḥ saṃyogas tulyaḥ | tadvat | paṅgvandhavat pradhānapuruṣau draṣṭavyau | paṅguvat puruṣo draṣṭavyaḥ | andhavat pradhānam | puruṣasya dṛkśaktiḥ | pradhānasya kriyāsāmarthyam | evaṃ pradhānam api puruṣasya mokṣaṃ kṛtvā nivartate | puruṣaḥ pradhānaṃ dṛṣṭvā mokṣaṃ gacchati | kiṃ cānyat --- tatkṛtaḥ sargaḥ | tacchabdena pradhānapuruṣau sambadhyete | tābhyāṃ pradhānapuruṣābhyāṃ kṛtas tatkṛtaḥ sargaḥ | tad yathā --- strīpuruṣasaṃyogāt putraḥ sambhavati | evaṃ pradhānapuruṣasaṃyogāt sargotpattir bhavati | sargaśabdena mahadādiliṅgotpattir iti bruvate // SkMv_21 //
children.translated_text: The conjunction [of <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s>] is for the purpose of seeing, with respect to <s>Puruṣa</s>. <s>Puruṣa</s> conjoins with <s>Pradhāna</s> [thinking]: 'I shall see this excellent <s>Prakṛti</s>' — this is the meaning. Likewise, the conjunction is for the purpose of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation) with respect to <s>Pradhāna</s> — [<s>Prakṛti</s> thinks]: 'I shall bring about <s>kaivalya</s> for this suffering <s>Puruṣa</s> who abides in knowledge.' <s>Kaivalya</s> means liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>)...

children.text: tām utpattiṃ brūmaḥ ---
children.translated_text: We now state that origination —

children.text: prakṛter mahāṃs tato 'haṅkāras tasmād gaṇaś ca ṣoḍaśakaḥ /
children.translated_text: From <s>Prakṛti</s> [arises] <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle); from that, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense); from that, the group of sixteen;

children.text: tasmād api ṣoḍaśakāt pañcabhyaḥ pañca bhūtāni // ISk_22 //
children.translated_text: And from five of those sixteen, the five gross elements (<s>bhūtas</s>). (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 22)

children.text: prakṛtiḥ pradhānam adhikurute | brahma avyaktaṃ bahudhātmakaṃ māyeti paryāyāḥ | tasyāḥ prakṛter mahān utpadyate prathamaḥ kaścit | mahān, buddhiḥ, matiḥ, prajñā, saṃvittiḥ, khyātiḥ, citiḥ, smṛtir āsurī hariḥ, haraḥ, hiraṇyagarbha iti paryāyāḥ | tato 'haṅkāraḥ | tasmān mahato 'haṅkāra utpadyate | tasya ime paryāyāḥ --- vaikṛtas taijaso bhūtādir abhimāno 'smitā iti | catuḥṣaṣṭivarṇaiḥ parādivaikharīparyantābhidheyair yat kim apy abhidhīyate buddhyā samarthya tatsakalamādyantākārahakāravarṇadvayagrahaṇenoparisthitapiṇḍīkṛtānukāriṇā bindunā bhūṣitaḥ pratyāhāranyāyenāhaṅkāra ity abhidhīyate | tasmāt ahaṅkārāt ṣoḍaśako gaṇa utpadyate | tāmasād bhūtādināmnaḥ pañcatanmātrāṇi śabdādīni | ata eva tāni mūḍhāni | sāttvikād vaikṛtābhidhānād buddhikarmātmakāni manaḥsahitāni ekādaśendriyāṇi | ata eva tāni kiñcij jānanti | rājasāt taijasābhidhānād ubhayam | mūḍhatvād dhi tamaḥ | prakāśatvāt sattvam | ubhayaguṇayogāt ṣoḍaśako gaṇo 'haṅkārād utpadyate | tasmād api ṣoḍaśakāt madhye yāni pañca śabdāditanmātrāṇi tebhyaḥ pañca bhūtāny ākāśādīni | tatra śabdatanmātrād ākāśam, sparśatanmātrād vāyuḥ, rūpatanmātrāt tejaḥ, rasatanmātrād āpaḥ, gandhatanmātrāt pṛthivī ityādikrameṇa pūrvapūrvānupraveśenaikadvitricatuṣpañcaguṇāny ākāśādipṛthvīparyantāni mahābhūtānīti sṛṣṭikramaḥ | ata eva bhūtānām utpattilayāvabodhanāt bha iti | āgatigatiparijñānāt ga iti | vidan yogī iti va(va iti?) | anati calatīti an | sakalavarṇasampradāyād bhagavān ity abhimānasiddhiḥ | "apy akṣaravarṇasāmānyān(p.27) nirbrūyān na saṃskāram ādriyeta"(nirukti 2 |4) iti nairuktaśrutiprāmāṇyāt | uktaṃ ca ---
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> is the principal term, referring to <s>Pradhāna</s>. <s>Brahman</s>, the unmanifest, the manifold-natured, <s>Māyā</s> — these are synonyms. From that <s>Prakṛti</s>, there arises first a certain [principle called] <s>Mahat</s>. <s>Mahat</s>, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>mati</s> (thought), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>saṃvitti</s> (cognition), <s>khyāti</s> (discernment), <s>citi</s> (consciousness), <s>smṛti</s> (memory), <s>Āsurī</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — these are synonyms. From that...

children.text: "utpattiṃ pralayaṃ caiva bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim /
children.translated_text: 'The origination and dissolution, the coming and going of beings,

children.text: vetti vidyām avidyāṃ ca sa vācyo bhagavān iti" //
children.translated_text: Knowledge and ignorance — one who knows these is to be called the Blessed One.'

children.text:
śrīviṣṇupurāṇe ṣaṣṭhe 'ṃśe(5 |78) parāśaravacaḥ |
yad uktam ---
vyaktāvyaktajña vijñānān mokṣaḥ prāpyata iti | tatra mahadādibhūtaparyantam ity etad vyaktaṃ vyākhyātam | avyaktam api "bhedānāṃ parimāṇāt"(sāṅkhyakārikā 15) ityādibhiḥ pañcabhir hetubhir vyākhyātam | yad uktam ---
children.translated_text: These are the words of <s>Parāśara</s> in the sixth section of the <s>Śrīviṣṇupurāṇa</s> (5.78). As stated: 'Liberation is attained through knowledge of the manifest and the unmanifest.' There, that which extends from <s>Mahat</s> up to and including the elements — this has been explained as the manifest. And the unmanifest has been established through five reasons, beginning with 'because of the finite measure of the differentiated...' (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 15)...

children.text: "pañcaviṃśatitattvajño yatra tatrāśrame rataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One who knows the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles), delighting in whatever <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life),

children.text: jaṭī muṇḍī śikhī vāpi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ" // SkMv_22 //
children.translated_text: Whether with matted locks, shaven head, or topknot — is liberated; there is no doubt about this.'

children.text: atrāha --- prakṛter mahān ity uktam | tasya mahataḥ kiṃ lakṣaṇam ity atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here a question is raised: it has been stated 'From <s>Prakṛti</s> [arises] <s>Mahat</s>.' What then is the characteristic of that <s>Mahat</s>? This is answered —

children.text: adhyavasāyo buddhir dharmo jñānaṃ virāga aiśvaryam /
children.translated_text: Determination is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect); <s>dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, and sovereignty —

children.text: sāttvikam etad rūpaṃ tāmasam asmād viparyastam // ISk_23 //
children.translated_text: These are its <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) form; its <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) form is the opposite of these. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 23)

children.text: adhyavasāyo buddhir iti | adhyavasāyo niścayaḥ pratipattiḥ ayaṃ sthāṇur ayaṃ puruṣa iti buddher lakṣaṇam | sā ca buddhir aṣṭāṅgā | sāttvikatāmasarūpabhedāt | tatra buddheḥ sāttvikaṃ rūpaṃ caturvidhaṃ bhavati dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyam aiśvaryam iti | tatra dharmo nāma varṇinām āśramiṇāṃ ca samayāvirodhena yaḥ prokto yamaniyamalakṣaṇaḥ sa dharmaḥ | tatra pañca yamāḥ pañca niyamāḥ | "ahiṃsāsatyāsteyabrahmacaryāparigrahā yamāḥ"(pātañjalayogasūtra 2 |30) | "śaucasantoṣatapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni niyamāḥ"(pātañjalayogasūtra 2 |32) | ebhir yamaniyamair yaḥ sādhyate sa dharmaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Determination is <s>buddhi</s>' — determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), i.e. ascertainment, conviction — 'this is a post, this is a person' — this is the characteristic of <s>buddhi</s>. And that <s>buddhi</s> has eight aspects, due to the division into <s>sāttvika</s> and <s>tāmasa</s> forms. Of these, the <s>sāttvika</s> form of <s>buddhi</s> is fourfold: <s>dharma</s>, knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), and sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>)...

children.text: dhāraṇārtho dhṛñ ity eṣa dhātuḥ śābdaiḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The root <s>dhṛ</s> has the meaning of 'holding' — thus it is declared by grammarians;

children.text: durgatiprapatatprāṇidhāraṇād dharma ucyate //
children.translated_text: Because it holds beings [who are] falling into misfortune, it is called <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: tatra yā sthāvarajaṅgamānāṃ bhūtānāṃ vāṅmanaḥkāyakarmabhir adrohatā sā ahiṃsā | tathā yad bhūtahitam atyantaṃ dṛṣṭaśrutānumitivijñāteṣv artheṣu yathāntaḥkaraṇapratyayopasthitaṃ tathaiva indriyāṇi avilupya vañcanābhrāntipratipattibandhyatāvirahitavāguccāraṇaṃ(p.28) tat satyam | tathā yat sambhrameṣv anyeṣu vātyantikeṣu prayojaneṣu sve sve sthāne samatvād grahaṇasyoparamas tad asteyam | tathā strīpuruṣasaṃyoge parasparaliṅgasaṃyoge śabdasparśarasarūpagandheṣu yaḥ saṅgavyudāsaḥ śrotādyuparatiḥ asaṅkalpaś ca manasa uparatiḥ so 'ṣṭāṅgaṃ brahmacaryam | evaṃ hy āhuḥ saṃyogaśabdasparśarasarūpagandhasaṅkalpasmṛtidharmaphalatyāgādyaṣṭāṅgaṃ brahmacaryam iti | anyac ca | brahmabījaṃ retas tac carati na muñcatīti brahmacārī | brahma vedaṃ vā guruṇā pradattaṃ caratīti | brahmā svayambhūs tasyāyaṃ daṇḍakamaṇḍaludhāraṇādirūpa ākāro brahmavac caratīti vā | evam arjanakrayavikrayādikalpanābhedānām anupādānaṃ sarvathā sarvasyāsvīkaraṇam aparigrahaḥ | iti pañca yamāḥ | yaś cendriyāṇām antaḥkaraṇoparamas tac chaucaṃ bāhyaṃ mṛjjalādinā |
children.translated_text: There, non-injury (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) is the absence of hostility in speech, mind, and bodily action toward all beings, both stationary and mobile. Likewise, truthfulness (<s>satya</s>) is what is beneficial to beings — with respect to objects known through perception, testimony, and inference, as presented to the inner instrument of cognition — speaking accordingly without distortion of the senses, free from deception, error, groundless conviction, and barrenness of speech...

children.text: "abhakṣyaparihāras tu saṃsargaś cāpy acintitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The avoidance of forbidden foods, association only with the blameless,

children.text: svadharme ca vyavasthānaṃ śaucam etat prakīrtitam" //
children.translated_text: And being established in one's own <s>dharma</s> — this is declared to be purity (<s>śauca</s>).'

children.text: tathā yad bhaikṣārjitena haviṣā prāṇayātrā | ādhyātmikasyāgner mantragṛhītena homaḥ kartavyaḥ | ahany ahani yajñaśeṣāśanārtham etad āhāralāghavaṃ santoṣaḥ | "sa yāṃ prathamām āhutiṃ juhuyāt prāṇāya svāhā"(chāndogyopaniṣad 5 |19 |1) ity ārabhya "sa ya idam avidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti yathāṅgārān apohya bhasmani hutaṃ(juhuyāt?) tādṛk tat syāt" (chāndogyopaniṣad 5 |24 |1) iti śruteḥ | tapaḥ kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādi śarīraśoṣaṇarūpam |
children.translated_text: Likewise, sustaining one's life with food obtained by begging. The <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) should be performed with the fire of the inner Self (<s>ādhyātmika agni</s>) using oblation consecrated by <s>mantras</s>. Day after day, eating the remnants of the sacrifice — this lightness of diet is contentment (<s>santoṣa</s>). [As the <s>Śruti</s> says:] 'That first oblation which he should offer — to <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>' (<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.19.1), up to 'One who, not knowing this, offers the <s>agnihotra</s> — that would be like pushing aside the embers and making an offering in ashes' (<s>Chāndogyopaniṣad</s> 5.24.1). <s>Tapas</s> (austerity) is in the form of bodily mortification such as <s>kṛcchra</s> and <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> [fasts].

children.text: "viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ |" (bhagavadgītā 2 |59)
children.translated_text: 'The sense-objects withdraw from the embodied one who abstains from food.' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 2.59)

children.text: iti smaraṇāt | nātapasvino yogaḥ siddhyati | anādivāsanāvicitrā pratyupasthitaviṣayajālā cāśuddhir nāntareṇa tapaḥ sambhedam āpadyata iti tapasa upādānam | tac ca cittaprasādanam abādhamānam āsevyam iti manyante | svādhyāyaḥ praṇavādipavitrāṇāṃ japaḥ | īśvarapraṇidhānaṃ kriyāṇāṃ paramagurāv arpaṇaṃ tatphalasaṃnyāso vā | "brahmārpaṇaṃ brahmahaviḥ(bhagavadgītā 4 |24)" iti, "anāśritaḥ karmaphalam(bhagavadgītā 6 |1)" iti śravaṇāt | ity amīṣāṃ yamaniyamādīnāṃ sevanāt "ahiṃsāpratiṣṭhāyāṃ tatsannidhau vairatyāgaḥ"(pātañjalayogasūtra 2 |35) ityādyāḥ siddhayaḥ | vaiparītye tu "vitarkabādhane pratipakṣabhāvanam"(pātañjalayogasūtra 2 |33), "vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam"(pātañjalayogasūtra 2 |34)(p.29) evaṃ ca vartamānasya yoginaḥ "sthānyupanimantraṇe saṅgasmayākaraṇaṃ punar aniṣṭaprasaṅgāt"(pātañjalayogasūtra 3 |51) iti bhikṣor ete yamaniyamāḥ | ebhir yamaniyamair vā sādhyate sa dharmo vyākhyātaḥ | adhunā jñānam āha --- jñānaṃ dvividham | bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ ca | tatra bāhyam --- vīṇāpaṇavagandharvacitrakathāgaṇitavyākaraṇaśāstrāṇi | ābhyantaram --- guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhilakṣaṇam | anye guṇāḥ sattvarajastamāṃsi anyaḥ puruṣa iti | bāhyena jñānena lokopapattir ābhyantareṇa mokṣa iti | etat jñānaṃ viṣayoparamāt | vairāgyam āha --- arjanarakṣaṇakṣayātṛptihiṃsādidoṣān dṛṣṭvā yo viṣayebhyo viraktas tasya mokṣo nāstīti | ābhyantareṇa jñānapūrvakeṇa vairāgyeṇa mokṣo bhavati bāhyena saṃsāra iti | aiśvaryaṃ īśvarabhāvenety aṣṭavidham | aṇimā laghimā garimā mahimā prāptiḥ prākāmyam īśitvaṃ vaśitvaṃ yatrakāmāvasāyitvam iti | etāni dharmādīni catvāri sāttvikarūpāṇi buddheḥ | yadā sattvena rajastamasī abhibhūte stas tadā sattvodriktaḥ pumān etān guṇān āpnoti | kiṃ cānyat | tāmasam asmāt viparyastam | asmāt sāttvikād dharmāder viparyastaṃ viparītam adharmājñānādyaṃ caturdhā buddhe rūpaṃ tāmasam | ye hiṃsādayo vitarkā ekāśītibhedāḥ | pṛthag daśāpi yamaniyamādyāḥ | tathā adharmo 'jñānam avairāgyam anaiśvaryam ity aṣṭadhā sāttvikatāmasabhedā buddhiḥ | asyā evam vidhāyā buddher ahaṅkāro jāyate // SkMv_23 //
children.translated_text: Thus from the <s>Smṛti</s>. <s>Yoga</s> does not succeed for one who is not an ascetic. The impurity — varied by beginningless <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) and entangled in the net of present sense-objects — does not disintegrate without <s>tapas</s> (austerity); hence the adoption of <s>tapas</s>. And it should be practiced in a way that purifies the mind without causing harm — so they hold. <s>Svādhyāya</s> (self-study) is the recitation of sacred syllables such as <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) and the like. <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s> (devotion to the Lord) is the offering of all actions to the Supreme Teacher, or the renunciation of their fruits. [As heard in scripture:] '<s>Brahman</s> is the offering, <s>Brahman</s> is the oblation' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 4.24), and 'Not depending on the fruit of action' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 6.1). Thus, from the practice of these <s>yamas</s> (restraints) and <s>niyamas</s> (observances), [arise] perfections (<s>siddhis</s>) such as: 'When established in non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), hostility ceases in one's presence' (<s>Pātañjalayogasūtra</s> 2.35), and so on. In the reverse case: 'When disturbed by wrong thoughts, one should cultivate the opposite' (<s>Pātañjalayogasūtra</s> 2.33); 'Wrong thoughts are violence and the like — whether done, caused to be done, or approved — preceded by greed, anger, or delusion — resulting in infinite pain and ignorance — thus one should cultivate the opposite' (<s>Pātañjalayogasūtra</s> 2.34). And for the <s>yogī</s> living thus: 'When invited by celestial beings, one should not feel attachment or pride, for there is the danger of the recurrence of the undesirable' (<s>Pātañjalayogasūtra</s> 3.51). These are the <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> of the renunciant (<s>bhikṣu</s>). That <s>dharma</s> which is achieved by these <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> has been explained. Now he states knowledge: Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is twofold — external and internal. Of these, the external [consists of]: the sciences of <s>vīṇā</s> (lute-playing), drum-playing, music (<s>gāndharva</s>), art of narrative (<s>citrakathā</s>), arithmetic, grammar, and [other] <s>śāstras</s>. The internal is characterized by the perception of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>: the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — are one thing; <s>Puruṣa</s> is another. Through external knowledge, worldly accomplishment [is attained]; through internal [knowledge], liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). This knowledge comes from the cessation of [attachment to] objects. He speaks of dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>): Seeing the faults of acquisition, preservation, loss, dissatisfaction, violence, and so on, one who is dispassionate toward objects — for him there is no liberation; [rather,] through internal dispassion preceded by knowledge, liberation occurs; through external [dispassion], [continued] <s>saṃsāra</s>. Sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) is the state of being the Lord — it is eightfold: <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), <s>garimā</s> (heaviness), <s>mahimā</s> (greatness), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will), <s>īśitva</s> (lordship), <s>vaśitva</s> (subjugation), and <s>yatrakāmāvasāyitva</s> (fulfillment of desire at will). These four — <s>dharma</s> and the rest — are the <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) forms of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). When <s>sattva</s> overpowers <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, then the person, predominated by <s>sattva</s>, attains these qualities. And what else? The <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) form is the opposite of this. Opposite to these <s>sāttvika</s> [forms] of <s>dharma</s> and the rest — <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), and so on — constitutes the fourfold <s>tāmasa</s> form of <s>buddhi</s>. The wrong thoughts (<s>vitarkas</s>) such as violence and the like have eighty-one divisions. Separately, the <s>yamas</s>, <s>niyamas</s>, and the rest are also ten each. Thus, <s>adharma</s>, <s>ajñāna</s>, <s>avairāgya</s> (non-dispassion), and <s>anaiśvarya</s> (non-sovereignty) — <s>buddhi</s> has an eightfold division into <s>sāttvika</s> and <s>tāmasa</s> forms. From this <s>buddhi</s> of such nature, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) is born. // <s>SkMv</s> 23 //

children.text: idānīm ahaṅkārasya lakṣaṇaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain the characteristic of <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>. This is stated:

children.text: abhimāno 'haṅkāras tasmād dvividhaḥ pravartate sargaḥ /
children.translated_text: Self-conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>) is <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego); from it proceeds a twofold creation (<s>sarga</s>):

children.text: aindriya ekādaśakas tanmātrapañcakaś caiva // ISk_24 //
children.translated_text: The group of eleven sense-organs (<s>aindriya</s>), and the set of five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). // <s>ISk</s> 24 //

children.text: abhimāno 'haṅkāra iti | rūpe aham rase aham gandhe aham, ahaṃ vidvān, ahaṃ darśanīya ityevamādy abhimāno 'haṅkāraḥ | tasmāt abhimānalakṣaṇād ahaṅkārād dvividhaḥ pravartate sargaḥ | sarga iti sṛṣṭeḥ paryāyaḥ | kaś cāsau sargaḥ? tad ucyate | aindriya ekādaśakaḥ | śrotrādīnīndriyāṇi manaḥparyantāni | tanmātrapañcakaś caiva | tanmātrāṇy atra śabdādīni gandhaparyantāni | evam ekādaśendriyāṇi pañcatanmātrāṇi cotpannāni // SkMv_24 //
children.translated_text: 'Self-conceit is <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>' — 'I am [identical with] form,' 'I am [identical with] taste,' 'I am [identical with] smell,' 'I am learned,' 'I am handsome' — such self-conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>) is <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>. From that <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, characterized by self-conceit, a twofold creation proceeds. <s>Sarga</s> (creation) is a synonym for <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (emanation). And what is that creation? This is stated: The group of eleven belonging to the senses (<s>aindriya</s>) — the sense-organs beginning with hearing (<s>śrotra</s>) up to the mind (<s>manas</s>). And the set of five <s>tanmātras</s> — the <s>tanmātras</s> here are sound (<s>śabda</s>) and the rest, up to smell (<s>gandha</s>). Thus the eleven sense-organs and the five <s>tanmātras</s> are produced. // <s>SkMv</s> 24 //

children.text: atrāha --- trividho 'haṅkāras taṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | tatra katarasmād ahaṅkārād indriyāṇy utpadyante, katarasmād vā tanmātrāṇīti | atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks: <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> is threefold — we shall explain that. Among those, from which <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> do the sense-organs arise, and from which do the <s>tanmātras</s> [arise]? This is answered:

children.text: sāttvika ekādaśakaḥ pravartate vaikṛtād ahaṅkārāt /
children.translated_text: The <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) group of eleven proceeds from the modified (<s>vaikṛta</s>) <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>;

children.text: bhūtādes tanmātraḥ sa tāmasas taijasād ubhayam // ISk_25 //
children.translated_text: From the <s>bhūtādi</s> (elemental source), the <s>tanmātras</s>; that [<s>bhūtādi</s>] is <s>tāmasa</s> (dark); from the <s>taijasa</s> (fiery), both. // <s>ISk</s> 25 //

children.text: sāttvika iti | yadā sattvam utkaṭaṃ bhavati ahaṅkāre tena ca sattvena rajastamasī abhibhūte syātāṃ tadā sāttviko 'haṅkāra ucyate | tasya sāttvikasya vaikṛtika iti pūrvācāryaiḥ saṃjñā kṛtā | sa vaikṛtiko bhūtvā ahaṅkāra ekādaśendriyāṇi utpādayati | tasmāt sāttvikānīmāni viśuddhāni svaviṣayagrahaṇasamarthāni bhavanti | tasmād ucyate --- "sāttvika ekādaśakaḥ pravartate vaikṛtād ahaṅkārāt" iti | bhūtādes tanmātrāḥ | bhūtādes tamobāhulyād gauṇībhūtasattvarajaso bhūtādināmnaḥ pūrvācāryair nirūpitād ahaṅkārāt tanmātraḥ śabdādipañcako gaṇo jāyate | abhibhūtasattvatamaso rājasāt taijasābhidhānād ahaṅkārāt pravṛttikarmaṇa ubhayaṃ prakāśātmakam ekādaśendriyakaṃ mohātmakaṃ tanmātrikaṃ cāsīd iti sambandhaḥ | taijasa eva rājase 'haṅkāre kriyāśaktir asti | sattvaṃ niṣkriyam ekāki na śaknoty utpādayitum | tamaś ca mūḍhatvād akriyam asamarthaṃ vinā rajaḥ sṛṣṭim utpādayitum | ata ubhe sattvatamasī sṛṣṭiviṣaye rajasānugṛhīte aindriyakaṃ tānmātrikaṃ ca gaṇadvayaṃ janayata iti tātparyārthaḥ // SkMv_25 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Sāttvika</s>': When <s>sattva</s> becomes predominant in <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, and by that <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are overpowered, then it is called <s>sāttvika Ahaṅkāra</s>. The earlier teachers (<s>pūrvācāryas</s>) gave it the designation <s>vaikṛtika</s> (modified). That <s>vaikṛtika Ahaṅkāra</s> produces the eleven sense-organs. Therefore, these [sense-organs] are <s>sāttvika</s> (pure), luminous, and capable of apprehending their respective objects. Hence it is said: 'The <s>sāttvika</s> group of eleven proceeds from the <s>vaikṛta Ahaṅkāra</s>.' 'From the <s>bhūtādi</s>, the <s>tanmātras</s>': From the <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> called <s>bhūtādi</s> (elemental source) — in which <s>tamas</s> predominates, with <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> becoming secondary — designated by the earlier teachers — the group of five <s>tanmātras</s> beginning with sound arises. From the <s>rājasa Ahaṅkāra</s> — in which <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s> are overpowered — called <s>taijasa</s> (fiery), the agent of activity — both proceed: the luminous group of eleven sense-organs and the obscuring group of <s>tanmātras</s>. This is the connection. In the <s>taijasa</s> (fiery), i.e. <s>rājasa</s>, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> alone is the power of action. <s>Sattva</s>, being inactive by itself alone, cannot produce. And <s>tamas</s>, being dull, is incapable of producing creation without <s>rajas</s>. Therefore, both <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>, when assisted by <s>rajas</s> in the matter of creation, generate the two groups — the sensory and the elemental — this is the intended meaning. // <s>SkMv</s> 25 //

children.text: tatra kāni buddhīndriyāṇi kāni karmendriyāṇīti? ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Now, which are the cognitive sense-organs (<s>buddhīndriya</s>) and which are the active sense-organs (<s>karmendriya</s>)? This is stated:

children.text: buddhīndriyāṇi śrotratvakcakṣūrasananāsikākhyāni /
children.translated_text: The cognitive sense-organs are called hearing (<s>śrotra</s>), touch (<s>tvac</s>), sight (<s>cakṣus</s>), taste (<s>rasana</s>), and smell (<s>nāsikā</s>);

children.text: vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthān karmendriyāṇy āhuḥ // ISk_26 //
children.translated_text: The active sense-organs, they say, are speech (<s>vāk</s>), hands (<s>pāṇi</s>), feet (<s>pāda</s>), excretory organ (<s>pāyu</s>), and generative organ (<s>upastha</s>). // <s>ISk</s> 26 //

children.text: śrotrādīni buddhīndriyāṇīti ucyante | śabdasparśarūparasagandhān buddhyanta iti buddhīndriyāṇi | indriyāṇy eva tānīndriyāṇi | in iti viṣayāṇāṃ nāma, tāninaḥ viṣayān prati dravantīti indriyāṇi | vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthān karmendriyāṇy āhuḥ | karma kurvanti kārayanti ca | karmendriyāṇāṃ vṛttiḥ | vāk vadatikarma, hastau grahaṇakarmāṇau, pādau viṣamasamanimnonnatabhūpradeśeṣu krāmataḥ, pāyur yathābhuktānnodakamalam utsṛjati, upastha ānandaṃ karoti putram utpādayatīty arthaḥ | evam etāḥ karmendriyāṇāṃ vṛttayo vyākhyātāḥ // SkMv_26 //
children.translated_text: Hearing (<s>śrotra</s>) and the rest are called cognitive sense-organs (<s>buddhīndriya</s>). They cognize (<s>buddhyante</s>) sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — hence they are cognitive sense-organs. They are sense-organs indeed — that is, <s>indriyas</s>. '<s>In</s>' is the name for sense-objects; they run (<s>dravanti</s>) toward those objects — hence they are <s>indriyas</s>. The active sense-organs, they say, are speech, hands, feet, excretory organ, and generative organ. They perform and cause action — these are the active sense-organs. The function of the active sense-organs [is as follows]: the function of speech (<s>vāk</s>) is speaking; the two hands have the function of grasping; the feet move over uneven, even, low, and elevated terrains; the excretory organ (<s>pāyu</s>) expels the waste matter of consumed food and water; the generative organ (<s>upastha</s>) produces pleasure and generates offspring — this is the meaning. Thus the functions of the active sense-organs have been explained. // <s>SkMv</s> 26 //

children.text: atrāha --- mana indriyaṃ tat kiṃ lakṣaṇam iti | atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks: The mind (<s>manas</s>) is a sense-organ — what is its characteristic? This is answered:

children.text: ubhayātmakam atra manaḥ saṅkalpakam indriyaṃ ca sādharmyāt /
children.translated_text: The mind (<s>manas</s>) is of the nature of both [cognitive and active]; it is the sense-organ of deliberation (<s>saṅkalpa</s>), and [it belongs] to both [groups] because of its similarity [to both];

children.text: guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣān nānātvaṃ grāhyabhedāc ca // ISk_27 //
children.translated_text: The diversity [of the manifest] arises from the specific modifications of the <s>guṇas</s>, and because of the differences in what is apprehended. // <s>ISk</s> 27 //

children.text: ubhayātmakam atra manaḥ | karmendriyeṣu karmendriyam, buddhīndriyeṣu buddhīndriyam | yathā devadatto gopālamadhye sthito gopālatvaṃ kurute mallamadhye sthito mallatvaṃ kurute | kasmāt? yasmād buddhīndriyāṇāṃ vṛttiṃ saṅkalpayati karmendriyāṇāṃ ca | tasmād ubhayātmakaṃ manaḥ | kiṃ cānyat | indriyaṃ ca sādharmyāt | sahadharmasya bhāvaḥ sādharmyam | yasmāt karmendriyāṇi buddhīndriyāṇi ca sāttvikād ahaṅkārād utpadyante, mano 'pi tasmād eva utpadyate | tasmād indriyaṃ manaḥ | tatra manasaḥ kā vṛttiḥ? saṅkalpo vṛttiḥ | buddhīndriyāṇāṃ śabdādayo vṛttayaḥ, karmendriyāṇāṃ vacanādayaḥ | evam ekādaśendriyāṇi saha vṛttibhir vyākhyātāni | atrāha --- ekādaśendriyāṇi kena kṛtāni puruṣeṇa īśvareṇa āhosvit svabhāveneti kuta iyam āśaṅketi cet, imāny ekādaśendriyāṇi ekādaśaviṣayagrāhakāṇi bhavanti | tatrāntaḥkaraṇapradhānabuddhyahaṅkārādyacetanam | tataś ca nūnaṃ cetanena puruṣeṇeśvareṇa vā svabhāveneti | atrocyate --- guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣān nānātvaṃ grāhyabhedāc ca | sattvādayas trayo guṇās te yathā pariṇamanti tasmād guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣād imāny ekādaśendriyāṇi nānā | tadarthāni bhinnāni | śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ pañcānāṃ, vacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandāḥ pañcānāṃ, saṅkalpaś ca manasaḥ | eteṣām eva ekādaśānām indriyāṇi grāhakāṇī bhaviṣyanti |(p.32) athaitan nānātvaṃ neśvareṇa na buddhyā nāhaṅkāreṇa na pradhānena na puruṣeṇa na svabhāvena kṛtam, guṇapariṇāmeneti | yady api uktam acetanānāṃ guṇānāṃ vṛttir ayukteti | tan na | kasmād iti cet, tad ucyate | acetanānām api pravṛttir dṛṣṭā | vakṣyati hi ---
children.translated_text: Here, <s>manas</s> (mind) is of both natures. Among the action-organs it functions as an action-organ; among the cognitive organs it functions as a cognitive organ. Just as <s>Devadatta</s>, standing among cowherds, acts as a cowherd, and standing among wrestlers, acts as a wrestler. Why? Because it conceptualizes the functions of both the cognitive organs and the action-organs...

children.text: "vatsavivṛddhinimittaṃ kṣīrasya yathā pravṛttir ajñasya /
children.translated_text: 'Just as the activity of milk, though unconscious, is for the purpose of the calf's nourishment,

children.text: puruṣasya vimokṣārthaṃ tathā pravṛttiḥ pradhānasya" //
children.translated_text: So too is the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s liberation.'

children.text: (sāṅkhyakārikā 57) iti |
children.translated_text: (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 57) — thus.

children.text: tasmād acetanā api guṇā ekādaśendriyabhāvena pariṇamanti | atrāha --- gṛhṇīmas tāvad ekādaśendriyāṇy ahaṅkārād utpannānīti | eteṣām indriyāṇāṃ yathāsthānanikṣepaḥ kena kṛtaḥ | cakṣur uccaiḥ sanniviṣṭaṃ dūrālokane samarthaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | śiraḥpradeśe śrotraṃ sanniviṣṭaṃ dūrāc śravaṇasamarthaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | tvak śarīrābhyantare bahiś ca sanniviṣṭā nānāsparśagrahaṇasamarthā bhaviṣyatīti | jihvā antarmukhaṃ sanniviṣṭā nānārasagrahaṇasamarthā bhaviṣyatīti | evaṃ nāsikā vāk | evam indriyāṇāṃ nikṣepaḥ puruṣeṇa vā kṛta īśvareṇa vā svabhāvena veti | atrocyate --- iha sāṅkhye puruṣeśvarasvabhāvā na kāraṇam | kiṃ tarhi --- asminn ahaṅkāre sthitaiḥ sattvarajastamobhis tribhir guṇair nikṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ | tasmād brūmaḥ --- "guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣān nānātvaṃ grāhyabhedāc ca" | guṇapariṇāmaviśeṣād ekādaśendriyāṇāṃ bhedaḥ | grāhyabhedāc ca | grāhyā ekādaśendriyārthās teṣāṃ bhedād apīndriyāṇāṃ bhedaḥ // SkMv_27 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even the unconscious <s>guṇas</s> evolve into the form of the eleven sense-organs. Here a question is raised: we accept that the eleven sense-organs are produced from <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>. But by whom was the placement of these organs in their respective locations made? [The reasoning is:] 'The eye, being placed high up, will be capable of seeing at a distance' — in the region of the head...

children.text: atrāha --- kā kasya vṛttiḥ? ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Here a question is raised: what is the function of each? It is answered —

children.text: rūpādiṣu pañcānām ālocanamatram iṣyate vṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: The function of the five [cognitive organs] with respect to form and the rest is considered to be mere apprehension;

children.text: vacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandās tu pañcānām // ISk_28 //
children.translated_text: Speech, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure are [the functions] of the [other] five [action-organs]. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 28)

children.text: mātraśabdo viśeṣārthaḥ | yathā bhikṣāmātraṃ labhyate nānyo viśeṣaḥ | tathā cakṣuḥ | gatārthe ālocanamātram iti | ekaikasya pratīndriyaṃ svaviṣayagrahaṇasāmarthyam eva | na hi cakṣuḥ śravaṇasamarthaṃ dānādānasamarthaṃ vā // SkMv_28 //
