children.translated_text: The word 'mere' (<s>mātra</s>) conveys a restrictive sense. Just as [when one says] 'only alms are obtained' — no other distinction [is implied]. So too with the eye: regarding its function, it is merely apprehension. Each individual organ has the capacity to grasp only its own object. For the eye is capable neither of hearing nor of giving and taking.

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ buddhyahaṅkāramanovṛttiṃ vakṣyāmaḥ | tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Hereafter we shall explain the functions of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense), and <s>manas</s> (mind). This is stated —

children.text: svālakṣaṇyā vṛttis trayasya saiṣā bhavaty asāmānyā
children.translated_text: The function of the three [internal organs] is specific to each, according to its own characteristic; it is not common.

children.text: sāmānyakaraṇavṛttiḥ prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañca // ISk_29 //
children.translated_text: The common function of the [entire] instrument [of cognition] is the five vital airs (<s>vāyu</s>) beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 29)

children.text: svālakṣaṇyeti | buddher adhyavasāya uktaḥ prāk lakṣaṇam | tasyāḥ sa evādhyavasāyo vṛttiḥ | evam abhimāno 'haṅkāralakṣaṇam | tasya vṛttir api sa eva | manasaḥ saṅkalpo lakṣaṇam | tasyāpi sa eva vṛttiḥ | yena yena lakṣaṇenāmī lakṣyante teṣāṃ sa eva vṛttiḥ | evaṃ yā buddhīndriyāṇāṃ na sā karmendriyāṇām | yā ca karmendriyāṇāṃ na sā buddhīndriyāṇām | buddhyahaṅkāramanasāṃ vṛttir abhihitā | sāpy asāmānyā | adhyavasāyābhimānasaṅkalpalakṣaṇā | saiṣā bhavaty asāmānyā asādhāraṇā evam ukte 'rthāt gamyate sāmānyāpi sādhāraṇāpi vṛttir asti | yadapekṣayāsāmānyety ucyate | evam indriyāṇām asāmānyā vṛttir ākhyātā kulastrīsaṃsthānīyā | ata ūrdhvaṃ sāmānyā vṛttir ucyate | sāmānyakaraṇavṛttiḥ prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañca | sāmānyakaraṇavṛttiḥ --- samastasyāntaḥkaraṇasyety arthaḥ | prāṇādyā vāyavaḥ pañceti prāṇāpānodānasamānavyānāḥ sarveṣām indriyāṇām sāmānyaṃ kurvanti | sa prāṇo nāma yo mukhanāsāntarago bāhye cāsya viṣaye vṛttiḥ | prāṇanāt prāṇa eṣa ity abhidhīyate | asmin prāṇe yat spandanakarma tat katamena kṛtam ity atrocyate --- trayodaśavidhena karaṇena kṛtam | yataś caivaṃ tasmāt prāṇakarma sarvasya karaṇagrāmasya vṛttiḥ sāmānyā | api cātra dṛṣṭāntaḥ --- yathā kasmiṃścid rājagṛhe pañjare śukāḥ prativasanti | tebhyo devadattena odano darśitaḥ | odanaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve pracalitāḥ | tadā pañjarakam api calitam | yat pañjarasya pracalanaṃ karma tat sarveṣām śukānāṃ sāmānyam | tadvat prāṇe yat spandanakarma tat sarveṣām indriyāṇāṃ sāmānyam | kiṃ cānyat --- apānenotsṛjati | itaś cāpakramaṇād apāna ity ucyate | apānabahulaś ca devadattaḥ sarpaṃ dṛṣṭvā apasarpati eṣo 'pānaḥ | tasminn apāne yat spandanakarma tat sarveṣām indriyāṇāṃ sāmānyā vṛttiḥ | ārohaṇād arthotkarṣe udāna ity abhidhīyate | nābhipradeśād utthitaṃ gacchati | udānavṛttiś ca devadatta ānandotkarṣaṃ mṛgayati | aham āḍhyo 'smād āḍhyataraḥ kathaṃ syām ity eṣa udānaḥ | asminn udāne yat spandanakarma tat sāmānyā vṛttiḥ sarvendriyāṇām | kiñ cānyat --- hṛdyavasthānaṃ sahabhāvaś ca tena samānaḥ | yo vāyur hṛddeśe vartate sa samānaḥ | tadbahulaś ca ekākī na ramata eṣa samānaḥ | tasmin yat spandanakarma tat sarvendriyāṇāṃ sāmānyavṛttiḥ | kiñ cānyat --- śarīravyāpitayā vyānaḥ | ānakhād ākeśāntaṃ śarīraṃ vyāpya anati calatīti vyānaḥ | vyānabahulo devadattaś ca atyantam anyena vinā ramate |(p.34) tasmin vyāne yat spandanakarma tat sarveṣām indriyāṇāṃ sāmānyavṛttiḥ | tad evaṃ sāmānyakāraṇavṛttiḥ prāṇādyā vāyavo vyākhyātāḥ // SkMv_29 //
children.translated_text: 'Specific to each' — the characteristic of <s>buddhi</s> is determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), as previously stated. That very determination is its function. Likewise, self-identification (<s>abhimāna</s>) is the characteristic of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>; its function too is that same [self-identification]. Conceptualization (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) is the characteristic of <s>manas</s>; its function too is that same [conceptualization]. The very characteristic by which each is defined — that itself is its function...

children.text: vṛttiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | tad ucyate ---
children.translated_text: We shall explain [their] function. This is stated —

children.text: yugapac catuṣṭayasya hi vṛttiḥ kramaśaś ca tasya nirdiṣṭā /
children.translated_text: The function of the four [i.e. the three internal organs plus one external organ] is indeed simultaneous, and also sequential — this is taught.

children.text: dṛṣṭe tathāpy adṛṣṭe trayasya tatpūrvikā vṛttiḥ // ISk_30 //
children.translated_text: In the case of the seen [object], so too in the case of the unseen — the function of the three [internal organs] is preceded by that [external organ]. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 30)

children.text: buddhir ahaṅkāro manaś cakṣur ity etāni catvāri yugapad rūpaṃ paśyanti, ayaṃ sthāṇur 'yaṃ puruṣa iti | evaṃ śabdaṃ sparśaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ catvāri yugapad gṛhṇanti | evam eṣā yugapac catuṣṭayasya vṛttiḥ | kiṃ cānyat | kramaśaś ca tasya nirdiṣṭā buddhyahaṅkāramanaścakṣuścatuṣṭayasya kramaśo vṛttir bhavati | dvāridvāravibhāgopadeśād hrasvakālatvād vibhāgo na śakyate vaktuṃ tato yugapad ity ucyate | yathā bālapatraśataṃ sūcyagreṇa viddham iti | tad yathā | devadattaḥ panthānaṃ gacchan sthāṇuṃ paśyati tatra tasya saṃśayo bhavati kim ayaṃ sthāṇur uta puruṣa iti | tatra sthāṇurūpaṃ paśyati śakuniṃ ca tatrasthaṃ tato 'sya buddhir bhavati sthāṇur ayam iti | ākuñcanaprasāraṇe karoti tato 'pi puruṣo 'yam iti pratītiḥ | evaṃ buddhyahaṅkāramanaścakṣuṣāṃ kramaśo vṛttir dṛṣṭā cakṣū rūpaṃ paśyati, manaḥ saṅkalpayati, ahaṅkāro 'bhimānayati, buddhir adhyavasyati | evaṃ rasanādiṣv api draṣṭavyam | kiṃ cānyat --- dṛṣṭe tathāpy adṛṣṭe | trayasya tatpūrvikā vṛttiḥ | tacchabdena samanantaroktāni buddhīndriyāṇi bhavanti | rūpe cakṣuḥpūrvikā, śabde śrotrapūrvikā, sparśe tvakpūrvikā, rase jihvāpūrvikā, gandhe ghrāṇapūrvikā buddhyahaṅkāramanasāṃ vṛttir iti // SkMv_30 //
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), <s>manas</s> (mind), and the eye — these four apprehend form simultaneously: 'this is a post, this is a person.' Likewise, they apprehend sound, touch, taste, and smell simultaneously — all four. Thus this is the simultaneous functioning of the four. Moreover: and sequentially — the functioning of the four, namely <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, <s>manas</s>, and the eye, is taught as sequential also. Because the interval between the successive gates is so brief, the division cannot be expressed — hence it is called 'simultaneous.' Just as a hundred young leaves are pierced by the tip of a needle [seemingly at once]. For example: <s>Devadatta</s>, walking along a road, sees a post. There a doubt arises: 'Is this a post or a person?' There he sees the form of the post and a bird perched upon it; thereupon his <s>buddhi</s> arises: 'This is a post.' It bends and stretches — then the cognition arises: 'This is a person.' Thus the sequential functioning of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, <s>manas</s>, and the eyes is observed: the eye sees form; <s>manas</s> conceptualizes; <s>ahaṅkāra</s> identifies; <s>buddhi</s> determines. The same should be understood for the tongue and other senses. Moreover: in the case of the seen, so too in the case of the unseen — the function of the three is preceded by that [external sense]. The word 'that' refers to the cognitive sense-organs just mentioned. For form, the function of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> is preceded by the eye; for sound, preceded by the ear; for touch, preceded by the skin; for taste, preceded by the tongue; for smell, preceded by the nose.

children.text: atrāha --- acetanānīndriyāṇi buddhyahaṅkārau manaś ceti kena hetunā svāṃ svāṃ vṛttiṃ pratipadyante ity atrāha ---
children.translated_text: Here a question arises: the senses, <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> are all non-conscious — by what cause do they engage in their respective functions? To this he says:

children.text: svāṃ svāṃ pratipadyante parasparākūtahetukāṃ vṛttim /
children.translated_text: Each engages in its own respective function, caused by their mutual intention;

children.text: puruṣārtha eva hetur na kenacit kāryate karaṇam // ISk_31 //
children.translated_text: The purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is the cause — the instrument is not made to act by anyone.

children.text: svāṃ svām iti vīpsām icchanti | (iti trayodaśavidhasya karaṇasya grahaṇaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati) | pratipadyante gṛhṇantīty arthaāḥ | kiṃ cānyat --- parasparākūtahetukāṃ vṛttim | buddher ākūtaṃ jñātvā ahaṅkāro 'bhimānayati, manaḥ saṅkalpayati, indriyāṇi svāṃ svāṃ vṛttiṃ pratipadyante | ākūtaṃ nāmābhiprāyaḥ | yathā kila caurasenā grāmaṃ hantuṃ gacchati tatra caurasenāpatinā saṅketaḥ(p.35) kṛto 'sti yadāhaṃ hā heti bravīmi tadā sarvaiḥ samavāyena praveṣṭavyam | yadā punar aham ahā heti bravīmi tadā nirgantavyam | etāṃ caurasenāpater ājñām ākūtaṃ jñātvā caurāḥ praviśanti nirgacchanti ca | tatheha caurasenāpatisthānīyā buddhiḥ caurasthānīyānīndriyāṇi | kiṃ svārthaṃ viṣayaṃ pratipadyante āhosvit parārtham ity atrocyate | parārthaṃ gamyate | yasmād āha --- puruṣārtha eva hetuḥ puruṣārthaḥ kartavya eva iti guṇānāṃ pravṛttiḥ | tasmād etat trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇaṃ puruṣārthaḥ pravartayati | yad apy uktam --- acetanāni karaṇāni kathaṃ pravartanta iti | atra brūmaḥ --- na kenacit kāryate karaṇam | neśvareṇa nāpi puruṣeṇa | svabhāvo nāma kaścit padārtho (nā)sti | yasmāt svayam eva ca trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇaṃ sve sve viṣaye pravartata iti // SkMv_31 //
children.translated_text: 'Each its own' — the repetition indicates 'each and every one' (of the thirteen-fold instrument is hereby understood). 'They engage in' means they apprehend — that is the meaning. Moreover: the function is caused by their mutual intention. Having known the intention (<s>ākūta</s>) of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> identifies, <s>manas</s> conceptualizes, and the senses engage in their respective functions. <s>Ākūta</s> means purpose, intention. Just as a band of thieves goes to plunder a village — the captain of the thieves has given a signal: 'When I say "hā hā," all should enter together; and when I say "ahā hā," all should exit.' Knowing this command, the intention of the thief-captain, the thieves enter and exit. So here, <s>buddhi</s> occupies the position of the thief-captain, and the senses occupy the position of the thieves. Do they engage in their objects for their own purpose or for another's purpose? To this it is replied: they function for another's purpose. Because he says: the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is the cause — the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> is solely for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>. Therefore, this thirteen-fold instrument is set in motion by the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>. As for what was said — 'the instruments are non-conscious; how do they function?' — to that we say: the instrument is not made to act by anyone — neither by <s>Īśvara</s> (God) nor by <s>Puruṣa</s>. There is a certain reality called 'inherent nature' (<s>svabhāva</s>). For the thirteen-fold instrument operates in its own respective domain by itself.

children.text:
atrāha --- uktaṃ ca bhagavatā na kenacit kāryate karaṇam iti |
tat katividhaṃ karaṇam iti? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here a question arises: the Blessed One has said 'the instrument is not made to act by anyone.' How many kinds of instruments are there? To this he says:

children.text: karaṇaṃ trayodaśavidhaṃ tadāharaṇadhāraṇaprakāśakaram /
children.translated_text: The instrument is thirteen-fold; its [function is] procuring, sustaining, and illuminating;

children.text: kāryaṃ ca tasya daśadhāhāryaṃ dhāryaṃ prakāśyaṃ ca // ISk_32 //
children.translated_text: And its object is tenfold — that which is to be procured, sustained, and illuminated.

children.text: yad atra karaṇam ity uktaṃ tat trayodaśavidham iti boddhyam | pañca karmendriyāṇi, pañca buddhīndriyāṇi, buddhyahaṅkārau mana iti etat trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇam iti | atrāha --- āhārakaṃ dhārakaṃ prakāśakaṃ ca tad iti | tatrāhārakam indriyalakṣaṇam | dhārakam abhimānalakṣaṇam | prakāśakaṃ buddhilakṣaṇam | atrāha --- kiṃ tad asti yasyāharaṇaṃ dhāraṇaṃ prakāśanaṃ ca kriyate | atrocyate --- kāryaṃ ca tasya daśadhāhāryaṃ dhāryaṃ prakāśyaṃ ca | kāryam iti śabdasparśarasarūpagandhāḥ pañca, vacanādānaviharaṇotsargānandāḥ pañca | ete daśa viṣayāḥ kāryam ity ucyate | taṃ daśavidhaṃ viṣayaṃ buddhīndriyaiḥ prakāśitam arthaṃ karmendriyāṇy āharanti dhārayanti ca | tad yathā tamasi sthitaṃ pradīpena prakāśitaṃ ghaṭaṃ hasta ādatte dhārayati ca | tad evaṃ yathā ghaṭaṃ tathā śeṣāṇy api // SkMv_32 //
children.translated_text: What has been called 'instrument' here is to be understood as thirteen-fold. The five action-organs, the five cognitive organs, <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s> — this is the thirteen-fold instrument. Here a question arises: it procures, sustains, and illuminates — so it is said. Among these, the procuring [function] has the characteristic of the senses. The sustaining [function] has the characteristic of self-identification (<s>abhimāna</s>). The illuminating [function] has the characteristic of <s>buddhi</s>. Here a question arises: is there something that is procured, sustained, and illuminated? To this he says: and its object is tenfold — that which is to be procured, sustained, and illuminated. 'Object' means: the five — sound, touch, taste, form, and smell; and the five — speech, grasping, movement, excretion, and pleasure. These ten objects are called the 'effect.' This tenfold domain, its meaning illuminated by the cognitive organs, is procured and sustained by the action-organs. Just as a pot standing in darkness, illuminated by a lamp, is taken up and held by the hand. As with the pot, so with the rest.

children.text: antaḥkaraṇaṃ trividhaṃ daśadhā bāhyaṃ trayasya viṣayākhyam /
children.translated_text: The inner instrument is threefold; the outer is tenfold, called the domain of the three;

children.text: sāmpratakālaṃ bāhyaṃ trikālam ābhyantaraṃ karaṇam // ISk_33 //
children.translated_text: The outer instrument operates in the present time; the inner instrument operates in all three times.

children.text: antaḥkaraṇaṃ trividham iti buddhyahaṅkāramanasāṃ grahaṇam | etat trividham antaḥkaraṇasaṃjñitam | daśadhā bāhyaṃ buddhikarmendriyabhedāt | kiṃ cānyat | trayasya viṣayākhyaṃ buddhyahaṅkāramanasāṃ trayāṇām antaḥkaraṇānāṃ bāhyaṃ daśavidhaṃ(p.36) karaṇaṃ viṣayākhyaṃ viṣaya(?) upabhogyam iti | ābhyantaraṃ trikaṃ svāmibhūtaṃ bāhyaṃ daśavidhaṃ bhṛtyabhūtam ity arthaḥ | kiṃ cānyat --- sāmpratakālaṃ bāhyam | yad etad bāhyaṃ daśavidhaṃ karaṇam uktaṃ tat sāmpratakālaṃ vartamānaviṣayagrāhakaṃ bhavati | śrotratvakcakṣurjihvāghrāṇāni vartamānāny eva śabdādīni gṛhṇanti | nātītāni na ca bhāvīni | evaṃ vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthāni vartamāneṣu vacanādeyabhūmimalotsargānandeṣu pravartante nātītābhaviṣyatoḥ | kiñ cānyat --- trikālam ābhyantaraṃ mano'haṅkārabuddhirūpaṃ karaṇaṃ pravartate | buddhir vartamānaṃ ghaṭaṃ buddhyate atītaṃ bhaviṣyantaṃ ca smarati | tad yathā --- yudhiṣṭhirabhīmasenāv āstām atītaviṣayagrāhiṇī buddhiḥ | kalkī bhaviṣyati bhāvivastugrāhiṇī | evam ahaṅkāro 'pi trikālavān | yathāham asmin gṛhe svāmī āsaṃ, bhaviṣyāmi ceti | evaṃ mano 'py atītaṃ saṅkalpayati vartamānaṃ bhāvi ca | yata evaṃ tasmād ucyate "trikālam ābhyantaraṃ karaṇam" iti // SkMv_33 //
children.translated_text: 'The inner instrument is threefold' — this refers to <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>. These three are designated as the inner instrument. 'The outer is tenfold' — due to the distinction of cognitive and action organs. Moreover: 'called the domain of the three' — the outer, tenfold instrument is the domain — the object of experience — of the three inner instruments: <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>manas</s>. The inner three are like masters; the outer tenfold are like servants — that is the meaning. Moreover: 'the outer operates in the present time' — the outer tenfold instrument that has been described apprehends only present-time objects. The ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose grasp sounds and the like only as they are present — not past ones, not future ones. Similarly, speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals function with respect to present activities of speaking, grasping, moving, excreting, and experiencing pleasure — not with respect to past or future ones. Moreover: 'the inner instrument operates in all three times' — the instrument in the form of <s>manas</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and <s>buddhi</s> operates [in all three times]. <s>Buddhi</s> cognizes a present pot, and it also remembers past and future [objects]. For example: '<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and <s>Bhīmasena</s> existed' — this <s>buddhi</s> grasps a past object. '<s>Kalki</s> will be' — this grasps a future object. Similarly, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> also operates in the three times: 'I was the master of this house, and I shall be.' Likewise, <s>manas</s> conceptualizes the past, present, and future. Because this is so, it is said: 'the inner instrument operates in all three times.'

children.text: atrāha --- kāni indriyāṇi saviśeṣaṃ viṣayaṃ gṛhṇanti, kāni nirviśeṣam | atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here a question arises: which senses grasp specific objects, and which grasp non-specific [objects]? To this he says:

children.text: buddhīndriyāṇi teṣāṃ pañca viśeṣāviśeṣaviṣayāṇi /
children.translated_text: The cognitive senses — of these five, some have specific and some have non-specific objects;

children.text: vāg bhavati śabdaviṣayā śeṣāny api pañcaviṣayāṇi // ISk_34 //
children.translated_text: Speech has sound as its object; the remaining five [action-organs] also have [all] five objects.

children.text: teṣām karaṇānāṃ madhye yeṣām ayam adhikāro vartate teṣāṃ yāni buddhīndriyāṇi śrotratvakcakṣurjihvāghrāṇāni pañca tāni saviśeṣaṃ gṛhṇanti aviśeṣam api viṣayaṃ gṛhṇanti | atrāha --- kasya saviśeṣaṃ viṣayaṃ gṛhṇanti kasya nirviśeṣam iti | atrocyate śabdasparśarasarūpagandhāḥ pajña devānāṃ tanmātrasaṃjñitā nirviśeṣāḥ kevalasukhalakṣaṇatvāt | yasmāt tatra duḥkhamohau na stas tasmān nirviśeṣās te iti | tathā hi | viśiṣyante śāntaghoramūḍhatvādineti viśeṣās taiḥ saha saviśeṣāḥ, kevalā nirviśeṣā iti tātparyam | evaṃ śabdādayo manuṣyāṇāṃ saviśeṣāḥ sukhaduḥkhamohayuktā ity arthaḥ | devānāṃ tu buddhīndriyāṇi nirviśeṣaṃ sukhātmakaṃ prakāśayanti | uktāni buddhīndriyāṇi devānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca | karmendriyāṇi vakṣyāmaḥ | vāg bhavati śabdaviṣayā śeṣāny api pañca viṣayāṇi | tatra devānāṃ vāk pādaṃ pādārdhaṃ ślokam uccārayati | asmākam api tathaiva | ato devānām asmākaṃ ca vāgindriyaṃ tulyam ity arthaḥ | kiṃ cānyat --- śeṣāṇy api pañca viṣayāṇi iti | teṣāṃ(p.37) caturṇām ekaikaṃ pañcaviṣayam | pāṇis tāvat śabdasparśarasarūpagandhayuktaḥ | evaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam eva pāṇīndriyaṃ sannikṛṣṭaṃ pañcalakṣaṇaṃ ghaṭaṃ gṛhṇāti | (yasmāt pañcalakṣaṇaṃ hastaṃ hastendriyaṃ ca) evaṃ śabdādipañcalakṣaṇaḥ pādaḥ pañcātmikāyām eva bhuvi viharati | evaṃ pañcalakṣaṇe pāyūpasthe api pañcalakṣaṇāv utsargānandau kurutaḥ | tasmāt yuktam abhihitam --- "śeṣāṇy api pañca viṣayāṇi" iti // SkMv_34 //
children.translated_text: Among those sense faculties (<s>karaṇas</s>) to which this topic pertains, the five cognitive faculties (<s>buddhīndriyas</s>) — hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell — grasp [objects] that are both specific (<s>saviśeṣa</s>) and non-specific (<s>aviśeṣa</s>). Here one asks: for whom do they grasp specific objects, and for whom non-specific? To this it is said: sounds, touches, tastes, forms, and smells — the five [sensory objects] of the <s>devas</s> (gods), called <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), are non-specific (<s>nirviśeṣa</s>), because they are characterized solely by pleasure. Since suffering and delusion do not exist there, they are non-specific. For thus: they are 'distinguished' (<s>viśeṣas</s>) by being peaceful, violent, or dull — 'specific' means 'together with those [distinctions]'; alone, they are 'non-specific' — this is the purport. Thus, sounds and the like for human beings are specific (<s>saviśeṣa</s>), i.e. endowed with pleasure, suffering, and delusion — that is the meaning. But for the <s>devas</s>, the cognitive faculties reveal [objects that are] non-specific and of the nature of pleasure alone. The cognitive faculties of <s>devas</s> and humans have been stated. We shall now explain the action-organs (<s>karmendriyas</s>). Speech has sound as its object; and the remaining [organs] also [have] five objects. Therein, the speech of the <s>devas</s> utters a verse-quarter, a half-verse, or a full verse. Ours is likewise. Therefore the speech-organ of the <s>devas</s> and ours is equal — that is the meaning. And furthermore: 'The remaining also have five objects.' Each of the [other] four has five objects. The hand, for instance, is endowed with sound, touch, taste, form, and smell. Thus the hand-organ, having five characteristics, grasps a pot that [also] has five characteristics. (Since the hand and the hand-organ have five characteristics.) Similarly, the foot, having five characteristics of sound and the rest, moves about only on the earth that has five characteristics. Likewise, the organs of excretion and generation, also having five characteristics, perform excretion and pleasure that have five characteristics. Therefore it is rightly stated: 'The remaining also have five objects.' [SkMv 34]

children.text: idānīṃ buddhiviṣayakhyāpanāyedam ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Now, for the purpose of declaring the object of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), this is stated:

children.text: sāntaḥkaraṇā buddhiḥ sarvaṃ viṣayam avagāhate yasmāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), together with the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), encompasses every object;

children.text: tasmāt trividhaṃ karaṇaṃ dvāri dvārāṇi śeṣāṇi // ISk_35 //
children.translated_text: Therefore the threefold [internal] instrument is the [primary] gateway; the remaining [organs] are the doors. [ISk 35]

children.text: sāntaḥkaraṇā antaḥkaraṇe ahaṃmanasī tābhyāṃ saha vartate yā buddhiḥ sā tathoktā | sā buddhiḥ sarvaṃ viṣayaṃ niravaśeṣaṃ triṣv api kāleṣu yasmād avagāhate vyāpnoti gṛhṇāti śabdādyaṃ pañcavidhaṃ tasmād eva tanmanobuddhyahaṅkāralakṣaṇaṃ trividham eva karaṇaṃ sādhanaṃ, kriyate 'nenetikṛtvā | śeṣāṇi punaḥ dvāri bāhye yāni buddhikarmendriyatayā pratītāni śrotravākprabhṛtīni daśa tāni tasyā eva mano'haṅkārayuktāyā buddher viṣayagrahaṇāya dvārāṇi pratīkāny eva na tu karaṇatayā sānvayāni | tathā etair daśabhir dvāraiḥ sāntaḥkaraṇā buddhir eva viṣayān gṛhṇātīti trividham eva karaṇam ity arthaḥ // SkMv_35 //
children.translated_text: 'Together with the internal organ' — [<s>buddhi</s>] operates together with the two internal organs, ego (<s>aham</s>) and mind (<s>manas</s>); that <s>buddhi</s> so described — that <s>buddhi</s> encompasses, pervades, grasps every object without remainder, in all three times, the fivefold [category of] sound and the rest. Therefore this very threefold instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) — characterized by mind, <s>buddhi</s>, and <s>ahaṅkāra</s> — is the means, the 'gateway' — because acting is accomplished through it. The remaining [organs], however, which are external — the ten that are known as the cognitive and action faculties beginning with hearing and speech — are merely doors, openings for that very <s>buddhi</s>, conjoined with <s>manas</s> and <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, to grasp objects. They are not inherently instrumental in their own right. Thus, through these ten doors, <s>buddhi</s> together with the internal organ alone grasps the objects — therefore the instrument is only threefold — that is the meaning. [SkMv 35]

children.text: kiñ cānyat ---
children.translated_text: And furthermore:

children.text: ete pradīpakalpāḥ parasparavilakṣaṇā guṇaviśeṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: These [thirteen instruments], like lamps, are mutually distinct specific modifications of the <s>guṇas</s>;

children.text: kṛtsnaṃ puruṣasyārthaṃ prakāśya buddhau prayacchanti // ISk_36 //
children.translated_text: Having illuminated the entire purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, they present it to <s>buddhi</s>. [ISk 36]

children.text: ete iti buddhikarmāntaḥkaraṇabhedās trayodeśa pradīpakalpāḥ pradīpatulyāḥ | kiṃ cānyat | parasparavilakṣaṇāḥ | bhinnalakṣaṇā visadṛśā ity arthaḥ | śrotraṃ hi śabdaṃ gṛhṇāti, na sparśādīn | evam itaratra | vāg vakty eva na gṛhṇāti gacchati viharaty ānandati | evaṃ pāṇyādiṣu | manaḥ saṅkalpayati nāhaṅkurute | ahaṅkāraś cābhimanute na saṅkalpayati | evaṃ dvādaśāpi svaṃ svam arthaṃ puruṣabhogyatayā prakāśya buddhau prayacchanti nikṣipanti | tad buddhisthaṃ viṣayaṃ sukhaduḥkhādyaṃ puruṣa upalabhate // SkMv_36 //
children.translated_text: 'These' — the thirteen, differentiated into cognitive, action, and internal organs — are 'like lamps,' equal to lamps. And furthermore, 'mutually distinct' — having different characteristics, dissimilar — that is the meaning. For hearing grasps sound, not touch and the rest. Likewise in the other cases. Speech only speaks; it does not grasp, walk, move about, or delight. Similarly with the hand and the rest. Mind conceptualizes; it does not make ego-assertions. And ego-sense identifies; it does not conceptualize. Thus all twelve, having illuminated each their own purpose as objects for <s>Puruṣa</s>'s experience, present them to — deposit them in — <s>buddhi</s>. That object established in <s>buddhi</s> — pleasure, suffering, and the like — <s>Puruṣa</s> apprehends. [SkMv 36]

children.text: kiñ cānyat ---
children.translated_text: And furthermore:

children.text: sarvaṃ pratyupabhogaṃ yasmāt puruṣasya sādhayati buddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Since <s>buddhi</s> accomplishes for <s>Puruṣa</s> the entire range of experience,

children.text: saiva ca viśinaṣṭi tataḥ pradhānapuruṣāntaraṃ sūkṣmam // ISk_37 //
children.translated_text: it is <s>buddhi</s> itself that also discriminates the subtle [difference] between <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. [ISk 37]

children.text: nirviśeṣaṃ triṣv api kāleṣu yo yo viṣayaṃ prati upabhogo devatiryagyoniṣu taṃ taṃ puruṣasya yasmād hetor buddhir eva sādhayati niṣpādayati | rājāmātyavat | yathā sarveṣāṃ bhṛtyānāṃ mantrī upalabdhiṃ vidhāya rājani nivedayati | evaṃ karmendriyāṇi prakāśya buddhau prayacchanti | buddhir api puruṣāya prayacchati samarpayati | anena prakāreṇa buddhir abhyudayaphalena | yāvajjñānaṃ notpadyate tāvat puruṣaṃ yojayati | svairiṇīva kāmukaṃ mūḍhavijñānaṃ ghṛtādyupacāraiḥ | buddhipreritā ahaṃmanobuddhikarmendriyākhyā viṣayān na svārthaṃ na ca buddhyarthaṃ kiṃ tu puruṣārtham eva sādhayanti | yathā salakṣmīkasvairiṇīgṛhe dāsyas tadādeśena rasavatīṃ na svārthaṃ na ca svāmitayāvasthitasvairiṇy arthaṃ kiṃ tu tayāpahṛtavivekavijñānasya kāmukasya kṛte nirvartayanti tadvat | yāvad asau vimūḍhas tāvad anayā buddhyā svairiṇy eva kāmuko viṣayair upahriyate | yadāsau katham api guruśāstrātmānubhavādibhir ātmānaṃ cetayate tadā svairiṇīva buddhir api puruṣaṃ vihāya saṃśāmyati | tato 'sau kevalatayāvatiṣṭhate | tadanubhavāvasthitir muktir iti yat kiñcid idam aprastutam | prastutam ucyate | kiñ cānyat | ataḥ saiva ca viśinaṣṭi tataḥ pradhānapuruṣāntaraṃ sūkṣmam | sūkṣmaṃ durvijñeyam | pradhānapuruṣāntaraṃ nānātvam | sūkṣmatvād atīva durbodham iti yāvat | buddhir hi adhyavasāyātmikā svavyāpāreṇa cādhyavasāyena sādhayati | ahaṅkārendriyatanmātrabhūtādhyavasāyena jagat pradhānapuruṣāntaravivecanena vivicya svayaṃ mriyate | ata evoktam ---
children.translated_text: Without distinction, in all three times, whatever experience (<s>upabhoga</s>) there may be in the births of <s>devas</s> (gods), animals, and the like — <s>buddhi</s> alone, for whatever reason, accomplishes, brings about that [experience] for <s>Puruṣa</s>. Like a king and his minister: just as a minister, having arranged the acquisitions of all the servants, reports them to the king — so the action-organs, having illuminated [their objects], present them to <s>buddhi</s>; and <s>buddhi</s> also presents, delivers them to <s>Puruṣa</s>. In this manner, <s>buddhi</s>, through the fruit of worldly prosperity — as long as knowledge has not arisen — keeps <s>Puruṣa</s> engaged, like a wanton woman [keeps] a lover whose discernment is deluded, through ministrations of ghee and the like. Directed by <s>buddhi</s>, the organs designated as ego, mind, cognitive, and action organs accomplish the objects not for their own sake, nor for <s>buddhi</s>'s sake, but solely for <s>Puruṣa</s>'s sake. Just as in the house of a beautiful, wanton woman, the maidservants, by her command, prepare a delicious [meal] — not for their own sake, nor for the sake of the wanton mistress, but for the sake of the lover whose discriminative knowledge she has stolen — in the same way. As long as he is deluded, so long is the lover plied with pleasures by this <s>buddhi</s>-like wanton woman. When, however, he somehow awakens through the guru, scriptures, self-experience, and the like, then <s>buddhi</s> too, like the wanton woman, having released <s>Puruṣa</s>, subsides. Thereafter, he abides in isolation (<s>kevalatā</s>). Abiding in the experience of that [isolation] is liberation (<s>mukti</s>) — this much is a digression. The main point is stated: and furthermore, it is <s>buddhi</s> itself that also discriminates the subtle [difference] — 'subtle' means difficult to know — between <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, that is, their distinctness. Being exceedingly difficult to understand because of its subtlety — that is what is meant. For <s>buddhi</s>, being of the nature of determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), accomplishes [this] through its own function of determination. Having discriminated through the determination of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, the sense faculties, the <s>tanmātras</s>, and the elements — [namely] the distinction between <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — [<s>buddhi</s>] itself dies. Therefore it is said:

children.text: "ahaṅkāro dhiyaṃ brūte mainaṃ suptaṃ prabodhaya /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) says to <s>buddhi</s> (intellect): do not awaken this sleeping one;

children.text: prabuddhe paramānande na tvaṃ nāhaṃ na tajjagat //
children.translated_text: When the supreme bliss is awakened, neither you exist, nor I, nor this world.'

children.text: mayi tiṣṭhaty ahaṅkāre puruṣaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'As long as <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) persists in me, <s>Puruṣa</s> is the twenty-fifth [principle];

children.text: tattvavṛndaṃ parityajya sa kathaṃ mokṣam icchati //
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the host of <s>tattvas</s> (principles), how can he desire liberation?'

children.text: yo 'sau sarveśvaro devaḥ sarvavyāpī jagadguruḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That one who is the Lord of all, the all-pervading God, the Guru of the world —

children.text: dehītipadam uccārya hā mayātmā laghuḥ kṛtaḥ" //
children.translated_text: By uttering the word 'embodied one' (<s>dehī</s>), alas, the Self has been diminished by me.'

children.text: akṛtapuṇyacaraṇair na prāpyaṃ pradhānapuruṣayor nānātvam | tayor evāntaraṃ darśayati | tvam anyam ātmānaṃ na vetsi | pradhānam anyat | sattvarajastamāṃsi trayo guṇāḥ prādhānikā amūrtāḥ sāmyāvasthāyāṃ pradhānākhyāḥ | teṣām ekatayodrekāt triguṇā buddhir anyā, anyo 'haṅkāraḥ, pañca tanmātrāṇy anyāni, ekādaśendriyāṇy anyānīti buddhvā tattvāni mokṣaṃ gacchanti | na hi bhagavataḥ kapilasya mate kim api kartavyam anuṣṭheyatayā, kiṃ tu sāṅkhyānāṃ (p.39) pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānam eva sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa ca niḥśreyasahetuḥ | uktaṃ ca ---
children.translated_text: The distinctness of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is not attainable by those who have not performed meritorious conduct. He shows the difference between those two: you do not know the other, the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). <s>Pradhāna</s> is something else. <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — these three <s>guṇas</s>, belonging to <s>Pradhāna</s>, formless, in the state of equilibrium — are called <s>Pradhāna</s>. Having understood that from the predominance of one of them, <s>buddhi</s>, marked by the three <s>guṇas</s>, is something else; <s>ahaṅkāra</s> is something else; the five <s>tanmātras</s> are something else; the eleven sense faculties are something else — [having understood] these <s>tattvas</s>, one attains liberation. For in the doctrine of the blessed <s>Kapila</s>, there is nothing whatsoever to be done by way of practice; rather, the knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> through [investigation of] similarities and dissimilarities is alone the cause of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). And it is said:

children.text: hasa piba lala moda nityaṃ viṣayānupabhuñja kuru ca mā śaṅkām /
children.translated_text: Laugh, drink, frolic, delight constantly, enjoy sense-objects — and do not be apprehensive;

children.text: yadi viditaṃ te kapilamataṃ tat prāpsyase mokṣasaukhyaṃ ca // SkMv_37 //
children.translated_text: If you have understood the doctrine of <s>Kapila</s>, then you shall attain the bliss of liberation. [SkMv 37]

children.text: atrāha --- uktaṃ bhagavatā pūrvasyām āryāyāṃ "viśeṣāviśeṣaviṣayāṇīndriyāṇi" iti | tatra ke viśeṣā ke 'viśeṣā iti | atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks: it was stated by the master in the earlier <s>kārikā</s> (verse) that 'the sense faculties have as their objects the specific and the non-specific.' Therein, what are the specific (<s>viśeṣas</s>), and what are the non-specific (<s>aviśeṣas</s>)? To this it is said:

children.text: tanmātrāṇy aviśeṣās tebhyo bhūtāni pañca pañcabhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) are the non-specific; from them arise the five gross elements from the five [subtle ones];

children.text: ete smṛtā viśeṣāḥ śāntā ghorāś ca mūḍhāś ca // ISk_38 //
children.translated_text: These are called the specific — peaceful, violent, and dull. [ISk 38]

children.text: yāni bhūtādisaṃjñāt tāmasād ahaṅkārād utpannāni pañca tanmātrāṇi śabdādīni tāny aviśeṣā ity ucyante | devānāṃ tanmātrāṇi sukhalakṣaṇā viṣayās tatrāpi rajastamasī staḥ kiṃ tu tatra sattvam utkaṭatvena vartate tasmād aviśeṣā ity ucyante | na viśiṣyante śāntaghoramūḍhatvādibhiḥ sattvodrekāt kevalasukhatayā ity arthaḥ | tarhi viśeṣāḥ ke? atrāha --- tebhyo bhūtāni pañca pañcabhyaḥ | śabdādibhyaḥ pañcabhyaḥ ākāśādīni pañca mahābhūtāni pūrvapūrvānupraveśād ekadvitricatuṣpañca guṇāny utpadyante | ete smṛtā viśeṣāḥ | atrāha --- eteṣāṃ kiṃ lakṣaṇam iti | atrocyate | etāni pañca mahābhūtāni manuṣyāṇāṃ viṣayāḥ | śāntā ghorā mūḍhāś ca | tatrākāśaṃ śāntaṃ ghoraṃ mūḍhaṃ ca | śāntaṃ tāvat sukhalakṣaṇam | yathā kaścid garbhagṛhāt niṣkrāntaḥ avakāśasthitas tasya tadākāśaṃ sukhahetutvāc chāntaṃ syāt | tad evoṣṇaśītavātādisaṃyogād duḥkhatvād ghoraṃ syāt | pathi gacchataḥ kāndiśīkasya kevalaṃ sarvatrākāśaṃ paśyato mārgādyanabhijñasya puṃsas tad eva mūḍhaṃ syāt | evaṃ vāyau traividhyam | yathā garbhagṛhavāsino vātāyanadvāreṇa vāyuḥ praviśan sukhahetutvāc chāntaḥ | tenaivoṣṇamāsi sampannena duḥkhotpādakatayā duḥkhī syād ity asau vāyur ghoraḥ | sa eva vāyuḥ śītakāle śītaṃ janayan mūḍhaḥ | evam agniḥ śītārtasya śāntaḥ | grīṣmakāle tāpārtasya ghoraḥ | grāmādidāhe pravṛddho 'gniḥ puṃso mohotpādakatayā mūḍhaḥ | evam āpo gharmārtasya sukhadatvāc chāntāḥ | hemante duḥkhadatvād ghorāḥ | samudramadhyagatasya puṃsaḥ tīram apaśyato mohahetutvān mūḍhāḥ | evaṃ pṛthvī navaśādvalopacitā prāvṛṣi sukhakāriṇīti śāntā | grīṣmakāle uṣṇabālukā ghorā | saiva pathikasya mārgānabhijñasya prāṇigrāmādyapaśyato mūḍhā | evaṃ devānāṃ nirviśeṣā viṣayāḥ | tanmātrasaṃjñitā nirviśeṣāḥ kevalā evānandamayāḥ śāntaghoramūḍhatayāviśiṣṭāḥ svabhāvarūpāḥ(p.40) śarkarākaṭutiktādirasā niścitaṃ svabhāvamādhuryāmṛtā upameyasukhaśālikṣīram iva | mādhuryakṣārakaṭvādipārthivaguṇasampṛktaṃ svabhāvarasaṃ jalam ivāmī viṣayāḥ(?) | devānām evaṃ nirviśeṣāḥ syuḥ | tanmātrasaṃjñitāḥ sukhalakṣaṇā eva | manuṣyāṇāṃ viyadādibhūtamayatvāt bhūtānīva sukhaduḥkhamohalakṣaṇās te ity arthaḥ // SkMv_38 //
children.translated_text: Those five subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>) — sound and the rest — which have arisen from the <s>tāmasic</s> <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> called <s>Bhūtādi</s> (the elemental origin), are called the 'non-specific' (<s>aviśeṣa</s>). The subtle elements of the gods are objects characterized by pleasure; even there, <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are present, but <s>sattva</s> predominates...

children.text: atrāha --- kim etāv anta eva viṣayāḥ, na hi | kiṃ tv anye 'pi santi | ke punas te iti? ucyate |
children.translated_text: Here a question is raised: are these the only objects? No, indeed. But there are others as well. What are they? It is answered —

children.text: sūkṣmā mātāpitṛjāḥ saha prabhūtais tridhā viśeṣāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: The subtle, those born of parents, and together with the gross — the specific (<s>viśeṣa</s>) objects are threefold.

children.text: sūkṣmās teṣāṃ niyatā mātāpitṛjā nivartante // ISk_39 //
children.translated_text: The subtle among them are permanent; those born of parents cease to exist. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 39)

children.text: tatra sūkṣmās tāvat pañca tanmātrakāḥ tair evādisarge sūkṣmaśarīrāṇi trayāṇām api lokānāṃ prārabdhāni | tat sūkṣmaśarīramṛtukāle mātur udaraṃ praviśati | mātū rudhiraṃ pituḥ śukram | vedāntavādino 'py evam āhuḥ | prāṇinaḥ svarganarakādiṣu svakarmabhogānantaramatrājigamiṣavaḥ somamaṇḍale līnā bhūtvā vṛṣṭayo bhavanti | tato 'nnam, tat strīpuṃsābhyām upabhuktaṃ śukraśoṇite, tataḥ puruṣa iti | "vettha yathā pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣavacasa"(chāndogyopaniṣad 5 |3 |3) ity ārabhya "iti tu pañcamyām āhutāv āpa"(chāndogyopaniṣad 5 |9 |1) ity āhuḥ | purāṇeṣv api
children.translated_text: Of these, the subtle ones are first: the five <s>tanmātras</s>. By those very [subtle elements], at the primordial creation, the subtle bodies (<s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s>) for all three worlds were initiated. That subtle body, at the time of [conception], enters the mother's womb. The mother [contributes] blood, the father semen. The <s>Vedānta</s> philosophers also [say]...

children.text: "somavṛṣṭyannaretāṃsi puruṣas tatra pañcamaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The moon, rain, food, semen — and the <s>Puruṣa</s> is the fifth there;

children.text: sa jīvaty agnaye paścād dharanty asmād yato 'bhavat" //
children.translated_text: He lives; afterward for the fire — they support him from that whence he came.'

children.text: iti |
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tad evaṃ sūkṣmaśarīrasyopacayaṃ karoti | mātur aśitapītānnaraso mātṛnāḍīsambandhena praviśya sūkṣmaśarīrasya śukraśoṇitamayasyopacayaṃ kurute | mātuś ca nāḍyā bālasya nābhirandhraṃ praviśati | yathaikena mārgeṇa śākavāṭasyāpy āyanam udakaṃ karoti evam annapānasya raso mātṛnāḍīgato bālasya nābhiṃ praviśati | praviśya bālaśarīrasyāpy āyanaṃ karoti | tatra sūkṣmaśarīrasyākṛtir yādṛglakṣaṇā bahiḥśarīrasya bhavati hastapādaśiraḥpṛṣṭhodarajaṅghāgulpha iti | api ca śiṣṭā vadanti bahiḥśarīraṃ ṣāṭkauśikam iti | rudhiramāṃsatvaco mātṛjāḥ snāyvasthimajjānaḥ pitṛjāḥ | evam etad bāhyaśarīram ābhyantarasūkṣmaśarīrasyopacayaṃ kurute | tasyaiva bahiḥśarīropacitasya sūkṣmaśarīrasya prasavakāle yonyā nirgatasya mātur udarāt bāhyāni pañca mahābhūtāni pṛthivyādīni viharaṇasaṃsthānīyāni kṛtāni | yathā kasyacid rājakumārasya mātāpitṛbhyām upacitasya pañca mahābhūtāni kṛtāni | ākāśam avakāśane, bhūmir viharaṇe, āpaḥ piṇḍīkaraṇe śuddhau ca, agnir(p.41) āhārapacane, vāyur vyūhane, asya śarīrasyaivam ete viśeṣāḥ trividhāḥ | sūkṣmā mātāpitṛjāḥ saha prabhūtaiḥ | pra ity upasargaḥ | evaṃ sūkṣmā mātāpitṛjā bhūtāni cety arthaḥ | tāni ca pṛthivyādīni | evam ete tridhā viśeṣāḥ | ye cānye prāg abhihitā viśeṣāḥ śāntā ghorā mūḍhāś ca | atrāha --- eteṣu triṣv api viśeṣeṣu ke nityāḥ ke 'nityā ity atrocyate --- sūkṣmās teṣāṃ niyatāḥ | sūkṣmā iti yair ādisargārambhas te niyatā nityā ity arthaḥ | tair ārabdhaṃ sūkṣmaśarīram asmin sthūlaśarīre patati tad adharmeṇa saṃyuktaṃ paśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpasthāvarāntāni pañca sthānāni paśyati | dharmādharmayoḥ sāmyena brāhmaṇādīni caṇḍālāntāni paśyati | evaṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ niyataṃ yāvat saṃsāram ity arthaḥ | tad yāvaj jñānaṃ guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhirūpaṃ notpadyate tāvat saṃsarati, utpanne jñāne nivartate | tasmiṃś ca nivṛtte puruṣo mokṣaṃ gacchati | uktaṃ ca ---
children.translated_text: In this way, the subtle body undergoes growth. The nutritive essence of food eaten and drunk by the mother enters through the connection of the mother's channels (<s>nāḍī</s>) and nourishes the subtle body, which consists of semen and blood. And through the mother's channel it enters the navel-opening of the child. Just as...

children.text: "dehe mohāśraye bhagne yuktaḥ sa paramātmani /
children.translated_text: 'When the body, the abode of delusion, is broken, [the Self] united with the Supreme Self,

children.text: kumbhākāśa ivākāśe labhate caikarūpatām" //
children.translated_text: Like the space within a pot [merging] into space, attains oneness of form.'

children.text: "yathā darpaṇābhāva ābhāsahānau" ityādi | tasmād etat sūkṣmam | mātāpitṛjā nivartante tat sūkṣmaśarīraṃ parityajya maraṇakāle mātāpitṛjaṃ patati | tat sūkṣmaśarīraṃ jñānam aviduṣāṃ saṃsarati // SkMv_39 //
children.translated_text: 'Just as in the absence of a mirror, the reflection ceases' — and so on. Therefore, this [body] is subtle. 'Those born of parents cease to exist' — abandoning the subtle body, at the time of death, the [gross body] born of parents falls. That subtle body, for those without knowledge, continues to transmigrate.

children.text: atrāha --- uktaṃ ca bhagavatā --- "mātāpitṛjā nivartante tat sūkṣmaṃ saṃsaratīty arthaḥ | atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here a question is raised: and the Blessed One stated — 'Those born of parents cease to exist; the subtle one transmigrates' — this is the meaning. This is addressed —

children.text: pūrvotpannam asaktaṃ niyataṃ mahadādisūkṣmaparyantam /
children.translated_text: Originated in the beginning, unattached, permanent, extending from <s>Mahat</s> down to the subtle elements,

children.text: saṃsarati nirupabhogaṃ bhāvair adhivāsitaṃ liṅgam // ISk_40 //
children.translated_text: The <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) transmigrates without [direct] experience, perfumed by dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>). (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 40)

children.text: pūrvotpannam ityādi | sargotpannam ity arthaḥ | yāvaj jñānaṃ notpadyate tāvat saṃsāre sthirataraṃ sthitam ity arthaḥ | kiñ cānyat --- asaktaṃ, kvacin na saktam ity asaktaṃ devamānuṣatiryakṣu sūkṣmatvāt | niyataṃ nityam ity arthaḥ | pañca karmendriyāṇi pañca buddhīndriyāṇi pañca tanmātrāṇi mano buddhir ahaṅkāra evam aṣṭādaśa --- mahadādisūkṣmaparyantam iti | mahāny asyādau, sūkṣmāṇi tanmātrāṇi śabdādiviṣayākhyāny ante yasya tat tathoktam | antaḥkaraṇabahiḥkaraṇāni trayodaśa tanmātrāṇi pañca ceti | atrāha --- tat kiṃ karoti | atrocyate --- saṃsarati devamānuṣatiryagyoniṣu jīvabhāvam āgacchati | tad dhi(p.42) nirupabhogaṃ śabdādayo viṣayā upabhogās tair virahitam | trayodaśakaraṇātmakam evety arthaḥ | bhāvair adhivāsitaṃ devamānuṣatiryagbhāvādhivāsitam evety arthaḥ | yathā tilapatanavastravāsanavat(?) | tadvat śāntā bhāvā bhavanti | devabhāvāḥ śubhena miśreṇa mānuṣā aśubhena tiryaktvam | liṅgaṃ pralayakāle pradhāne layaṃ gacchatīti liṅgam | prakarṣeṇa dhīyate kṣipyate 'tra sarvam iti pradhānam // SkMv_41 //
children.translated_text: "Originated in the beginning" and so on — the meaning is: originated at the time of creation. As long as knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) has not arisen, so long it remains more firmly established in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) — this is the meaning. And what else — "unattached" (<s>asakta</s>): not attached anywhere, meaning unattached to gods, humans, or animals due to its subtlety. "Permanent" (<s>niyata</s>) means eternal — this is the meaning. Five organs of action (<s>karmendriya</s>), five organs of cognition (<s>buddhīndriya</s>), five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), <s>manas</s> (mind), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), and <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense) — thus eighteen — "extending from <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One) down to the subtle elements." That which has the great ones (<s>Mahat</s> etc.) at its beginning, and the subtle ones — the <s>tanmātras</s> known as the objects of sound and so forth — at its end, is so called. The thirteen internal and external instruments (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> and <s>bahiḥkaraṇa</s>) and the five <s>tanmātras</s>. Here one asks — what does it do? To this it is said — it transmigrates (<s>saṃsarati</s>) through the wombs of gods, humans, and animals, arriving at the state of a living being (<s>jīvabhāva</s>). For it is without [direct] experience (<s>nirupabhoga</s>) — the objects such as sound are experiences (<s>upabhoga</s>), and it is devoid of those; it consists only of the thirteen instruments — this is the meaning. "Perfumed by dispositions (<s>bhāvas</s>)" means perfumed by the dispositions of gods, humans, and animals — this is the meaning. Just as a cloth is scented by the fragrance of sesame seeds placed upon it, so the <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions) become subtle. The divine dispositions arise through meritorious [action], mixed [action produces] human [birth], and through demeritorious [action comes] animal birth. The <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) at the time of dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) merges into <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) — hence it is called <s>liṅga</s>. That into which everything is cast forth (<s>prakarṣeṇa dhīyate kṣipyate</s>) is <s>pradhāna</s>. (Commentary on <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 41)

children.text: atrāha --- sūkṣmaśarīreṇa nāsti prayojanam | tarhi trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇam eva kathaṃ saṃsaratīti? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one objects — there is no purpose for the subtle body (<s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s>); then how does the thirteen-fold instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) alone transmigrate? To this it is said —

children.text: citraṃ yathāśrayamṛte sthāṇvādibhyo vinā yathā chāyā /
children.translated_text: Just as a painting does not [exist] without a support, just as a shadow [does not exist] without posts and the like,

children.text: tadvad vināviśeṣais tiṣṭhati na nirāśrayaṃ liṅgam // ISk_41 //
children.translated_text: So too the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) does not stand without support, without the <s>aviśeṣas</s> (unparticularized elements). (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 41)

children.text: ihāśrayāśrayiṇoḥ sambandho dṛṣṭaḥ | na hy āśrayaṃ vināśrayī tiṣṭhati | kuḍyāpaṭāśrayaṃ kṛtvā citram avatiṣṭhate | tad idaṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ kuḍyapaṭasthānīyaṃ citrasaṃsthānīyaṃ trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇam | tad evaṃ sati yad uktaṃ bhavatā trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇam eva saṃsaratīti tan mithyā | kiṃ cānyat --- sthāṇvādibhyo vinā yathā chāyā iti | sthāṇupuruṣādibhir vinā yathā chāyā na bhavati | chāyāṃ vinā te ca na bhavanti | yathāgninā vinā prakāśo na bhavati | tadvad vināviśeṣais tiṣṭhati na nirāśrayaṃ liṅgam iti | aviśeṣā iti tanmātrāṇi svābhāvikakṣīrajalavac śāntaghoramūḍhatvarahitatvāt | tair ārabdhaṃ sūkṣmaśarīram | tena sūkṣmaśarīreṇa sargādiprārabdhena vinā nirāśrayaṃ trayodaśakaraṇākhyaṃ liṅgaṃ na tiṣṭhati | ato yad uktaṃ bhavatā "kim aviśeṣair ārabdhasūkṣmaśarīrakalpanayā prayojanaṃ trayodaśavidhaṃ karaṇam ea saṃsarati" iti, tan mithyā // SkMv_41 //
children.translated_text: Here the relationship between support and the supported is observed. For the supported does not stand without a support. A painting exists by taking a wall or cloth as its support. This subtle body (<s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s>) occupies the position of the wall or cloth, while the thirteen-fold instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) occupies the position of the painting. This being so, what was stated by you — that the thirteen-fold instrument alone transmigrates — that is false. And what else — "just as a shadow without posts and the like": just as without a post, a person, and so forth, there is no shadow, and without a shadow they too do not exist; just as without fire there is no light — "so too the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) does not stand without support, without the <s>aviśeṣas</s> (unparticularized elements)." The <s>aviśeṣas</s> are the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), which are devoid of the qualities of tranquility (<s>śānta</s>), turbulence (<s>ghora</s>), and delusion (<s>mūḍha</s>), like naturally occurring milk or water. From those the subtle body is produced. Without that subtle body, which has been produced since the beginning of creation, the <s>liṅga</s> called the thirteen instruments does not stand unsupported. Therefore what was stated by you — "what is the purpose of positing a subtle body produced from the <s>aviśeṣas</s>, since the thirteen-fold instrument alone transmigrates" — that is false. (Commentary on <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 41)

children.text: atrāha --- sūkṣmaśarīraṃ trayodaśavidhakaraṇasampannaṃ kena hetunā saṃsaratīti? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks — for what reason does the subtle body (<s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s>), endowed with the thirteen-fold instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), transmigrate? To this it is said —

children.text: puruṣārthahetukam idaṃ nimittanaimittikaprasaṅgena /
children.translated_text: This [subtle body functions] for the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>'s (the conscious self's) goal, through the connection of cause and effect,

children.text: prakṛter vibhutvayogān naṭavad vyavatiṣṭhate liṅgam // ISk_42 //
children.translated_text: And due to the conjunction with the pervasive power of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) operates like an actor. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 42)

children.text: puruṣārthaḥ kartavya iti pradhānasya tāvat pravṛttiḥ | sa cārtho dvividhaḥ | śabdādyupalabdhilakṣaṇo guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhilakṣaṇaś ca | śabdādyupalabdhir brahmalokādiṣu bhogāvāptir guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhir mokṣa iti | tasmād uktam --- puruṣārthahetukam idaṃ sūkṣmaśarīram iti | kiṃ cānyat --- nimittanaimittikaprasaṅgena(p.43) | tatra nimittaṃ dharmādyaṣṭavidham | tat purastāt vakṣyāmaḥ "dharmeṇa gamanam ūrdhvam" ityādi | prakṛtiḥ pradhānam | vibhutvaṃ prabhutvaṃ tasya yogāt(tadvibhutvayogāt) | yathā kaścid rājā prabhutvayogena svarāṣṭre yad yad icchati tat tat karoti | evaṃ pradhānam api prabhutvayogena mānuṣyaṃ vā daivaṃ vā tairyagyonyaṃ vā kurute | evaṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ trayodaśavidhena karaṇena saṃyuktaṃ hastinyā udara praviśya hastī bhavati | strīśarīraṃ praviśya manuṣyo bhavati | paśur bhavati | tasmāt naṭavad vyavatiṣṭhate liṅgam // SkMv_42 //
children.translated_text: The purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the conscious self) is what must be accomplished — for this reason <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) first engages in activity. And that purpose is twofold: that characterized by the apprehension of sound and other [sense objects], and that characterized by the apprehension of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents of nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s>. The apprehension of sound and so forth is the attainment of enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) in <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of <s>Brahmā</s>) and other [realms]; the apprehension of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). Therefore it is said — "this subtle body functions for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s goal." And what else — "through the connection of cause and effect": therein the cause (<s>nimitta</s>) is the eightfold [set] beginning with <s>dharma</s> (virtue). We shall explain that further on with "through <s>dharma</s> there is movement upward" and so forth. <s>Prakṛti</s> is <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). Pervasive power (<s>vibhutva</s>) means sovereignty (<s>prabhutva</s>), and due to conjunction with that [power] — just as a certain king, by virtue of his sovereign power, does whatever he wishes in his own kingdom, so too <s>Pradhāna</s>, by virtue of its sovereign power, produces a human birth, or a divine birth, or an animal birth. Thus the subtle body, conjoined with the thirteen-fold instrument, enters the womb of an elephant and becomes an elephant; entering a woman's body it becomes a human being; it becomes an animal. Therefore the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) operates like an actor. (Commentary on <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 42)

children.text: atrāha --- ukta purā bhāvair adhivāsitaṃ liṅgaṃ sūkṣmaśarīraṃ saṃsarati | tat ke bhāvā iti? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks — it was said earlier that the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), the <s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s> (subtle body), transmigrates perfumed by <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions). What then are these <s>bhāvas</s>? To this it is said —

children.text: sāṃsiddhikāś ca bhāvāḥ prākṛtikā vaikṛtāś ca dharmādyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions), beginning with <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and the rest, are <s>sāṃsiddhika</s> (innate), <s>prākṛtika</s> (natural), and <s>vaikṛtika</s> (acquired through transformation);

children.text: dṛṣṭāḥ karaṇāśrayiṇaḥ kāryāśrayiṇaś ca kalalādyāḥ // ISk_43 //
children.translated_text: They are observed to depend on the instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>), and [also] to depend on effects (<s>kārya</s>), beginning with <s>kalala</s> (the embryonic stage). (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 43)

children.text: trividhā bhāvāś cintyante | tatra kecit sāṃsiddhikāḥ, kecit prākṛtikāḥ, kecid vaikṛtāḥ | tatra sāṃsiddhikās tāvat --- yathā kapilasya bhagavataḥ paramarṣer ādisarge utpannasyeme catvāro bhāvāḥ sahotpannā dharmo jñānaṃ vairāgyam aiśvaryam iti | ete sāṃsiddhikā ucyante | prākṛtikā nāma brahmaṇaḥ putrāḥ kila sanakādayo babhūvuḥ | teṣām utpannakāryakāraṇānāṃ śarīravatāṃ ṣoḍaśavarṣāṇām evaite catvāro bhāvā akasmād evotpannā nidhidarśanavat | ete ca prākṛtikā bhāvā ucyante | vaikṛtikā yathā --- ācāryādimūrtim adhikṛtya utpannā vaikṛtikā ity ucyante | ācāryaṃ nimittaṃ kṛtvā jñānam utpadyate | jñānād vairāgyaṃ, vairāgyād dharmo, dharmād aiśvaryam | evam ete catvāro bhāvā asmadādiṣv api vartante | tad eva vaikṛtā ity ucyante | evam ete tridhā bhāvā vyākhyātā yair adhivāsitaṃ mahadādi liṅgaṃ saṃsarati | atrāha --- dharmo, jñānam, vairāgyam aiśvaryam, adharmo 'jñānam avairāgyam anaiśvaryam | evam ete 'ṣṭau bhāvāḥ kva vartante? pūrvarṣibhiḥ dṛṣṭāḥ karaṇāśrayiṇaḥ | karaṇāny(p.44) ucyante buddhikarmāntaḥkaraṇabhedāt trayodaśa | tāny āśrityāṣṭau bhāvāḥ pravartante | uktaṃ hi "adhyavasāyo buddhir dharmo jñānaṃ virāga aiśvaryam" ity evamādi | kiṃ cānyat --- kāryāśrayiṇaś ca kalalādyāḥ | yathā sūkṣmaśarīram utpattikāle mātur udaraṃ praviśati | mātuḥ rudhiraṃ pituḥ śukraṃ tasya sūkṣmaśarīrasyopacaya kurute | kalalabudbudaghanamāṃsapeśīgarbhakumārayauvanasthāvirādayo 'nnapānarasanimittā utpadyante | tatra ucyate --- "kāryāśrayiṇaś ca kalalādyā" iti | kalalagrahaṇaṃ virāganimittam // SkMv_43 //
children.translated_text: The <s>bhāvas</s> (dispositions) are considered to be of three kinds. Among them, some are <s>sāṃsiddhika</s> (innate), some are <s>prākṛtika</s> (natural), and some are <s>vaikṛtika</s> (acquired through transformation). First, the <s>sāṃsiddhika</s>: just as for the blessed <s>Kapila</s>, the supreme sage, who arose at the first creation — these four <s>bhāvas</s> arose together with him: <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty). These are called <s>sāṃsiddhika</s> (innate). The <s>prākṛtika</s> (natural) are as follows: <s>Brahmā</s>'s sons, namely <s>Sanaka</s> and the others, it is said, came into being. For them, who had bodies and possessed the [evolutes of] cause and effect, at the age of sixteen years these four <s>bhāvas</s> arose spontaneously, like the discovery of a treasure. These are called <s>prākṛtika</s> <s>bhāvas</s>. The <s>vaikṛtika</s> (acquired through transformation) are as follows — those that arise by resorting to the form of a teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) and so forth are called <s>vaikṛtika</s>. By taking a teacher as the instrumental cause, knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) arises; from knowledge comes dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>); from dispassion comes virtue (<s>dharma</s>); from virtue comes sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>). Thus these four <s>bhāvas</s> exist in people like us as well. These are called <s>vaikṛtika</s>. Thus these three kinds of <s>bhāvas</s> have been explained — perfumed by which the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) beginning with <s>Mahat</s> (the Great One) transmigrates. Here one asks — <s>dharma</s> (virtue), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), <s>adharma</s> (vice), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), <s>avairāgya</s> (attachment), <s>anaiśvarya</s> (powerlessness) — thus these are eight <s>bhāvas</s>; where do they abide? The ancient sages (<s>pūrvarṣi</s>) have observed [them] to depend on the instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>). The instruments are said to be thirteen, distinguished as <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>karma</s> (action organs), and <s>antaḥkaraṇa</s> (inner organ). Depending on those, the eight <s>bhāvas</s> operate. For it has been said: "Ascertainment is <s>buddhi</s>; <s>dharma</s>, <s>jñāna</s>, <s>virāga</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s>" and so forth. And what else — "depending on effects, beginning with <s>kalala</s> (the embryonic stage)": when the subtle body enters the mother's womb at the time of birth, the mother's blood and the father's semen nourish and augment that subtle body. The stages of <s>kalala</s> (fluid embryo), <s>budbuda</s> (bubble), <s>ghana</s> (solid mass), <s>māṃsapeśī</s> (lump of flesh), <s>garbha</s> (fetus), <s>kumāra</s> (childhood), <s>yauvana</s> (youth), <s>sthāvira</s> (old age) and so forth arise due to the nourishment of food and drink. There it is said — "depending on effects, beginning with <s>kalala</s>." The mention of <s>kalala</s> is for the purpose of [illustrating] dispassion (<s>virāga</s>). (Commentary on <s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 43)

children.text: uktaṃ pūrvasyām āryāyāṃ "nimittanaimittikaprasaṅgena" "naṭavad vyavatiṣṭhate liṅgam" iti | tatra kiṃ nimittaṃ kiṃ ca naimittikam iti? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: It was stated in the previous verse: "through the connection of cause and effect" and "the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) operates like an actor." Therein, what is the cause (<s>nimitta</s>) and what is the effect (<s>naimittiika</s>)? To this it is said —

children.text: dharmeṇa gamanam ūrdhvaṃ gamanam adhastād bhavaty adharmeṇa /
children.translated_text: Through <s>dharma</s> (virtue) there is movement upward; through <s>adharma</s> (vice) there is movement downward;

children.text: jñānena cāpavargo viparyayād iṣyate bandhaḥ // ISk_44 //
children.translated_text: Through <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) [is attained], and from the opposite [i.e., ignorance], bondage (<s>bandha</s>) is held [to result]. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 44)

children.text: tatra dharmo nimittam | iha loke dharmaṃ yaḥ kurute tan nimittaṃ kṛtvā sūkṣmaśarīram ūrdhvaṃ gacchati | ūrdhvam ity aṣṭānāṃ devayonīnāṃ grahaṇam | tatra ādyaṃ brāhmam | prājāpatyam, aindraṃ, pitryaṃ, gāndharvaṃ, yākṣaṃ, rākṣasaṃ, paiśācam ity etāny aṣṭau sthānāni sūkṣmaśarīraṃ gacchati | tatra dharmo nimittam, ūrdhvagamanaṃ naimittikam | kiṃ cānyat --- gamanam adhastād bhavaty adharmeṇa | iha loke yamaniyamalakṣaṇo dharmas tadviparīto hy adharmaḥ, tenādharmeṇa sūkṣmaśarīram adhastād gacchati paśvādi | paśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpasthāvaram iti pañcadhā tiryak sthāvarāntam | atrādharmo nimittam, adhogamanaṃ naimittikam | kiṃ cānyat --- jñānena cāpavargaḥ | yat pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānaṃ tena jñānena tatsūkṣmaśarīraṃ nivartate | paramātmāpavargaṃ prāpnoti mokṣaṃ gacchatīty arthaḥ | ato jñānaṃ nimittam apavargo naimittikaḥ | anyac ca viparyayād iṣyate bandhaḥ | kasya viparyayāt | jñānasya viparyayo 'jñānaṃ, tenājñānenāhaṃ darśanīyaḥ subhago 'haṃ bhoktāham iti manyate | tenājñānena manuṣyatiryagdeveṣv ātmānaṃ nibadhnāti | na mokṣaṃ gacchatīty arthaḥ | ato 'jñānaṃ nimittaṃ bandho naimittikāḥ | sa ca bandhas trividhaḥ | prakṛtibandho vaikārikabandho dakṣiṇābandhaś ceti | tatra prakṛtibandho nāmāṣṭāsu prakṛtiṣu paratvenābhimānaḥ | vaikārikabandho nāma brahmādisthāneṣu śreyobuddhiḥ | dakṣiṇābandho nāma gavādidānejyānimittaḥ | evaṃ caturvidhaṃ nimittanaimittikaṃ vyākhyātam // SkMv_44 //
children.translated_text: There, <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) is the cause (<s>nimitta</s>). In this world, one who practices <s>dharma</s> — on account of that cause, the subtle body (<s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s>) goes upward. 'Upward' means to the eight divine births (<s>devayoni</s>). Of these, the first is the <s>Brāhma</s> (realm of <s>Brahmā</s>); then <s>Prājāpatya</s> (realm of <s>Prajāpati</s>), <s>Aindra</s> (realm of <s>Indra</s>), <s>Pitrya</s> (realm of the ancestors), <s>Gāndharva</s> (realm of the <s>Gandharvas</s>), <s>Yākṣa</s> (realm of the <s>Yakṣas</s>), <s>Rākṣasa</s> (realm of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>), and <s>Paiśāca</s> (realm of the <s>Piśācas</s>) — to these eight stations the subtle body goes. There, <s>dharma</s> is the cause; upward movement is the result (<s>naimittika</s>). And what else — movement downward occurs through <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness). In this world, <s>dharma</s> is characterized by <s>yama</s> (restraints) and <s>niyama</s> (observances); their opposite is <s>adharma</s>. Through that <s>adharma</s>, the subtle body goes downward to animal realms and the like — animals, wild beasts, birds, reptiles, and plants — fivefold, ending with the stationary. There, <s>adharma</s> is the cause; downward movement is the result. And what else — through knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), there is final liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). That knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles) — through that knowledge, the subtle body is dissolved. The supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) attains liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), goes to <s>mokṣa</s> — this is the meaning. Therefore knowledge is the cause; liberation is the result. And another thing — from the opposite [of knowledge], bondage is held to occur. The opposite of what? The opposite of knowledge is ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>); through that ignorance, one thinks 'I am handsome, I am fortunate, I am the enjoyer.' Through that ignorance, one binds oneself in human, animal, and divine [births]. One does not attain liberation — this is the meaning. Therefore ignorance is the cause; bondage is the result. And that bondage is threefold: <s>prakṛtibandha</s> (bondage to <s>Prakṛti</s>), <s>vaikārikabandha</s> (bondage to modifications), and <s>dakṣiṇābandha</s> (bondage to merit). Of these, <s>prakṛtibandha</s> is the self-identification with the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (productive principles) as being the supreme. <s>Vaikārikabandha</s> is the conviction that the stations of <s>Brahmā</s> and the like are the highest good. <s>Dakṣiṇābandha</s> is caused by the giving of cows and the like, and by sacrificial worship. Thus the fourfold cause-and-result [relationship] has been explained. // <s>SkMv</s> 44 //

children.text: anyad apy evaṃvidham ucyate caturdhā ---
children.translated_text: Another fourfold [classification] of this kind is stated:

children.text: vairāgyāt prakṛtilayaḥ saṃsāro rājasād bhavati rāgāt /
children.translated_text: From dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s> (<s>prakṛtilaya</s>); from attachment (<s>rāga</s>), which is <s>rājasa</s>, transmigration (<s>saṃsāra</s>) occurs;

children.text: aiśvaryād avighāto viparyayāt tadviparyāsaḥ // ISk_45 //
children.translated_text: From sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), non-obstruction; from its opposite, the reverse. // <s>ISk</s> 45 //

children.text: yathā kasyacid vairāgyam asti | (jitendriyo viṣayebhyo virakto na yamaniyamaparaḥ kevalam) na tu jñānam asti guṇapuruṣāntarākhyam | tenājñānena vairāgyapūrveṇa nāsti mokṣaḥ | kevalam aṣṭāsu prakṛtiṣu layo bhavati pradhānabuddhyahaṅkāratanmātreṣu | tatra līnam ātmānaṃ muktam ity avagacchati bhūyaḥ saṃsaraṇakāle saṃsarati triṣu lokeṣu śarīrotpattir bhavati | tatra vairāgyaṃ nimittaṃ prakṛtilayo naimittikaḥ | kiṃ cānyat --- saṃsāro rājasād bhavati rāgāt | yo 'yaṃ rājaso rāgo 'vairāgyaṃ yajñaṃ karoti, dānaṃ dadāti, amunāmuṣmin loke sukhaṃ me bhāvīti | tena rāgeṇa saṃsāro bhavati | brahmādisthāneṣu janma bhavati | tatra rāgo nimittaṃ saṃsāro naimittikaḥ | kiṃ cānyat --- aiśvaryād avighātaḥ yat pūrvam aiśvaryam aṇimādikam aṣṭavidhaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ tasmād aiśvaryāt prārthitānām avighāto bhavati na muktiḥ | avighāto 'skhalanam | viparyayāt tadviparyāsaḥ | viparyayād anaiśvaryāt tadviparyāsaḥ prārthitānām aprāptir ity arthaḥ | tatrānaiśvaryaṃ nimittam | prārthitasyāprāptilakṣaṇo viparyāso naimittikaḥ | evaṃ ṣoḍaśako nityanaimittikaprasaṅgo vyākhyātaḥ | prakṛtilayaḥ prakṛtibandha ity ucyate | yajñādibhir dakṣiṇābandha ity ucyate | aiśvaryādinimitto bhogo vaikārika ity ucyate // SkMv_45 //
children.translated_text: Suppose someone has dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) — his senses are conquered, he is dispassionate toward objects, yet is not devoted to <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> — but does not have the knowledge called 'discrimination between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>.' Through that ignorance, accompanied by dispassion, there is no liberation. Only dissolution (<s>laya</s>) into the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> occurs — into <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, and the <s>Tanmātras</s>. There, he considers his dissolved self as liberated; [but] at the time of re-creation, he transmigrates again — birth in a body occurs in the three worlds. There, dispassion is the cause; dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s> is the result. And what else — from <s>rājasa</s> (passionate) attachment, transmigration occurs. This passionate attachment (<s>rāga</s>), which is non-dispassion — [thinking] 'by performing sacrifice, by giving gifts, I shall have happiness in such-and-such a world' — through that attachment, <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) occurs. Birth occurs in the stations of <s>Brahmā</s> and the like. There, attachment is the cause; transmigration is the result. And what else — from sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), non-obstruction: that eightfold sovereignty beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) previously described — from that sovereignty, non-obstruction of [one's] desires occurs, but not liberation. Non-obstruction means non-stumbling. From the opposite, the reverse: from the opposite — from non-sovereignty (<s>anaiśvarya</s>) — the reverse, meaning the non-attainment of desires — this is the meaning. There, non-sovereignty is the cause; the reverse, characterized by non-attainment of desires, is the result. Thus the sixteenfold perpetual cause-result connection has been explained. Dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s> is called <s>prakṛtibandha</s> (bondage to <s>Prakṛti</s>). [Bondage] caused by sacrifices and the like is called <s>dakṣiṇābandha</s> (bondage to merit). Enjoyment caused by sovereignty and the like is called <s>vaikārika</s> (modification-based). // <s>SkMv</s> 45 //

children.text: nanu nimittanaimittikaprasaṅgaḥ kimātmaka iti? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Now, what is the nature of this cause-result connection? This is answered:

children.text: eṣa pratyayasargo viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhyākhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the intellectual creation (<s>pratyayasarga</s>), called error (<s>viparyaya</s>), incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>), contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), and attainment (<s>siddhi</s>);

children.text: guṇavaiṣamyavimardena tasya bhedās tu pañcāśat // ISk_46 //
children.translated_text: Through the clash of the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s>, its divisions are fifty. // <s>ISk</s> 46 //

children.text: eṣa iti | āryādvayena ṣoḍaśavidho naimittikaḥ sarga uktaḥ | pratyayasarga ucyate | pratyayād buddher utpanno yasmāt tasmāt pratyayasarga ity ucyate | uktaṃ hi purastāt "adhyavasāyo buddhiḥ" ityādi | so 'yaṃ pratyayasargo bhūyaś caturdhā bhidyate | yasmād āha --- viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhyākhyaḥ | saṃśayabuddhir viparyayaḥ sthāṇur ayaṃ puruṣo veti | bhūyo 'pi sthāṇuṃ prasamīkṣya na śaknoty antaraṃ gantum evam asyāśaktir utpannā | tatas tṛtīyaḥ tam eva sthāṇuṃ(p.46) jñātuṃ saṃśayituṃ vā necchati kim anenāsmākam ity eṣā tuṣṭiḥ | bhūyaś caturtho (dṛṣṭe yas tasmin) sthāṇvādirūḍhāṃ vallīṃ paśyati śakuniṃ vā | tato 'sya niścaya utpadyate sthāṇur ayam ity eṣā siddhiḥ | evam eṣa pratyayasargo bhinnaś caturdhā viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhyākhyaḥ | tasya caturvidhapratyayasargasya guṇavaiṣamyavimardena pañcāśat bhedā bhavanti | sattvarajastamāṃsi trayo guṇās teṣāṃ vaiṣamyaṃ tadvimardena | yadā sattvam udriktaṃ tadā rajastamasī gauṇe | yathādityodayān nakṣatratejaso gauṇatvam | evaṃ yadā rajasā sattvatamasī, tamasā sattvarajasī gauṇe tadā tadvimardo bhavati | tena vimardena tasya caturvidhasya pratyayasargasya pañcāśad bhedā bhavanti // SkMv_46 //
children.translated_text: 'This' — by means of two verses, the sixteenfold resultant creation has been stated. It is called the intellectual creation (<s>pratyayasarga</s>). Since it arises from the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), it is called <s>pratyayasarga</s>. For it was previously stated: 'Determination is <s>buddhi</s>' and so on. This intellectual creation is further divided fourfold. As he says: 'called error, incapacity, contentment, and attainment.' Doubt-cognition is error (<s>viparyaya</s>) — 'Is this a post or a person?' Then, examining the post again, one is unable to ascertain the difference — thus one's incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>) has arisen. Then, a third [person] does not wish to know or doubt that very post — 'What does this matter to us?' — this is contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>). Then a fourth, having seen a creeper growing on that post, or a bird [perched upon it], arrives at certainty: 'This is a post' — this is attainment (<s>siddhi</s>). Thus this intellectual creation is divided fourfold, called error, incapacity, contentment, and attainment. Of this fourfold intellectual creation, through the clash of the disequilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s>, there are fifty divisions. The three <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — their disequilibrium and its clash: when <s>sattva</s> is predominant, then <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> become secondary. Just as at sunrise the radiance of the stars becomes secondary. Similarly, when <s>rajas</s> [overpowers] <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>, or when <s>tamas</s> [overpowers] <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s> — then that clash occurs. Through that clash, there are fifty divisions of the fourfold intellectual creation. // <s>SkMv</s> 46 //

children.text: tān āha ---
children.translated_text: He states those [divisions]:

children.text: pañca viparyayabhedā bhavanty aśakteś ca karaṇavaikalyāt /
children.translated_text: There are five divisions of error (<s>viparyaya</s>); and of incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>), due to deficiency of the sense-organs,

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśatibhedā tuṣṭir navadhāṣṭadhā siddhiḥ // ISk_47 //
children.translated_text: Twenty-eight divisions; contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) is ninefold; attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) is eightfold. // <s>ISk</s> 47 //

children.text: sugamam // SkMv_47 //
children.translated_text: This is easy to understand. // <s>SkMv</s> 47 //

children.text: viparyayasya ca tamo moho mahāmohas tāmisro 'ndhatāmisra iti pañca bhedāḥ | teṣāṃ bhedāntarāṇy āha ---
children.translated_text: And the five divisions of error (<s>viparyaya</s>) are: <s>tamas</s> (darkness), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom), and <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness). Their sub-divisions are stated:

children.text: bhedas tamaso 'ṣṭavidho mohasya ca daśavidho mahāmohaḥ /
children.translated_text: The division of <s>tamas</s> is eightfold; <s>moha</s> (delusion) is tenfold; <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion)

children.text: tāmisro 'ṣṭādaśadhā tathā bhavaty andhatāmisraḥ // ISk_48 //
children.translated_text: Is eighteenfold; and likewise <s>tāmisra</s> (gloom) and <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness) [together are eighteen]. // <s>ISk</s> 48 //

children.text: tamasas taqavad aṣṭavidhā prakṛtiḥ | tadvastu malayatīti tamaḥ | tasya param aṣṭāsu prakṛtiṣu layo bhavati | tad yathā pradhānaṃ buddhir ahaṅkāraḥ pañcatanmātrāṇīty eteṣu | tatra līnam ātmānaṃ mukto 'ham iti manyate | sa ca tasya viparyayaḥ | evaṃ tamaso 'ṣṭadhā bhedaḥ | mohasya ca aṣṭavidha evety arthaḥ | yattadaṇimādyaṣṭavidham aiśvaryam uktaṃ tasmin saktā brahmādayo devatā na mokṣapadam icchanti | tasyaiśvaryasya śubhakarmaṇopāttasya kṣaye punaḥ saṃsaranti | ayam aṣṭavidho mohasyāpi bhedaḥ | mahāmohasya daśavidho bhedaḥ | devānāṃ śabdādayaḥ pañcatanmātrākhyā viṣayā aviśeṣāḥ kevalānandarūpā nirupādhidugdhavac chāntādisañjātasukhādivirahitā ye bhavanti svargaprāptau | evaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ bhautikaśarīratayā sukhaduḥkhamohasampannāḥ śāntaghoramūḍhā bhavantīty eṣa daśavidho mahāmohaḥ | tad eteṣu daśasu brahmendrādayo devā manuṣyāś(p.47) ca tiryagyonyāsaktāś ca dṛśyante | tena hi viṣayebhyaḥ param astīti mūḍhavijñānās tadāsaktyā guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhirūpaṃ nityaniratiśayasukhābhivyaktaye jñānāvabodhaṃ na kurvantīty eṣa mahāmohaḥ | tenāmī te muktiṃ na bhajante | tāmisro 'ṣṭādaśadheti | devamanuṣyāṇāṃ daśa viṣayāḥ prāg abhihitā aviśeṣasaviśeṣatayā | aṇimādyaiśvaryaṃ cāṣṭaguṇam evam aṣṭādaśadhā bhavati | tebhyaḥ kenacid vaiguṇyenāprāptyābhihitasya yaḥ krodhaḥ sa tāmisra ity ucyate | tathā aṣṭādaśadhā cety arthaḥ | andhatāmisro 'pi bhavati tatsaṅkhya eva | tathā evam aṣṭādaśadhātrāpi | teṣu ca maraṇatrāsād duḥkham utpadyate | aiśvarye vidyamāna aiśvaryaṃ parityajya mṛtyunā hriyamāṇasya gacchāmīti saṅkalpayato yas trāsaḥ so 'ndhatāmisra ity ucyate daśa viṣayānaiśvaryaṃ prāpyāpi bhoktuṃ na labhate 'ntarāle 'pi mriyata iti yāvat | evam amī viparyayasya tamaḥprabhṛtayaḥ pañca bhedā vibhidyamānā dviṣaṣṭibhedāḥ sañjātāḥ | ata ūrdhvam aśakter aṣṭāviṃśatibhedān vakṣyāmaḥ // SkMv_48 //
children.translated_text: The eightfold <s>prakṛtilaya</s> (dissolution into nature) corresponds to <s>tamas</s>. That reality into which one dissolves is <s>tamas</s>. Its ultimate dissolution occurs in the eight <s>prakṛtis</s>. These are: <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense), and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). The self that is dissolved therein, [though seemingly] liberated...

children.text: ekādaśendriyavadhāḥ saha buddhivadhair aśaktir uddiṣṭā /
children.translated_text: The impairments of the eleven sense-organs, together with the impairments of <s>buddhi</s>, are designated as incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>);

children.text: saptadaśa vadhā buddher viparyayāt tuṣṭisiddhīnām // ISk_49 //
children.translated_text: Seventeen impairments of <s>buddhi</s> [are derived] from the opposites of contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) and attainment (<s>siddhi</s>). (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 49)

children.text: ekādaśendriyavadhāḥ āndhyabādhiryaghrānapākajaḍatvakuṣṭhatvamūkatvakuṇitvapaṅgutvagudāvartaklaibyonmādā ity ekādaśendriyavadhāḥ | indriyāṇāṃ svaviṣayagrahaṇāsāmarthyaṃ vadha iva vadhaḥ | yatheha loke kaścid devadatto yajñadattam āhūya abravīt --- bho duḥkhito 'smi kiṃ karavāṇīti | sa tenoktaḥ sāṅkhyajñānādhigamaṃ kuruṣva duḥkhāntamokṣaṃ prāpsyasīti | evam ukto 'sāv āha --- nāham etad abhyāsaṃ kartum alam | bādhiryāt guruvacanaṃ na śṛṇomi, śuśrūṣāyām asamartho 'smi | āndhyakuṇitvapaṅgutvādidoṣāśrayatvāt kuto mama jñānādhigama iti | evam evāndhyamūkatvonmādāda indriyopaghātā vidyāgrahaṇe asamarthā boddhavyāḥ | evam ete ekādaśendriyavadhā aśaktir ucyante | kiñ ca --- saha buddhivadhair iti | buddher vadhā buddhivadhās taiḥ saha | ke te buddhivadhāḥ? saptadaśasaṅkhyāḥ | te ca saptadaśāpi --- nava tuṣṭibhedā aṣṭau siddhayaḥ | tannirūpaṇaprastāve vyākhyāsyāmaḥ // SkMv_49 //
children.translated_text: The eleven impairments of the sense-organs are: blindness, deafness, loss of smell, skin disease, numbness, leprosy, dumbness, lameness of the hand, lameness of the legs, intestinal obstruction, impotence, and madness — these are the eleven impairments of the sense-organs. The incapacity of the organs to grasp their respective objects is 'impairment' — like [actual] death. Just as in this world...

children.text: tatra navadhā tuṣṭim āha ---
children.translated_text: There, the ninefold contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) is stated —

children.text: ādhyātmikyaś catasraḥ prakṛtyupādānakālabhāgyākhyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The four internal [contentments] are named <s>prakṛti</s> (nature), <s>upādāna</s> (acquisition), <s>kāla</s> (time), and <s>bhāgya</s> (fortune);

children.text: bāhyā viṣayoparamāt pañca nava ca tuṣṭayo 'bhihitāḥ // ISk_50 //
children.translated_text: The five external ones arise from cessation regarding objects — thus nine contentments are declared. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 50)

children.text: ātmany adhikṛtya pravartante tāś catasras tuṣṭayaḥ | prakṛtituṣṭir upādānatuṣṭiḥ kālatuṣṭiḥ bhāgyatuṣṭiś ceti | yathā kaścit prakṛtimātraṃ vetti, na tu jānīte saguṇāguṇatvanityānityatvacetanācetanatvasarvagatatvadharmān asyāḥ kevalaṃ prakṛtyastitvamātrajñānenāhaṃ jānāmīti tuṣṭaḥ pravrajitas tasya nāsti mokṣaḥ | eṣā prakṛtituṣṭiḥ | kaścit tridaṇḍakuṇḍikākṣamālākṛṣṇājinopādānamātreṇaivāhaṃ mukta ity abhimānī brūte | tena mama mokṣo bhāvīti | etāvanmātreṇa tuṣṭo jñānādhigame na pravartate | tasyāpi na mokṣa ity eṣā upādānatuṣṭiḥ | kaścid evaṃ brūte kālena svayaṃ mokṣo bhāvī kiṃ tattvavijñāneneti | jñāne pravṛttyaiva tuṣṭaḥ | tasyāpi na mokṣa iti kālatuṣṭiḥ | kaścid eva mahābhāgyenaiva mukto bhavati | tasmāj jñānam asādhakaṃ mukteḥ syād iti tāvatā tuṣṭaḥ tasya na mokṣa eṣā bhāgyatuṣṭiḥ | evam etā ātmany adhikṛtya jāyante ity ādhyātmikyaś catasras tuṣṭayaḥ | bāhyās tu pañca tuṣṭayaḥ | pañcānāṃ viṣayāṇām uparamād bhavanti, arjanarakṣaṇakṣayātṛptihiṃsādoṣān bhāvayataḥ pañca | evam ubhayatra nava tuṣṭayaḥ | tatrārjanaṃ nāma viṣayāṇāṃ tadarthaṃ kṛṣipāśupālyādivyavasāyaduḥkham avadhārya tebhya evoparatas tuṣṭiṃ labhate | eṣā pañcamī tuṣṭiḥ | arjitānām api rājacaurādibhyo duḥkhaṃ viṣayāṇāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ kartuṃ tasmān na viṣayaiḥ kāryam ity uparatas tuṣṭiṃ labhate, sā ṣaṣṭhī tuṣṭiḥ | rakṣaṇe 'pi kṛta upabhujyamānās te kṣīyanta iti na taiḥ kāryam ity uparatas tuṣṭiṃ labhate, eṣā saptamī | tathārjanakṣayādipratīkārair api kṛtair nāstītīndriyāṇāṃ vaitṛṣṇyam, tasmān na taiḥ kāryam ity uparatasyāṣṭamī tuṣṭiḥ | proktānāṃ pratīkāre kṛte 'py arjanādipravṛttena hiṃsām antareṇa bhūtoparodhaṃ vināmī na prāpyante tasmān na taiḥ kāryam ity uparataḥ tuṣṭiṃ labhate | eṣā navāmī tuṣṭiḥ | evam etāḥ pañca bāhyās tuṣṭayaḥ | ubhayaṃ nava bhavanti | (evam etābhis tuṣṭibhir jñānaṃ vinā mokṣo 'stīti kevalena vairāgyeṇa tuṣṭaḥ |) āsāṃ navānām api tuṣṭīnāṃ granthāntare saṃjñāntarāṇi | tad yathā --- (p.49) ambhaḥ salilam ogho vṛṣṭiḥ tāraṃ sutāraṃ sunetraṃ sumarīcam uttamāmbhasikam iti | āsāṃ viparītā atuṣṭayo 'nambha ityādyāḥ | evaṃ tuṣṭyatuṣṭayo vyākhyātāḥ // SkMv_50 //
children.translated_text: Those four contentments operate with reference to the self. They are: contentment with [mere knowledge of] <s>Prakṛti</s>, contentment with acquisition, contentment with time, and contentment with fortune. For example, someone knows <s>Prakṛti</s> merely [as a concept], but does not know its possession or absence of <s>guṇas</s>, its eternality or non-eternality, its consciousness or unconsciousness...

children.text: idānīṃ siddhayo vyākhyāyante ---
children.translated_text: Now the attainments (<s>siddhis</s>) are explained —

children.text: ūhaḥ śabdo 'dhyayanaṃ duḥkhavighātatrayaṃ suhṛtprāptiḥ /
children.translated_text: Reasoning (<s>ūha</s>), verbal instruction (<s>śabda</s>), study (<s>adhyayana</s>), the removal of the three kinds of suffering, the attainment of friends,

children.text: dānaṃ ca siddhayo 'ṣṭau siddheḥ pūrvo 'ṅkuśas trividhaḥ // ISk_51 //
children.translated_text: And generosity (<s>dāna</s>) — these are the eight <s>siddhis</s> (attainments). The threefold obstacle (<s>aṅkuśa</s>) is prior to [these] attainments. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 51)
