children.text: tatra ūho nāma yathā kaścic cintayati, kiṃ paraṃ yāthātmyam, kiṃ niḥśreyasam, kiṃ kṛtvā sukhaṃ prāpyate | evam asya cintayato jñānam utpadyate svataḥ śāstrato guruto vā | yat pradhānabuddhyahaṅkāratanmātrendriyabhūtāny anyāni, aham anya iti tato mokṣaṃ gacchati | eṣā ūhasiddhiḥ prathamā | caurasādhutadanugāmisvāmipathikasaṃyogādivat | prakṛtipuruṣaśiṣyagurukramajñānam | tad yathā grāmam ācchidya caurā yānti | tatsārthamadhye sādhur eko gacchati | tadanugāmī ca svāmī | caturthaḥ pathikas tadabhijñaḥ | pathikacauramadhye sādhur api cauraguṇāspṛṣṭo 'pi tadanugāminā cauratayā pratītas tādṛggaṇanāyāṃ (pratītaḥ) tadabhijñena pathikena svāmī sambodhito yad ahaṃ sarvaṃ jānāmi, amī caurā ayaṃ sādhur eva tatsārthānuvartīti | evaṃ caurasthānīyo buddhyahaṅkāratanmātrendriyabhūtasamavāyaḥ, sādhusthānīyaś ca puruṣaḥ, tadanugāmisthānīyaḥ śiṣyo, bhedena bodhyāḥ | pathikasthānīyo guruḥ | tasmāj jñānaṃ pratīkatrayeṇaivāvagamyate --- gurutaḥ śāstrataḥ, svata ity ūhasiddhiḥ prathamoktā | śabdo nāma yathā kasyacit paṭhataḥ (tam asya janaṃ) śabdaṃ śrutvānyat pradhānam anyo 'ham iti tanmārgapravṛttiprabuddho mokṣaṃ gacchati | evam eṣā dvitīyā siddhiḥ śabdata utpannā | kaścid gurūpāsanayā tato 'dhītyāvagamya sakalaṃ jñānam āpnoti, tṛtīyādhyayanasiddhiḥ sāṅkhyajñānam adhītya sañjātā | evam etās tisraḥ siddhayaḥ | śeṣā vyākhyāyante | duḥkhavighātatrayam iti | yathā kaścid ādāv abhihitādhyātmikādiduḥkhatrayeṇābhibhūto 'sya pratīkārāyohaṃ śabdam adhyayanaṃ vā pratipadya jñānam adhigamya mokṣaṃ yātīti duḥkhavighātāya yatrohāditrayam adhikurute tad api siddhitrayam | evaṃ ṣaṭ siddhayaḥ | kaścid durmedhā guroḥ sakāśān nāvadhārayati | tat kenacit pratyupakārānapekṣeṇa suhṛdā tasmāt saṃsārakūpād ujjihīrṣuṇā tadanukūlatayā kṛpāvatā sugamavacobhir vairāgyapūrvakaṃ guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhirūpaṃ sāṅkhyajñānam upadiśatā samuddhṛtam ālokyāha, (p.50) bhagavān śāstrakāraḥ --- suhṛtprāptir iti | te hi suhṛdas tathopadiśanti suhṛttayā yathā pāṣāṇo 'py avabudhyate | uktaṃ ca ---
"eṣā āturacittānāṃ mātrāsparśecchayā vibhuḥ /
bhavasindhuplavo dṛṣṭo yad ācāryānuvartanam" //
(bhāgavatapurāṇa 1 |6 |35)

eṣā saptamī siddhiḥ | kaścid āvāhanasaṃvāhanabhikṣāpātravastracchatrakamaṇḍaluprabhṛtidānena gurūn ārādhya sāṅkhyam adhigamya mokṣaṃ gacchatīty eṣāṣṭamī siddhir dānādibhir upāyair niṣpannā | āsām aṣṭānāṃ pūrvavannāmāntarāṇi | tāraṃ sutāraṃ tāratāraṃ pramodaṃ pramuditaṃ mohanaṃ ramyakaṃ sadāpramuditam iti | viparītā asiddhayaḥ | tad yathā atāram ityādyāḥ | tataś ca ekādaśendriyavadhāḥ, navānāṃ tuṣṭīnāṃ viparyayāḥ prakṛtyupādānakālabhāgyākhyānāṃ pañcaviṣayoparamatuṣṭīnāṃ ca | aṣṭānāṃ siddhīnāṃ viparyayā anūhādayaḥ | saptadaśa vadhā buddher evam ekādaśa saptadaśa cāṣṭāviṃśatibhedā aśakter abhidhīyante | evaṃ viparyayāśaktituṣṭisiddhīnām uddeśaḥ kṛta iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | siddheḥ pūrvo 'ṅkuśas trividhaḥ | yā ūhādyāṣṭadhā siddhis tasyā pūrvo viparyayāśaktituṣṭirūpo 'ṅkuśo niyāmakaḥ | trividhas triprakāra ity arthaḥ | yathāṅkuśena gṛhīto gajo vaśyo bhavati | evaṃ viparyayāśaktituṣṭirūpaṃ trividhaṃ pratyayasargaṃ hitvā siddhiḥ saṃsevyā, siddhes tattvajñānaṃ, tasmāc ca mokṣa iti tātparyam // SkMv_51 //

atrāha --- bhagavatā uktaṃ pūrvasyām āryāyāṃ bhāvair adhivāsitaṃ liṅgaṃ saṃsarati | tatra kiṃ liṅgaṃ pūrvotpannam āhosvit bhāvā ity atrocyate --- liṅgaṃ tāvat sūkṣmaṃ tānmātrikaṃ śarīram anādikālotpannaṃ trayodaśavidhena karaṇena saṃyuktaṃ bhāvair adhivāsitaṃ saṃsarati | karaṇāni buddhyahaṅkāramanobuddhikarmākhyāni trayodaśa | evaṃ trayodaśavidhakaraṇam āśritya sūkṣmaśarīraṃ tānmātrikaṃ saṃsarati | śarīraṃ karaṇāni caitalliṅgam ity atrocyate | bhāvair adhivāsitam iti bhāvā dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryāṇi catvāraḥ sāttvikāḥ | viparītās tāmasāḥ | evam aṣṭau bhāvāḥ | tatra sandehaḥ | kiṃ liṅgaṃ pūrvotpannam, utasvid bhāvā iti | ucyate ---
na vinā bhāvair liṅgaṃ na vinā liṅgena bhāvanirvṛttiḥ /
liṅgākhyo bhāvākhyas tasmād bhavati dvidhā sargaḥ // ISk_52 //

liṅgena vinā bhāvo na bhavati bhāvaiś ca vinā liṅgaṃ na bhavati | yathāgninā vinā noṣṇatvam uṣṇatvaṃ vinā nāgniḥ | evam etayor liṅgabhāvayor yugapadutpattiḥ, goviṣāṇavat, kumārīstanavat | yatra liṅgaṃ tatra bhāvā yatra bhāvās tatra liṅgam | tasmād ucyate --- liṅgākhyo bhāvākhyaḥ | liṅgena ākhyāyate sa liṅgākhyaḥ | bhāvair ākhyāyata iti bhāvākhyaḥ | tasmād dvidhā sargo bhavati jāyate // SkMv_52 //
atrāha --- kiṃ dvividha eva sargaḥ kiṃ tasmād anyas tṛtīyo 'py asti iti | atrocyate ---
aṣṭavikalpo daivas tairyagyonaś ca pañcadhā bhavati /
mānuṣyaś caikavidhaḥ samāsato bhautikaḥ sargaḥ // ISk_53 //

aṣṭavikalpo daiva iti | tad yathā --- brāhmaṃ prājāpatyam aindraṃ paitraṃ gāndharvaṃ yākṣaṃ rākṣasaṃ paiśācam ity evam aṣṭavidho devasargaḥ | tairyagyonaś ca pañcadhā bhavati | atra tulyaliṅgatvād bhavati paśupakṣimṛgasarīsṛpasthāvarāntaś ceti | mānuṣya ekavidhas tulyaliṅgatvād brāhmaṇāadicāṇḍālāntaḥ | samāsataḥ saṅkṣepeṇa trividho 'yaṃ bhūtamayaḥ sargaḥ | evaṃ caturdaśavidhaḥ // SkMv_53 //
atrāha --- eteṣu triṣu sthāneṣu kataro guṇa utkaṭatvena vartate ---
ūrdhvaṃ sattvaviśālas tamoviśālaś ca mūlataḥ sargaḥ /
madhye rajoviśālo brahmādistambaparyantaḥ // ISk_54 //

ūrdhvaṃ sattvaviśāla iti | brahmādipiśācānto yo 'ṣṭavidhaḥ sargaḥ | asau sattvabahulaḥ | yasmāt teṣu sattvam utkaṭatvena vartate | tatrāpi rajastamasī staḥ kiṃ tu sattvasyodriktatā | tasmāt sukhaprāyā devāḥ | tamoviśālaś ca mūlataḥ | paśvādiṣu tamasa udrekāt paśvādisthāvaraparyanto yasmāt teṣu tama utkaṭatvena vartate tatrāpi gauṇatayā sattvarajasī staḥ | tasmāt te tamobahulāḥ | madhye rajoviśālaḥ | tatrāpi sattvatamasī staḥ | kiṃ tu raja utkaṭatvena vartate | tasmāt te duḥkhaprāyā manuṣyāḥ | brahmādistambaparyantaḥ | caturvidha eṣa svedajāṇḍajādinā bhūtasargaḥ // SkMv_54 //

atrāha --- bhūtasarga utpanno bhāvasargaḥ sampanno liṅgasargaḥ sampanna iti yatra sargāḥ prādhānikā iti pradhānakāryaṃ samāptam iti | utpannās trayo lokāḥ pradhānaṃ coparatam utpādya lokān iti teṣu devamanuṣyatiryagyonigateṣu duḥkhaṃ ko 'nubhavati | kiṃ caturviṃśatitamaṃ pradhānam, āhosvit mahadāditrayoviṃśatikam, utasvit puruṣa iti? atrocyate ---
atra jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpnoti cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here [in the three worlds], the conscious <s>Puruṣa</s> experiences suffering caused by old age and death;

children.text: liṅgasyāvinivṛttes tasmād duḥkhaṃ samāsena // ISk_55 //
children.translated_text: Because of the non-cessation of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body), suffering [persists] in brief. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 55)

children.text: atra triṣu lokeṣv iti | devaloke, manuṣyaloke, tiryagyonau ca jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpnoti cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ | tatra jarākṛtaṃ valīpalitair abhibhūtaḥ kāsaśvāsaiḥ parigṛhīto yaṣṭiviṣṭambhagāmī putrasnuṣādyabhibhūto yad duḥkham anubhavati taj jarākṛtam | maraṇakṛtam iti | aṣṭavidham aiśvaryam asti yat prāg abhihitam aṇimādi, daśa viṣayāḥ santi | devānāṃ pañcāviśeṣāḥ kevalasukharūpāḥ | manuṣyāṇāṃ saviśeṣās ta eva śabdādayaḥ sukhaduḥkhamohasampannāḥ | tanmaraṇapātāvasthāyāṃ yad duḥkham utpadyate tan maraṇakṛtam ity eva | evam etair duḥkhair antakāle ca janitaduḥkhāni sarvāṇi prāpnoti cetanaḥ puruṣa eva pradhānādīnām acetanatvāt | tasmāt tasyaiva vijñānitayā duḥkhaṃ na tu jaḍānāṃ pradhānādīnām | tarhi kiyantaṃ kālaṃ puruṣo duḥkham āpnoti | atrocyate --- liṅgasyāvinivṛtteḥ | yāvan mahadādiliṅgaṃ na nivartate tāvat kālaṃ puruṣo duḥkhabhoktā | tasmād duḥkhaṃ samāsena --- saṅkṣepeṇa prāpnoti cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ | yadā tu tat pratinivartate mahadādiliṅgaṃ jñānotpattyā tato mokṣaṃ prāpnoti | mokṣaṃ gatasya duḥkhaṃ nāsti | jñānena hi liṅgaṃ nivartate | yadā pratyekaṃ pradhānamahadahantanmātrendriyabhūtāny anyāni aham anya iti jñānaṃ tadā liṅgābhāvaḥ // SkMv_55 //
children.translated_text: 'Here in the three worlds' means: in the world of the gods, the human world, and the animal realm — the conscious <s>Puruṣa</s> experiences suffering caused by old age and death. Of these, the suffering caused by old age [is described]: overcome by wrinkles and grey hair, seized by coughing and labored breathing, walking supported by a staff, sons...

children.text: prakṛteḥ kiṃ nimittam ārabhya ity atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: For what purpose does <s>Prakṛti</s> begin [its activity]? This is answered —

children.text: ity eṣa prakṛtikṛto mahadādiviṣayabhūtaparyantaḥ /
children.translated_text: This [creation], made by <s>Prakṛti</s>, extending from <s>Mahat</s> and the rest to the gross elements,

children.text: pratipuruṣavimokṣārthaṃ svārtha iva parārtha ārambhaḥ // ISk_56 //
children.translated_text: Is undertaken for the liberation of each <s>Puruṣa</s> — [seemingly] for its own purpose, [but actually] for the other's purpose. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 56)

children.text: ity eṣa prakṛtikṛta iti | evamādir yaḥ pūrvam upavarṇito liṅgasargo mahadādibhūtaparyantaḥ, eṣa prakṛtikṛta iti | atrāha --- evaṃ liṅgasargaḥ pradhānena kimarthaṃ kṛta iti? atrocyate --- pratipuruṣavimokṣārtham | puruṣaṃ puruṣaṃ prati vimokṣas tadarthaṃ pratipuruṣavimokṣārtham | devalokagatānām, manuṣyalokagatānām, tiryagyonigatānāṃ ca mokṣārtham ity arthaḥ | svārtha iva parārtha ārambhaḥ | svakīyo 'rthaḥ svārthaḥ | ivopamāyām | yathā kaścit svārtham iva mitrārthaṃ karoti tathā svārtham iva pradhānaṃ puruṣārthaṃ karoti | sa cārtho dvividhaḥ | śabdādyupalabdhir ādir guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhir antaś ca | triṣu lokeṣu śabdādiviṣayaiḥ puruṣaṃ yojayati | ante ca guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhyā mokṣaṃ kurute // SkMv_56 //
children.translated_text: 'This is made by <s>Prakṛti</s>' — the creation of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) described earlier, from <s>Mahat</s> up to and including the elements — this is made by <s>Prakṛti</s>. Here a question is raised: for what purpose was the <s>liṅga</s>-creation made by <s>Pradhāna</s>? This is answered: for the liberation of each <s>Puruṣa</s>...

children.text: atrāha --- uktaṃ bhagavatā pradhānaṃ svārtham iva parārtham ārabhate | atha ca tvayā pradhānam acetanam uktaṃ tat kathaṃ pravartate | acetanānām api pravṛttir dṛṣṭā, nivṛttiś ca |
children.translated_text: Here a question is raised: the Blessed One stated that <s>Pradhāna</s> undertakes [activity] for the other's purpose as if it were its own. Yet you have said <s>Pradhāna</s> is unconscious. How then does it act? [We reply:] the activity of unconscious things is indeed observed, as is their cessation.

children.text: vatsavivṛddhinimittaṃ kṣīrasya yathā pravṛttir ajñasya /
children.translated_text: Just as the activity of unconscious milk is for the purpose of the calf's nourishment,

children.text: puruṣavimokṣanimittaṃ tathā pravṛttiḥ pradhānasya // ISk_57 //
children.translated_text: So too is the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s liberation. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 57)

children.text: yathā tṛṇodakaṃ gavā bhakṣitaṃ pītaṃ ca kṣīrabhāvena pariṇamati, vatsavṛddhiṃ karoti, puṣṭe vatse nivartate | evaṃ puruṣavimokṣanimittaṃ pradhānasyājñasya pravṛttiḥ // SkMv_57 //
children.translated_text: Just as grass and water eaten and drunk by a cow transform into milk, nourish the calf, and cease when the calf is nourished — so too is the activity of the unconscious <s>Pradhāna</s> for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s liberation.

children.text: autsukyanivṛttyarthaṃ yathā kriyāsu pravartate lokaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as people engage in activities for the purpose of removing their restless longing,

children.text: puruṣasya vimokṣārthaṃ pravartate tadvad avyaktam // ISk_58 //
children.translated_text: So too does the Unmanifest operate for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s liberation. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 58)

children.text: yathā loka iṣṭaviṣayautsukye sati tasya nivṛttyarthaṃ kriyāsu gamanāgamanāsu pravartate kṛtakāryo nivartate | tathāvyaktaṃ puruṣasya vimokṣārthaṃ śabdādibhogalakṣaṇaṃ guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhilakṣaṇaṃ dvividhaṃ puruṣārthaṃ kṛtvā nivartate // SkMv_58 //
children.translated_text: Just as people in the world, when restless longing for desired objects arises, engage in activities — going and coming — for its removal, and having accomplished their purpose, cease — so too does the Unmanifest, characterized by the enjoyment of sound and the rest, characterized by the discernment of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>...

children.text: kiñ cānyat ---
children.translated_text: And further —

children.text: raṅgasya darśayitvā nivartate nartakī yathā nṛtyāt /
children.translated_text: Just as a dancer, having displayed [her art] to the audience, withdraws from the dance,

children.text: puruṣasya tathātmānaṃ prakāśya vinivartate prakṛtiḥ // ISk_59 //
children.translated_text: So too does <s>Prakṛti</s>, having revealed herself to <s>Puruṣa</s>, withdraw. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 59)

children.text: yathā nartakī śṛṅgārādirasair hāvabhāvaiś ca nibaddhagītavāditranṛtyāni raṅgasya darśayitvā kṛtakāryā nṛtyān nivartate | evaṃ prakṛtir mahadahaṅkāratanmātrendriyabhūtabhāvena(p.54) devamānuṣatiryagrūpāsu yoniṣu sukhaduḥkhamohākṛtiḥ śāntaghoramūḍhaviṣayā satī ātmānaṃ puruṣasya prakāśya nivartate | tasyāṃ ca nivṛttāyām asau kevalaḥ puruṣo duḥkhatrayaṃ nānubhavati | yathā jalavāhakasya ghaṭābhāve tadādheyasyodakasyābhāvaḥ | tathā duḥkhābhāvaḥ | tato 'sau mokṣaṃ gacchati // SkMv_59 //
children.translated_text: Just as a dancer, having displayed to the audience dances bound with songs and instruments, along with the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) and other <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments), <s>hāvas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> (gestures and emotions), having accomplished her purpose, withdraws from the dance — so too <s>Prakṛti</s>, in the form of <s>Mahat</s>, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, <s>tanmātras</s>, sense-organs, and elements, in the forms of gods, humans, and animals...

children.text: atrāha --- yathā nartakī nṛtyādibhir upāyair ātmānaṃ prakāśya raṅgād vinivartate, evaṃ prakṛtiḥ puruṣasya kair upāyair ātmānaṃ prakāśya vinivartate? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here a question is raised: just as a dancer, having displayed herself by means of dance and other devices, withdraws from the stage — by what means does <s>Prakṛti</s>, having revealed herself to <s>Puruṣa</s>, withdraw? This is answered —

children.text: nānāvidhair upāyair upakāriṇy anupakāriṇaḥ puṃsaḥ /
children.translated_text: By various means, the benefactress [serves] the non-beneficent <s>Puruṣa</s>;

children.text: guṇavaty aguṇasya satas tasyārtham apārthakaṃ carati // ISk_60 //
children.translated_text: The one possessing <s>guṇas</s> acts for the purpose of him who is without <s>guṇas</s>, [yet acts] without purpose [for herself]. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 60)

children.text: nānāvidhair upāyaiḥ | śabdasparśādibhir upakartuṃ śīlam asyāḥ sā tathoktā | anupakāriṇaḥ puṃsaḥ | niṣkriyatvād iti yāvat | tasyopakāriṇī prakṛtis tasyopakṛtyāham anyā tvam anya iti nivartate (prakṛtiḥ) | kiṃ cānyat --- guṇavatī | sā sattvarajastamomayī | aguṇasya sataḥ | puṃsaḥ niṣkriyodāsīnāmūrtādilakṣaṇavattvāt | evam asya puṃso 'guṇasyāpi sataḥ (nityasya) seyaṃ guṇavatī artham apārthakaṃ carati | karoti | yathā kaścid anurakto mitrasuhṛttvam avalambya mitrārtham anuktam api pratyupakāram anapekṣya kurute | evaṃ pradhānaṃ puruṣasya dvividham api viṣayopalabdhimokṣātmakam arthaṃ kurute | pumān punaḥ pradhānasya kim api na pratyupakaroti | tat pradhānapuṃsoḥ śikhipicchavadekapakṣacitranyāyaḥ // SkMv_60 //
children.translated_text: 'By various means' — by sound, touch, and the rest. She whose nature it is to benefit — she is so designated. 'Of the non-beneficent <s>Puruṣa</s>' — because of his inactivity. <s>Prakṛti</s>, having benefited him, [realizing] 'I am one; you are another,' withdraws...

children.text: nivṛttā kiṃ karoty etad āha ---
children.translated_text: What does she do upon withdrawal? He states this —

children.text: prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ na kiñcid astīti me matir bhavati /
children.translated_text: There is nothing more delicate than <s>Prakṛti</s> — this is my considered view;

children.text: yā dṛṣṭāsmīti punar na darśanam upaiti puruṣasya // ISk_61 //
children.translated_text: She who [realizes] 'I have been seen' does not again come into the sight of <s>Puruṣa</s>. (<s>Sāṃkhyakārikā</s> 61)

children.text: prakṛtir api pradhānam api kurute | yatheha snuṣā vrīḍayā svagṛhāntaḥ praviśati ato bravīti iyaṃ viśiṣṭatareti | evam iyaṃ prakṛtiḥ sukumāratarā | tasmāt prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ nānyad astīti | evaṃ puruṣasya paramātmano 'pi matir utpannā | nāstīti me matir bhavati | mameti puruṣa ātmānaṃ bravīti | tatra sukumārataratvaṃ varṇayati īśvaraḥ kāraṇam iti kecid ācāryā bravate | uktaṃ ca ---
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s>, also called <s>Pradhāna</s>, acts [accordingly]. Just as a daughter-in-law, out of modesty, enters inside her own house — therefore he says 'she is most distinguished.' Thus this <s>Prakṛti</s> is most delicate. Therefore, there is nothing more delicate than <s>Prakṛti</s>. Thus <s>Puruṣa</s>...

children.text: "ajño jantur anīśo 'yam ātmanaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The ignorant creature, powerless over its own pleasure and pain,

children.text: īśvaraprerito gacchet svargaṃ narakam eva vā" //
children.translated_text: Impelled by the Lord, goes to heaven or indeed to hell.'

children.text: (mahābhārata 3 |31 |27)(p.55)
children.translated_text: (<s>Mahābhārata</s> 3.31.27) (p.55)

children.text: vedavādinaḥ punar itthaṃ kāraṇam āhuḥ | "puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam"(śvetāśvataropaniṣad 3 |15) ity ataḥ puruṣaṃ kāraṇam āhuḥ | apare svabhāvam āhuḥ | svabhāvaḥ kāraṇam iti | tathā hi ---
children.translated_text: The followers of the <s>Veda</s>, however, state the cause thus: '<s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this' (<s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s> 3.15) — therefore they declare <s>Puruṣa</s> to be the cause. Others declare <s>svabhāva</s> (inherent nature) [to be the cause]. 'Inherent nature is the cause' — for thus [it is said]:

children.text: "yena śuklīkṛtā haṃsāḥ śukāś ca haritīkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By whom the swans were made white, the parrots made green,

children.text: mayūrāś citritā yena sa no vṛttiṃ vidhāsyati" //
children.translated_text: And the peacocks made multicolored — he shall provide for our sustenance.'

children.text: (hitopadeśa 1 |183)
children.translated_text: (<s>Hitopadeśa</s> 1.183)

children.text: atra sāṅkhyā vadanti | īśvaraḥ kāraṇaṃ na bhavati | kasmāt, nirguṇatvāt | imāḥ saguṇāḥ prajāḥ | sattvarajastamāṃsi trayo guṇāḥ, te ca prajāsu santi | tāṃś ca guṇān dṛṣṭvā sādhayāmaḥ | prakṛter imāḥ samutpannāḥ prajāḥ | yad īśvaraḥ kāraṇaṃ syāt tato nirguṇād īśvarān nirguṇā eva prajāḥ syuḥ | na caivam | tasmād īśvaraḥ kāraṇaṃ na bhavati | evaṃ puruṣo 'pi draṣṭavyaḥ | svabhāvo nāma na kaścit padārtho 'sti | yataḥ prajānām utpattisaṅgatiḥ syāt | tasmād yo brūte svabhāvaḥ kāraṇam iti tan mithyā | kecit kālaṃ kāraṇatayā varṇayanti ---
children.translated_text: Here the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> say: <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is not the cause. Why? Because he is devoid of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). These beings possess <s>guṇas</s>. <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — these three <s>guṇas</s> exist in beings. And having observed those <s>guṇas</s>, we establish: these beings have arisen from <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). If <s>Īśvara</s> were the cause, then from that <s>Īśvara</s> who is devoid of <s>guṇas</s>, beings too would be devoid of <s>guṇas</s>. But this is not so. Therefore <s>Īśvara</s> is not the cause. <s>Puruṣa</s> should be considered in the same way. There is no entity called '<s>svabhāva</s>' (inherent nature) from which the origination of beings would be logically possible. Therefore, one who says '<s>svabhāva</s> is the cause' speaks falsely. Some describe <s>kāla</s> (time) as the cause:

children.text:
"kālaḥ sṛjati bhūtāni kālaḥ saṃharate prajāḥ /
(mahābhārata 3 |13 |70 |57)
kālaḥ supteṣu jāgarti tasmāt kālas tu kāraṇam" //
children.translated_text: 'Time creates beings; time destroys creatures; time is awake when [all] are asleep; therefore time is the cause.'

children.text: tad api sāṅkhyo nirākurute | kālo nāma na kaścit padārtho 'sti | vyaktam avyaktaṃ puruṣa iti traya eva padārthāḥ | tatra kālo 'ntarbhūtaḥ | evaṃ pradhānaṃ hitvā nāsty anyat kāraṇam | tatpradhānāvagamaṃ prati yadā puruṣasya samyagjñānam utpadyate tadā tena jñānena dṛṣṭā prakṛtiḥ puruṣasaṅgān nivartate | svairiṇīva puruṣeṇopalakṣitā | aye iyam asādhvī māṃ mohayati, tasmān na mamānayā kāryam itivat | tasyāṃ ca nivṛttāyāṃ mokṣaṃ gacchati | evam īśvarādīni akāraṇāni | sukumārataram ity etad vākyaśeṣaḥ kṛtaḥ | yasmāt sukumārataraṃ pradhānaṃ tasmād ucyate --- prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ na kiñcid astīti me matir bhavati | iti me puruṣasya | atrāha --- sā dṛṣṭā puruṣeṇa kathaṃ nivartate prakṛtiḥ | atrocyate --- yā dṛṣṭāsmīti punar na darśanam upaiti puruṣasya | yathā kācit kulastrī sādhvī svagṛhadvāri sthitā puruṣeṇa sahasaivāgatena dṛṣṭā sahasaivaṃ vrīḍamānā tvaritaṃ gṛhaṃ praviṣṭā sā evaṃ matvā dṛṣṭāham aneneti na punar darśanam upaiti puruṣasya | evaṃ prakṛtiḥ paramātmanā puruṣeṇa jñānacakṣuṣā dṛṣṭā savrīḍā kulastrīvan na punar darśanam upaiti puruṣasya | tasyāṃ ca nivṛttāyāṃ puruṣo mokṣaṃ gacchati // SkMv_61 //
children.translated_text: That too the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> refutes. There is no entity called 'time.' The manifest, the unmanifest, and <s>Puruṣa</s> — these are the only three categories. Time is included within them. Thus, apart from <s>Pradhāna</s>, there is no other cause. When, with regard to the understanding of that <s>Pradhāna</s>, right knowledge arises in <s>Puruṣa</s>, then <s>Prakṛti</s>, seen through that knowledge, desists from association with <s>Puruṣa</s> — like a wanton woman noticed by the man: 'Ah, this unchaste woman deceives me; therefore I have nothing to do with her!' — and thus. When she has withdrawn, he attains liberation. Thus <s>Īśvara</s> and the rest are not causes. 'More delicate' — this completes the sentence. Since <s>Pradhāna</s> is more delicate, therefore it is said: 'Nothing exists more delicate than <s>Prakṛti</s> — such is my conviction.' 'My' means <s>Puruṣa</s>'s. Here one asks: when <s>Prakṛti</s> is seen by <s>Puruṣa</s>, how does she withdraw? To this it is said: she who [knows] 'I have been seen' does not again come into the view of <s>Puruṣa</s>. Just as a certain virtuous woman from a good family, standing at her own doorway, suddenly seen by a man who has arrived unexpectedly, suddenly ashamed, hastily enters the house — having thought 'I have been seen by this one,' she does not again come into his view. Similarly, <s>Prakṛti</s>, seen by the supreme <s>Ātman</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, through the eye of knowledge, like a modest woman from a good family, does not again come into the view of <s>Puruṣa</s>. And when she has withdrawn, <s>Puruṣa</s> attains liberation. [SkMv 61]

children.text: atrāha --- loke śiṣṭā vadanti puruṣo baddhaḥ, puruṣo muktaḥ, puruṣaḥ saṃsarati | atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks: in the world, the learned say '<s>Puruṣa</s> is bound,' '<s>Puruṣa</s> is liberated,' '<s>Puruṣa</s> transmigrates.' To this it is said:

children.text: tasmān na badhyate nāpi mucyate nāpi saṃsarati kaścit /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, no one is bound, nor liberated, nor transmigrates;

children.text: saṃsarati badhyate mucyate ca nānāśrayā prakṛtiḥ // ISk_62 //
children.translated_text: It is <s>Prakṛti</s>, abiding in various substrata, that transmigrates, is bound, and is liberated.' [ISk 62]

children.text: puruṣo na badhyate sarvagatatvāt, avikāratvāt, niṣkriyatvāt, akartṛtvāt | yasmān na badhyate tasmān na mucyate | mukta eva saḥ | abaddhaḥ kuto mucyate | kasyābhuktena visūcī bhavati | na saṃsarati sarvagatatvāt | sarvagatasya bandhamokṣau kutaḥ | anadhigataprāpaṇārthaṃ saṃsaraṇam ity upadiśyate | tena ca sunipuṇaṃ sarvaṃ prāptam | puruṣaṃ na vidanti ye ta evaṃ vadanti | puruṣo baddhaḥ, puruṣo muktaḥ, puruṣaḥ saṃsarati | atrāha --- yadi puṃso bandhamokṣasaṃsaraṇāni na syuḥ tarhi kasya bhavanti | tad ucyate --- saṃsarati badhyate mucyate ca nānāśrayā prakṛtiḥ | prakṛtir ātmānaṃ badhnāti, mocayati, saṃsarati ca | yat tat sargādau sūkṣmaṃ śarīraṃ tānmātrikaṃ prāg uktaṃ trayodaśavidhena karaṇena saṃyuktaṃ trividhena bandhena baddhaṃ saṃsarati | sa ca bandhas trividhaḥ pūrvam ākhyātaḥ | tad eva sūkṣmaśarīram utpanne jñāne tridhā bandhān mucyate | tasmān mucyate badhyate saṃsarati nānāśrayā prakṛtiḥ | nānāśrayā devamanuṣyatiryakśarīrabhūtety arthaḥ | evaṃ yat pradhānaṃ tat sūkṣmaṃ śarīraṃ tat pradhānaṃ prakṛtir ity anarthāntaram | tatra yaḥ puṃso bandhamokṣasaṃsaraṇāni brūte sa mūḍhaḥ // SkMv_62 //
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> is not bound — because of being all-pervading, because of being unchanging, because of being inactive, and because of being a non-agent. Since he is not bound, therefore he is not liberated. He is already liberated. When one is unbound, how can one be liberated? Who gets dysentery from food not eaten? He does not transmigrate, because of being all-pervading. How can there be bondage and liberation for the all-pervading? Transmigration is taught for the purpose of arriving at what has not yet been attained. But he has already subtly attained everything. Those who do not know <s>Puruṣa</s> say thus: '<s>Puruṣa</s> is bound, <s>Puruṣa</s> is liberated, <s>Puruṣa</s> transmigrates.' Here one asks: if bondage, liberation, and transmigration do not belong to <s>Puruṣa</s>, then to whom do they belong? That is stated: it is <s>Prakṛti</s>, abiding in various substrata, that transmigrates, is bound, and is liberated. <s>Prakṛti</s> binds itself, liberates itself, and transmigrates. That subtle body (<s>sūkṣmaśarīra</s>), composed of <s>tanmātras</s> as previously described, conjoined with the thirteen-fold instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), bound by the threefold bondage, transmigrates at the beginning of creation. And that bondage is threefold, as was previously explained. That very subtle body, when knowledge arises, is freed from the threefold bondage. Therefore, <s>Prakṛti</s>, abiding in various substrata, is bound, is liberated, and transmigrates. 'Abiding in various substrata' means having become the bodies of gods, humans, and animals — that is the meaning. Thus, that which is <s>Pradhāna</s> is the subtle body; that <s>Pradhāna</s> is <s>Prakṛti</s> — there is no difference in meaning. One who speaks of bondage, liberation, and transmigration as belonging to <s>Puruṣa</s> is deluded. [SkMv 62]

children.text: atrāha --- sā prakṛtiḥ kair guṇair ātmānaṃ bandhayati, kair vā mocayatīti? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks: by which qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) does that <s>Prakṛti</s> bind herself, and by which does she liberate herself? To this it is said:

children.text: rūpaiḥ saptabhir evaṃ badhnāty ātmānam ātmanā prakṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'By seven forms does <s>Prakṛti</s> bind herself by herself;

children.text: saiva ca puruṣasyārthaṃ prati vimocayaty ekarūpeṇa // ISk_63 //
children.translated_text: and she herself liberates, for the sake of <s>Puruṣa</s>, by a single form.' [ISk 63]

children.text: saptabhī rūpair iyam evaṃ prakṛtir dharmādibhir vinā jñānam ātmanātmānaṃ badhnāti | saiva ca prakṛtiḥ guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhirūpaṃ prati, ekarūpeṇa jñānenātmānaṃ vimocayati // SkMv_63 //
children.translated_text: By seven forms — <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and the rest, excluding knowledge — does this <s>Prakṛti</s> bind herself by herself. And that very <s>Prakṛti</s>, for the sake of the [eighth] form, which is the apprehension of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, liberates herself by the single form of knowledge. [SkMv 63]

children.text: katham taj jñānam utpadyate ---
children.translated_text: How does that knowledge arise?

children.text: evaṃ tattvābhyāsān nāsmi na me nāham ity apariśeṣam /
children.translated_text: 'Thus, from the practice of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles), the knowledge arises: "I am not, nothing is mine, I do not exist" — complete,

children.text: aviparyayād viśuddhaṃ kevalam utpadyate jñānam // ISk_64 //
children.translated_text: free from error, pure, and absolute.' [ISk 64]

children.text: evam iti | yathā, etāni pañcaviṃśatitattvāni puruṣādyāni bhūtaparyantāni teṣām abhyāsas tattvābhyāsaḥ | abhyāsenaiva tattvadarśanam | tasmād abhyāsāt puruṣasya buddhir utpadyate | nāsmi tattvāni, na me tattvāni, nāhaṃ tattvānām, kiṃ tu prādhānikāny etāni | tasmāj jñānam utpadyata evamādi | apariśeṣaṃ niravaśeṣam ity arthaḥ | kiṃ cānyat (jñānaṃ yasmād āha) --- aviparyayāt | viparyayaḥ saṃśayas tadviparīto 'viparyayas tasmād aviparyayād asaṃśayād yathābhūtārthadarśanād viśuddham niravadyam avyāmiśraṃ kevalaṃ jñānam utpadyate prādurbhavati | kiṃ jñānam? guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhirūpam ity arthaḥ // SkMv_64 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus' — as follows: these twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>, beginning with <s>Puruṣa</s> and ending with the elements — the practice of them is <s>tattvābhyāsa</s> (practice of the principles). Through practice alone comes the vision of the <s>tattvas</s>. From that practice, the conviction arises in <s>Puruṣa</s>: 'I am not the <s>tattvas</s>; the <s>tattvas</s> are not mine; I do not belong to the <s>tattvas</s> — rather, these belong to <s>Pradhāna</s>.' Therefore, knowledge of this kind arises. 'Complete' (<s>apariśeṣa</s>) means without remainder — that is the meaning. And furthermore, the knowledge is: 'Free from error' (<s>aviparyaya</s>) — error is doubt; its opposite is freedom from error; from that freedom from error, from being free from doubt, from seeing the object as it really is, pure (<s>viśuddha</s>) — faultless, unmixed — absolute (<s>kevala</s>) knowledge arises, comes into being. What kind of knowledge? Having the form of the apprehension of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — that is the meaning. [SkMv 64]

children.text: atrāha --- tena jñānena puruṣaḥ kiṃ karoti | atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks: what does <s>Puruṣa</s> do with that knowledge? To this it is said:

children.text: tena nivṛttaprasavām arthavaśāt saptarūpavinivṛttām /
children.translated_text: 'With that [knowledge], <s>Puruṣa</s> sees <s>Prakṛti</s> — [now] with creative activity ceased, withdrawn from the seven forms due to having fulfilled its purpose —

children.text: prakṛtiṃ paśyati puruṣaḥ prekṣakavad avasthitaḥ svasthaḥ // ISk_65 //
children.translated_text: abiding like a spectator, self-established.' [ISk 65]

children.text: yathā kaścit prekṣako raṅgasthito gītavāditranṛtyādibhir vartamānāṃ nartakīṃ svastho nirvikalpaḥ paśyati | evaṃ puruṣa ātmakṛtena jñānena tāsu tāsv avasthāsu vartamānāṃ prakṛtiṃ paśyati --- iyaṃ sā prakṛtir yā sarvapurāṇam ātmānaṃ badhnāti | prekṣakavat prekṣakeṇa tulyaḥ svasthaḥ svasmin bhāve sthitaḥ | kiṃbhūtāṃ prakṛtim? nivṛttaprasavām | nivṛttabuddhyahaṅkārakāryām | arthavaśāt saptarūpavinivṛttām | nirvarttitobhayapuruṣaprayojanavaśād yaiḥ saptabhī rūpair dharmādibhir ātmānaṃ badhnāti tebhyo rūpebhyo vinivṛttām | yāvaj jñānacakṣuṣā dṛṣṭā prakṛtiḥ puruṣeṇa tathā ca pumān dṛṣṭaḥ // SkMv_65 //
children.translated_text: Just as a certain spectator, seated in the theater, self-possessed and free from conceptualization, watches a dancer who is performing through song, instrumental music, dancing, and the like — so <s>Puruṣa</s>, through the knowledge produced by his own [discriminative effort], sees <s>Prakṛti</s> as she operates in those various states: 'This is that <s>Prakṛti</s> who has bound the self from time immemorial.' 'Like a spectator' — equal to a spectator; 'self-established' — abiding in his own nature. What kind of <s>Prakṛti</s>? One whose creative activity has ceased — whose production of <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and their effects has stopped. Withdrawn from the seven forms due to having fulfilled its purpose — because the purpose of both [<s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s>] has been accomplished, she has withdrawn from those seven forms of <s>dharma</s> and the rest by which she binds herself. When <s>Prakṛti</s> is seen by <s>Puruṣa</s> through the eye of knowledge, and the man is likewise seen [by <s>Prakṛti</s>]. [SkMv 65]

children.text: atrāha --- jñānacakṣuṣā dṛṣṭvā prakṛtiṃ puruṣaḥ kiṃ karoti? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks: having seen <s>Prakṛti</s> through the eye of knowledge, what does <s>Puruṣa</s> do? To this it is said:

children.text: dṛṣṭā mayety upekṣaka eko dṛṣṭāham ity uparatānyā /
children.translated_text: '"I have seen her" — thus the one becomes indifferent; "I have been seen" — thus the other ceases;

children.text: sati saṃyoge 'pi tayoḥ prayojanaṃ nāsti sargasya // ISk_66 //
children.translated_text: Even though the conjunction of the two still exists, there is no purpose for [further] creation.' [ISk 66]

children.text: yathemāṃ raṅgagatāṃ nartakīṃ sarvāsv avasthāsu vartamānāṃ dṛṣṭvā viramati raṅgāt prekṣakaḥ dṛṣṭā mayety upekṣaka ekaḥ kevalaḥ śuddhaḥ puruṣaḥ | tathā prakṛtir api --- "anenāhaṃ dṛṣṭā" iti nivṛttā | ekā trailokyasyāpi pradhānakāraṇabhūtā na dvitīyā prakṛtir asti | nartaky api --- "aham anena dṛṣṭā" ity uparamate nṛtyāt, evaṃ puruṣo 'pi "dṛṣṭā mayeyaṃ jñānacakṣuṣā prakṛtiḥ" iti prekṣakavad uparamate mokṣaṃ gacchatīty arthaḥ | tathā prakṛtir api dṛṣṭāham aneneti svavyāpārād uparamaty eva | atrāha --- puṃprakṛtyoḥ sarvagatatvāt sarvaniṣedho na śakyate vaktum | tad asya saṃsārasargasya vinivṛttir eva | tat katham idaṃ sādhanaṃ samīcīnam iti | atrocyate --- sati saṃyoge 'pi tayoḥ prayojanaṃ nāsti sargasyeti | yady api pradhānapuruṣayoḥ sarvagatayoḥ saṃyogo bhavaty eva | tasmiṃś ca sati sargasambhavas tathāpi nāsau sargaḥ syāt prayojanābhāvāt | yasmāt pradhānasya puruṣārthā pravṛttiḥ | sa ca puruṣārtho dvividhaḥ | śabdādyupalabdhir ādir guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhir antaś ca | brahmādisthāvarānteṣu puruṣaḥ śabdādibhir viṣayair yojayitavyaḥ | ante ca guṇapuruṣāntaropalabdhyā mokṣayitavyaḥ | evaṃ puruṣadarśanārthaṃ samprayogaḥ kṛtaḥ | evaṃ prakṛtipuruṣayos tayoḥ śarīrotpattir nāsti punaḥ ṛṇikadhāriṇakavad yatheha loke ṛṇikadhāriṇakau uttamādhamarṇau devadattayajñadattau yo 'smin ṛṇaṃ dhārayati sa uttamarṇas tenādhamarṇāktaḥ --- "ṛṇaṃ me dehī" iti | tatas tena taddattam | tatas tau kṛtaprayojanau parasparam arthena santyaktāv atha tayor bhūyaḥ saṃyogo bhavati | tathāpi nārthakṛtyaṃ prayojanābhāvāt | yathā vā vṛddhasaṃyogād apatyaṃ na bhavati, prayojanābhāvāt | tathā pradhānapuruṣayoḥ kṛtaprayojanayoḥ prayojanaṃ nāstīti siddham // SkMv_66 //
children.translated_text: Just as a spectator, having seen this dancer on stage going through all her states, withdraws from the stage [thinking] 'She has been seen by me' — equanimous, alone, pure — such is <s>Puruṣa</s>. So too <s>Prakṛti</s>: 'I have been seen by him' — she desists. She is one, the primordial cause of all three worlds; there is no second <s>Prakṛti</s>. The dancer too — [thinking] 'I have been seen by him' — ceases from dancing. In the same way, <s>Puruṣa</s> too — [thinking] 'This <s>Prakṛti</s> has been seen by me through the eye of knowledge' — desists like a spectator and goes to liberation — this is the meaning. And <s>Prakṛti</s> too, [thinking] 'I have been seen by him,' ceases from her own activity. Here one objects: Since both <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s> are all-pervading, a complete denial [of their contact] cannot be made. Then this cessation of the creation of <s>saṃsāra</s> [would be impossible] — how then is this means valid? To this it is answered: Even though there is conjunction of those two, there is no purpose for creation. Even though the conjunction of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, who are all-pervading, does indeed occur, and even though creation would be possible when that [conjunction] exists, nevertheless that creation would not occur because of the absence of purpose. For the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> is for the sake of <s>Puruṣa</s>. And that purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is twofold: the experience of sound and other [sense-objects] is the beginning; the discrimination between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is the end. Among beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the stationary, <s>Puruṣa</s> is to be conjoined with objects of sound and the like. And at the end, he is to be liberated through the discrimination between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. Thus the conjunction was made for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s seeing. In this way, there is no further birth of a body for those two — <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — like a debtor and creditor. Just as in this world, a debtor and creditor — <s>Devadatta</s> the superior creditor and <s>Yajñadatta</s> the inferior debtor — the one who holds the debt says to the other: 'Give me my debt.' Then he gives it. Then, their purpose fulfilled, the two are released from mutual obligation. Even if their conjunction occurs again, there is no [new] transaction, due to the absence of purpose. Or just as from the conjunction of the aged, offspring is not born, due to the absence of purpose. In the same way, for <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> whose purpose has been fulfilled, there is no [further] purpose — this is established. // <s>SkMv</s> 66 //

children.text: kiñ cānyat, yadi puruṣasyotpanne jñāne mokṣas tarhi mama kasmān na bhavati | ata ucyate ---
children.translated_text: Furthermore, if <s>Puruṣa</s> attains liberation when knowledge arises, then why does it not happen for me? Therefore it is said:

children.text: samyagjñānādhigamād dharmādīnām akāraṇaprāptau /
children.translated_text: Through the attainment of right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>), when <s>dharma</s> and the rest become non-causal,

children.text: tiṣṭhati saṃskāravaśāc cakrabhramavad dhṛtaśarīraḥ // ISk_67 //
children.translated_text: [The knower] remains, bearing the body through the force of latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), like the continued spinning of a [potter's] wheel. // <s>ISk</s> 67 //

children.text: yadā puruṣeṇa pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānam adhigataṃ bhavati tadā dharmādīny akāraṇāni prāptāni punarjanmasamarthāni na bhavanti | ko dṛṣṭāntaḥ --- yatheha (p.89) loke bījāny agnidagdhāni na prarohasamarthāni bhavanti | dharmo yeṣām ādis tāni dharmādīni teṣām akāraṇānāṃ prāptir akāraṇaprāptiḥ | tathā satyāṃ punarjanma na bhavati | atrāha --- yadi samyagjñānān mokṣo bhavati tatrācāryasyopadeṣṭuḥ samyagjñānam utpannaṃ kimarthaṃ mokṣaṃ na gato 'sti, atha vā tvatprasādāt tajjñānaṃ mamāpi sañjātaṃ kim ahaṃ mokṣaṃ na gacchāmi | atrocyate --- tiṣṭhati saṃskāravaśāt | saṃskāro nāma dharmādharmau nimittaṃ kṛtvā śarīrotpattir bhavati tiryaṅmanuṣyadevādiṣu | tasya saṃskāreṇa grahaṇam | sa ca saṃskāraḥ phalam adattvā kṣayaṃ na gacchati, utpannajñānasyāpi tasmād idaṃ śarīraṃ vināśaṃ yāsyati | tannimittābhāvād idaṃ śarīraṃ patiṣyati | yathā ca vidvān mokṣaṃ yāsyati | tasmāt hetor utpannajñānasyāpi dharmādharmavaśāt tiṣṭhati śarīram | ko dṛṣṭāntaḥ? atrocyate --- cakrabhramavad dhṛtaśarīraḥ | yathā kulālaś cakraṃ bhramayati ghaṭaṃ kariṣyāmīti | sa kulālo ghaṭaṃ kṛtvā yathā svastho bhavati, avatiṣṭhate | yasmiṃś cāvatiṣṭhamāne cakraṃ bhramaty eva | saṃskāravaśāt --- karmavaśād ity arthaḥ | evam eva pūrvakṛtayor dharmādharmayor balavattvād durbalatvāj jñānasya, utpanne 'pi jñāne vidvāṃs tiṣṭhati saṃskāravaśāc cakrabhramavad dhṛtaśarīraḥ // SkMv_67 //
children.translated_text: When the knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> has been attained by <s>Puruṣa</s>, then <s>dharma</s> and the rest, having become non-causal, are no longer capable of [producing] rebirth. What is the illustration? Just as in this world, seeds burned by fire are no longer capable of sprouting. <s>Dharma</s> and the rest — those of which <s>dharma</s> is the first — their attainment of non-causality is the 'attainment of non-causality.' When that is the case, rebirth does not occur. Here one objects: If liberation comes from right knowledge, then the teacher who instructs has attained right knowledge — why has he not gone to liberation? Or, by your grace, that knowledge has arisen in me too — why do I not go to liberation? To this it is answered: [he] remains through the force of latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>). <s>Saṃskāra</s> is the name for the birth of a body in animal, human, divine, and other [realms], caused by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. The word refers to that latent impression. And that latent impression does not perish without giving its fruit. Therefore, even for one in whom knowledge has arisen, this body will [eventually] be destroyed. Due to the absence of its cause, this body will fall. And thus the wise one will go to liberation. Therefore, even for one in whom knowledge has arisen, the body remains through the force of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. What is the illustration? To this it is answered: like the continued spinning of a wheel, bearing the body. Just as a potter spins the wheel [thinking] 'I shall make a pot.' That potter, having made the pot, becomes at ease, rests. But while he rests, the wheel continues to spin — through the force of latent impressions, meaning through the force of [previous] action. In the same way, because of the strength of the previously performed <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, and because of the weakness of knowledge, even when knowledge has arisen, the wise one remains bearing the body through the force of latent impressions, like the continued spinning of a wheel. // <s>SkMv</s> 67 //

children.text: atrāha --- utpannajñānaḥ phalanirapekṣaṃ karma nirbījaṃ kurvan na deham ārabhate, ārabdhaphalaṃ yāvat janmadāyi "nābhuktaṃ kṣīyate karma" "avaśyam eva bhoktavyaṃ kṛtam" iti kṣapayan, anārabdhaphaleṣu "yathaidhāṃsi samiddho 'gniḥ(bhagavadgītā 4 |37)" iti parihāreṇa bhasmīkaraṇam | evaṃ karmaṇāṃ dhvaṃse, utpanne jñāne 'pi kadā vidvān mokṣaṃ gacchatīti? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one objects: The one in whom knowledge has arisen, performing action without regard for results, making it seedless, does not initiate a [new] body. [For] action whose fruit has begun [to ripen], which produces [this] birth — 'Action that has not been experienced does not perish'; 'What has been done must necessarily be experienced' — [the knower] exhausts [this]. As for actions whose fruits have not yet begun to ripen — 'Just as a blazing fire [burns] fuel' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 4.37) — [the knower] reduces them to ashes by this remedy. Thus, when actions are destroyed, even after knowledge has arisen, when does the wise one go to liberation? To this it is answered:

children.text: prāpte śarīrabhede caritārthatvāt pradhānavinivṛttau /
children.translated_text: When the separation of the body is reached, and <s>Pradhāna</s> ceases because its purpose has been fulfilled,

children.text: aikāntikam ātyantikam ubhayaṃ kaivalyam āpnoti // ISk_68 //
children.translated_text: [The wise one] attains absolute and final — both [kinds of] — isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>). // <s>ISk</s> 68 //

children.text: tad evaṃ sati śarīrabhede dehanāśe prāpta āyāta ity arthaḥ | caritārthatvāt | sa cārtho dvividhaḥ (śābdātmikaḥ) pūrvam uktaḥ | tasyārthasya caritārthatvāt kṛtvety arthaḥ | pradhānavinivṛttau | yadā pūrvakṛtayor dharmādharmayoḥ kṣayo bhavati tadā śarīraṃ bhidyate | tasmiṃś ca śarīre bhinne pūrvoktena jñānena śarīraṃ pradhānākhyaṃ kāraṇam aviśeṣamayaṃ tānmātrikaṃ sargādāv utpannaṃ tan nivartate | iha śarīre yat pārthivaṃ tat prthivīṃ praviśati | evam anyad anyeṣu praviśati | evaṃ sthūlaṃ śarīraṃ pañcadhā bhidyate | pradhānaṃ ca kṛtaprayojanaṃ bhūyo 'nyat(p.60) śarīraṃ dvitīyaṃ nārabhate viduṣaḥ | evam ayaṃ vidvān tasmin śarīre bhinne --- aikāntikam ātyantikam ubhayaṃ kaivalyam āpnoti | aikāntikam avaśyambhāvitvād ātyantikam apunarāvṛttitvāt sarvathety arthaḥ | na tv auṣadhādivat kādācitkaroganivṛttivat | na ca nivṛtte roge punaḥ sambhaved ity ubhayodāharaṇam aikāntikātyantikayoḥ | ittham ekāntātyantas tāpatrayasyābhāvād uparamād anutpatteḥ kaivalyaṃ mokṣa ity arthaḥ | tam āpnoti // SkMv_68 //
children.translated_text: Thus, when the separation — the destruction — of the body has been reached and arrived at — this is the meaning. Because its purpose has been fulfilled: that purpose is twofold, as previously stated. Because that purpose has been fulfilled — meaning 'because it has been accomplished.' When <s>Pradhāna</s> ceases: when the previously performed <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are exhausted, then the body breaks apart. And when that body breaks apart, through the previously described knowledge, the body called <s>Pradhāna</s> — the causal [body] made of the non-specific [elements], the <s>tānmātrika</s> [body] originated at the beginning of creation — that ceases. In this body, what is earthy enters the earth; similarly, what belongs to each [element] enters into its [respective element]. Thus the gross body breaks apart fivefold. And <s>Pradhāna</s>, its purpose fulfilled, does not initiate another, second body for the wise one. Thus this wise one, when that body breaks apart — attains absolute and final, both [kinds of] isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>). 'Absolute' (<s>aikāntika</s>) because it is inevitable; 'final' (<s>ātyantika</s>) because there is no return — meaning 'in every way.' It is not like the occasional cessation of disease through medicine and the like. Nor could the disease, once removed, recur — this is the twofold illustration of the 'absolute' and 'final.' Thus, due to the absence and cessation and non-arising of the threefold suffering — that is <s>kaivalya</s>, meaning <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). That [the wise one] attains. // <s>SkMv</s> 68 //

children.text: atrāha --- kiṃprayojanam idaṃ jñānam ucyate | atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks: For what purpose is this knowledge taught? To this it is answered:

children.text: puruṣārthajñānam idaṃ guhyaṃ paramarṣiṇā samākhyātam /
children.translated_text: This knowledge for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> [i.e., liberation] — secret — was expounded by the supreme sage (<s>paramarṣi</s>);

children.text: sthityutpattipralayāś cintyante yatra bhūtānām // ISk_69 //
children.translated_text: Wherein the arising, continuance, and dissolution of beings are contemplated. // <s>ISk</s> 69 //

children.text: yaś cāsau puruṣārtho mokṣas tadarthaṃ puruṣavimokṣārthaṃ jñānam idam iti | yad etat pūrvavarṇitaṃ jñānaṃ etad guhyaṃ durvijñeyam ity arthaḥ | paramarṣiṇā kapilena samākhyātaṃ kathitam ity arthaḥ | atrāha --- asmin jñāne ke 'rthāś cintyante | atrocyate --- sthityutpattipralayāḥ tatra devādīnām aṣṭau sthānāni bhavanti | mānuṣyaṃ caikavidham, bhūloke pañcavidhaṃ tairyagyonam | eṣu sthāneṣu brahmādīni tiryagyoniparyantāni tiṣṭhanti | eṣā sthitiḥ | utpattiṃ prādurbhāvaṃ pradhānān mahadahaṅkāratanmātrendriyamahābhūtānīty utpattiḥ | evaṃ bhūtotpattir bhāvotpattiś ca vyākhyātā | layaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ --- bhūtāni tanmātreṣu līyante, tānīndriyeṣu, indriyāṇi līyante cāhaṅkāre, sa buddhau, sā pradhāne layaṃ gacchati | pradhānaṃ tu kvacin na līyate 'vikṛtatvāt | evaṃ pralayaḥ // SkMv_69 //
children.translated_text: That purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> which is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) — for that purpose, for the liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s>, is this knowledge. This knowledge, as previously described, is secret (<s>guhya</s>) — meaning difficult to comprehend. It was expounded, meaning taught, by the supreme sage <s>Kapila</s>. Here one asks: What subjects are contemplated in this knowledge? To this it is answered: the arising, continuance, and dissolution [of beings]. There, for the gods and the like, there are eight stations. Humanity is of one kind. In the earthly realm, animal birth is fivefold. In these stations, beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the animal-born abide — this is continuance. Arising means manifestation — from <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Mahat</s>, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, <s>Tanmātras</s>, sense-organs, and gross elements arise — this is arising. Thus the arising of beings and of dispositions has been explained. Now we shall explain dissolution: the gross elements dissolve into the <s>tanmātras</s>; those into the sense-organs; the sense-organs dissolve into <s>ahaṅkāra</s>; that into <s>buddhi</s>; that goes to dissolution in <s>Pradhāna</s>. But <s>Pradhāna</s> does not dissolve anywhere, because it is unmodified. Thus is dissolution. // <s>SkMv</s> 69 //

children.text: atrāha --- yad etad bhagavatā vyākhyātaṃ pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānam, tasya kuta āgama iti? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here one asks: This knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> that has been expounded by the Blessed One — what is its source (<s>āgama</s>)? To this it is answered:

children.text: etat pavitryam agryaṃ munir āsuraye 'nukampayā pradadau /
children.translated_text: This most sacred and supreme [teaching], the sage (<s>Muni</s>) gave to <s>Āsuri</s> out of compassion;

children.text: āsurir api pañcaśikhāya tena ca bahulīkṛtaṃ tantram // ISk_70 //
children.translated_text: <s>Āsuri</s> [gave it] also to <s>Pañcaśikha</s>; and by him the <s>tantra</s> (doctrine) was widely propagated. // <s>ISk</s> 70 //

children.text: etat vijñānam adhikurute | etat pavitraṃ, kathaṃ pavitram? | yasmān narakapretatiryagyoniṣu patanāt trāyate tasmāt pavitram | agryaṃ śraiṣṭhyāt | vedapurāṇabhāratam anvādibhyo 'pi dharmaśāstrebhya etat pañcaviṃśatitattvajñānam uttamam | kasmāt? aikāntikatvāt, ātyantikatvāc ca | ato duḥkhābhāvaś ca | munir bhagavān kapilaḥ āsurisagotrāya brāhmaṇāya varṣasahasrayājine 'dhikāritām avagamya (asmai) pradadau | tadanukampayā tadvimokṣārtham | andhe tamasy ajñāne 'yaṃ tapasvī vartata ity utpannayānukampayā | munir mananāt | bhagavān bhūtānāṃ gatim āgatiṃ ca vidann anati calatīti bhagavān kapilaḥ | pratyupakārānapekṣasarvopakārī suhṛd ity artham avalambyovāca | tad eva jñānaṃ bhūya āsurisagotro 'nukampayā pañcaśikhāya provāca | pañcaśikhena tena bahudhākṛtaṃ tantram | bahūnāṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ pradattam // SkMv_70 //
children.translated_text: This knowledge is supreme. This is sacred — how is it sacred? Because it saves one from falling into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animal births, therefore it is sacred. It is foremost, due to its excellence. Compared to the <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>Mahābhārata</s>, and other <s>dharmaśāstras</s> beginning with <s>Manu</s>, this knowledge of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> is supreme. Why? Because of its absolute certainty and its absolute finality. And therefore there is the absence of suffering. The sage, the Blessed <s>Kapila</s>, having recognized the qualification of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Āsuri</s> lineage who had performed sacrifices for a thousand years, bestowed [this knowledge] upon him — out of compassion for him, for the purpose of his liberation. [Seeing that] 'this ascetic dwells in blind darkness of ignorance,' compassion arose [in him]. He is called 'sage' (<s>muni</s>) because of contemplation (<s>manana</s>). 'Blessed One' (<s>Bhagavān</s>) — knowing the going and coming of beings, he moves forth — thus he is <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kapila</s>. 'Friend' (<s>suhṛd</s>) means one who benefits all without expectation of return — relying on this meaning, he spoke. That same knowledge, <s>Āsuri</s>'s descendant out of compassion imparted to <s>Pañcaśikha</s>. By that <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, the <s>tantra</s> (systematic treatise) was elaborated in many ways and given to many disciples. // <s>SkMv</s> 70 //

children.text: tantram iti vyākhyāyate | "tama eva khalv idam agra āsīt"(maitryupaniṣad 5 |2) | tasmiṃs tamasi kṣetrajño 'bhivartate prathamam | tama iti ucyate prakṛtiḥ, puruṣaḥ kṣetrajñaḥ | ṣaṣṭipadārthā yasmin śāstre tantryante tat ṣaṣṭitantram | ṣaṣṭitantraṃ jñātvā kuśalaḥ kileśvarakṛṣṇanāmā | tena īśvarakṛṣṇena vistaragranthagrahaṇabhīruṇā hitārthaṃ ṣaṣṭitantram atisaṅkṣiptam | tad āha ---
children.translated_text: The word '<s>tantra</s>' is now explained. 'Indeed, in the beginning this was <s>tamas</s> (darkness) alone' (<s>Maitrī Upaniṣad</s> 5.2). In that darkness, the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) manifests first. '<s>Tamas</s>' refers to <s>Prakṛti</s>; '<s>Puruṣa</s>' is the <s>kṣetrajña</s>. The treatise in which sixty topics are systematically expounded — that is the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> (Sixty-Topic Treatise). Having mastered the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>, the skilled one named <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s> — by that <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, who was averse to grasping lengthy texts, the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> was extremely condensed for the benefit [of students]. He states this —

children.text: śiṣyaparamparayāgatam īśvarakṛṣṇena caitad āryābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: This [knowledge], which has come down through a succession of disciples, by <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s> in <s>āryā</s> verses,

children.text: saṅkṣiptam āryamatinā samyag vijñāya siddhāntam // ISk_71 //
children.translated_text: Has been condensed by one of noble intellect, having properly understood the established doctrine. // <s>ISk</s> 71 //

children.text: śiṣyaparamparayāgatam iti | kapilād āsuriṇā prāptam idaṃ jñānam | tataḥ pañcaśikhena, tasmād bhārgavolūkavālmīkihārītadevalaprabhṛtīn āgatam | tatas tebhya īśvarakṛṣṇena prāptam | tad eva ṣaṣṭitantram āryābhiḥ saṅkṣiptam āryamatinā vistīrṇamatinā samyag vijñāya siddhāntam kāryakāraṇasiddhasya śarīrasyānto 'punarbhāvo mokṣas tasya tādātmyam ity arthaḥ | tatisiddhasya śarīrasya sūkṣmasya tānmātrikasya sargādibhavasyānto mūrtināśa iti vā | eṣa ṣaṣṭitantra iti tātparyam // SkMv_71 //
children.translated_text: 'Through a succession of disciples' — this knowledge was obtained from <s>Kapila</s> by <s>Āsuri</s>. Then by <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, and from him it came to <s>Bhārgava</s>, <s>Ulūka</s>, <s>Vālmīki</s>, <s>Hārīta</s>, <s>Devala</s>, and others. From them it was obtained by <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>. That same <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> was condensed in <s>āryā</s> verses by one of noble intellect (<s>āryamati</s>), that is, one of expansive understanding, having properly comprehended the established doctrine — the meaning being: the end of the body established through cause and effect, i.e., non-return (<s>apunarbhāva</s>) which is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), its identity [with knowledge]. Or alternatively: the end of the subtle body composed of <s>tanmātras</s>, existing from the beginning of creation, is the destruction of the form — this is the purport of the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>. // <s>SkMv</s> 71 //

children.text: saptatyāṃ kila yo 'rthās te 'rthāḥ kṛtsnasya ṣaṣṭitantrasya /
children.translated_text: The topics that are in the Seventy [verses] — those are the topics of the entire <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>,

children.text: ākhyāyikāvirahitāḥ paravādavivarjitāś ceti // ISk_72 //
children.translated_text: Devoid of illustrative stories and free from polemics against rival doctrines. // <s>ISk</s> 72 //

children.text: ye ṣaṣṭitantre padārthā abhihitās te saptatyāṃ vyākhyātāḥ kathitāḥ | ṣaṣṭitbhedāḥ prāg vyākhyātāḥ | "bhedas tamaso 'ṣṭavidha" iti āryāyāṃ "pañca viparyayabhedā" ity atra cābhihitā ity ete pañcāśat pratyayāḥ ime cānye daśa maulikāḥ | tathā hi ---
children.translated_text: The topics that were expounded in the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> — those have been explained and stated in the Seventy [verses]. The sixty divisions were explained earlier. In the <s>āryā</s> verse 'The division of <s>tamas</s> is eightfold' and in 'The five divisions of error' — therein are stated these fifty <s>pratyayas</s> (categories), and these other ten are fundamental. Namely —

children.text: astitvam ekatvam athārthavattvaṃ pārārthyam anyatvam atho nivṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Existence, oneness, and purposefulness, other-directedness, difference, and cessation,

children.text: yogo viyogo bahavaḥ pumāṃsaḥ sthitiḥ śarīrasya ca śeṣavṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> (conjunction), <s>viyoga</s> (disjunction), the multiplicity of <s>Puruṣas</s>, the persistence of the body, and residual activity.

children.text: tatra "bhedānāṃ parimāṇāt" ity etaiḥ pañcabhir hetubhiḥ pradhānāstitvam ekatvam arthavattvaṃ ca siddham | "saṅghātaparārthatvāt" iti parārthatvam uktam | "janmamaraṇakaraṇānām" iti puruṣabahutvaṃ siddham | "cakrabhramavad dhṛtaśarīra" iti sthitiḥ siddhā, ete daśa, "pañca viparyayāḥ" aṣṭāviṃśatidhā aśaktiḥ, navadhā tuṣṭiḥ aṣṭadhā siddhir iti pañcāśat | ubhayaṃ militvā ṣaṣṭipadārthāḥ ṣaṣṭitantre | tantryante vyutpādyante padārthā iti tantram | ṣaṣṭipadārthānāṃ tantram iti saṅgatiḥ | ākhyāyikāvirahitāḥ paravādavivarjitāś ceti | pareṇa saha vādaḥ paravādaḥ tena varjitāś ca | iti parisamāptam iti // SkMv_72 //
children.translated_text: There, by the five reasons [beginning with] 'from the finitude of divisions,' the existence, oneness, and purposefulness of <s>Pradhāna</s> are established. By 'because of the purpose of aggregation for another,' its other-directedness is stated. By 'because of birth, death, and the instruments,' the multiplicity of <s>Puruṣas</s> is established. By 'like the turning of a wheel, the sustained body,' persistence is established — these are ten. 'Five errors,' twenty-eight-fold incapacity, nine-fold contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>), eight-fold attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) — [these are] fifty. Both together make sixty topics in the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>. A <s>tantra</s> is [so called because] topics are systematically expounded (<s>tantryante</s>) in it. The <s>tantra</s> of sixty topics — this is the connection. 'Devoid of illustrative stories and free from polemics against rival doctrines' — debate with an opponent is <s>paravāda</s>; free from that as well. Thus it is concluded. // <s>SkMv</s> 72 //

children.text: atrāha --- katham etad alpagranthaṃ śāstraṃ kṛtsnasya vācakaṃ bhaviṣyati? atrocyate ---
children.translated_text: Here an objection is raised: how can this small treatise be expressive of the entire [doctrine]? To this it is replied —

children.text: tasmāt samāsadṛṣṭaṃ śāstram idaṃ nārthataś ca parihīnam /
children.translated_text: Therefore this treatise is seen in condensed form, yet it is not deficient in content;

children.text: tantrasya ca bṛhanmūrter darpaṇasaṅkrāntam iva bimbam // ISk_73 //
children.translated_text: Like an image reflected in a mirror of the vast body of the <s>tantra</s>. // <s>ISk</s> 73 //

children.text: yasmāt ṣaṣṭitantram iti hetuḥ | samāsadṛṣṭaṃ saṅkṣepato grantham ity arthaḥ | śāstram iti | śāsyate yenotpathād iti śāstram | tīrthodakamahatphalam | kartā bhoktā bhojyaṃ mokṣaś cātra cintyate | atha duḥkhānāṃ śāsanāt śāstram | idam --- imāṃ saptatiṃ darśayati | nārthataś ca parihīnam | ṣaṣṭipadārthavicāraṇāyām(p.63) ahīnam ity arthaḥ | tantrasyeti | yathā svalpe 'pi darpaṇe mahato rūpasya nirūpaṇaṃ syāt | evam alpaśāstre ṣaṣṭitantrasya kṛtsnasyāpi vyaktir abhihitety arthaḥ // SkMv_73 //
children.translated_text: 'Because it is the <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s>' — this is the reason. 'Seen in condensed form' means the text is in abbreviated form. '<s>Śāstra</s>' (treatise) — that by which one is governed from the wrong path is a <s>śāstra</s>. The fruit of sacred waters is great. The agent, the experiencer, the object of experience, and liberation — these are contemplated herein. Or: because it disciplines (<s>śāsana</s>) sufferings, it is a <s>śāstra</s>. 'This' — he indicates this Seventy [verses]. 'Yet not deficient in content' — (p.63) meaning not lacking in the examination of the sixty topics. 'Of the <s>tantra</s>' — just as in even a small mirror there can be the perception of a large form, so too in a small treatise the manifestation of the entire <s>Ṣaṣṭitantra</s> is expressed — this is the meaning. // <s>SkMv</s> 73 //

children.text:
ity ācāryeśvarakṛṣṇaproktāyāḥ sāṅkhyasaptatyā vṛttir ācāryamāṭharakṛtiḥ samāptā |
(p.64)
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>vṛtti</s> (commentary) on the <s>Sāṅkhyasaptati</s> (Sāṃkhya Seventy) composed by <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, authored by <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Māṭhara</s>, is completed. (p.64)
